sanskrit: जन्म कर्म च मे दिव्यमेवं यो वेत्ति तत्त्वतः | त्यक्त्वा देहं पुनर्जन्म नैति मामेति सोऽर्जुन
english: He who thus know, in their true light, My divine birth and action, having abandoned the body, is not born again, he comes to Me, O Arjuna.
brief_explanation: The Lord, though appearing to be born, is beyond birth and death. He is ever beyond all actions, establishing righteousness firmly. One who knows this never gets reborn.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: वीतरागभयक्रोधा मन्मया मामुपाश्रिताः | बहवो ज्ञानतपसा पूता मद्भावमागताः
english: Freed from attachment, fear and anger, absorbed in Me, taking refuge in Me, purified by the fire of knowledge, many have attained to My Being.
brief_explanation: When one gains self-knowledge, attachment to sense objects ceases. Realizing the constant, indestructible, and eternal Self, fearlessness arises. Becoming desireless, free from selfishness, and perceiving the Self everywhere prevents anger.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: ये यथा मां प्रपद्यन्ते तांस्तथैव भजाम्यहम् | मम वर्त्मानुवर्तन्ते मनुष्याः पार्थ सर्वशः
english: In whatever way men approach Me even so do I reward them; My path do men tread in all ways, O Arjuna.
brief_explanation: The text describes that individuals are rewarded according to their approach towards the selfless worship of Me (God). If they seek Me for selfish reasons, I grant them desired objects. However, if they unselfishly seek Me for Self-knowledge, I grant them liberation.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: काङ्क्षन्तः कर्मणां सिद्धिं यजन्त इह देवताः | क्षिप्रं हि मानुषे लोके सिद्धिर्भवति कर्मजा
english: Those who long for success in action in this world sacrifice to the gods; because success is ickly attained by men through action.
brief_explanation: Aspirants who long for success in actions (fruits of work) through sacrifice in this world, attain it quickly due to their human birth, but not Self-realization which demands perfect renunciation, the four means, and intense meditation.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: चातुर्वर्ण्यं मया सृष्टं गुणकर्मविभागशः | तस्य कर्तारमपि मां विद्ध्यकर्तारमव्ययम्
english: The fourfold caste has been created by Me according to the differentiation of Guna and Karma; though I am the author thereof know Me as non-doer and immutable.
brief_explanation: The four castes (Brahmana, Kshatriya, Vaishya, Sudra) are classified based on the differentiation of Guna and Karma, with each caste reflecting a predominance of Sattva, Rajas, or Tamas. While the Lord is the creator, He is considered immutable and not the active doer in the creation of the caste system. Society thrives when each caste performs their respective duties properly, preventing chaos and discord.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: न मां कर्माणि लिम्पन्ति न मे कर्मफले स्पृहा | इति मां योऽभिजानाति कर्मभिर्न स बध्यते
english: Actions do not taint Me, nor have I a desire for the fruit of actions. He who knows Me thus is not bound by actions.
brief_explanation: The verse suggests that those who do not have ego or desire for the fruit of their actions are not bound by them, implying freedom from repeated births and deaths. This contrasts with worldly individuals who identify as agents of action and seek rewards, perpetuating the cycle of rebirth.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: एवं ज्ञात्वा कृतं कर्म पूर्वैरपि मुमुक्षुभिः | कुरु कर्मैव तस्मात्त्वं पूर्वैः पूर्वतरं कृतम्
english: Having known this, the ancient seekers after freedom also performed action; therefore do thou also perform action, as did the ancients in days of yore.
brief_explanation: The passage suggests that one should perform their duty, having understood that the Self is untouched by actions and their fruits, and that egoism should be avoided. Ancients such as Janaka performed actions, thus you too should act, whether for purifying an impure heart or for the wellbeing of the world if self-realization has been attained.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: किं कर्म किमकर्मेति कवयोऽप्यत्र मोहिताः | तत्ते कर्म प्रवक्ष्यामि यज्ज्ञात्वा मोक्ष्यसेऽशुभात्
english: What is action? What is inaction? As to this even the wise are confused. Therefore I shall teach thee such action (the nature of action and inaction) by knowing which thou shalt be liberated from the evil (of Samsara, the wheel of birth and death).
brief_explanation: In the Bhagavad Gita, verse 4.16 discusses action and inaction. It states that wise individuals, who may appear deluded, will be taught about action, which when known can lead to liberation from evil.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: कर्मणो ह्यपि बोद्धव्यं बोद्धव्यं च विकर्मणः | अकर्मणश्च बोद्धव्यं गहना कर्मणो गतिः
english: For verily (the true nature) of action (enjoined by the scriptures) should be known, also (that) of forbidden (or unlawful) action, and of inaction; hard to understand is the nature (path) of action.
brief_explanation: The commentary does not provide explicit explanations for this verse, but here's an interpretation based on the context: Karmanah (action) should be known for its purpose and api (also) its consequences. The forbidden action (vikarmana), inaction (akarmana), deep (hidden or secret) aspects of karma, and their paths (gatih) should also be understood.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: कर्मण्यकर्म यः पश्येदकर्मणि च कर्म यः | स बुद्धिमान्मनुष्येषु स युक्तः कृत्स्नकर्मकृत्
english: He who seeth inaction in action and action in inaction, he is wise among men; he is a Yogi and performer of all actions.
brief_explanation: The verse describes "inaction in action" and "action in inaction." Inaction in action occurs when one perceives themselves as a silent witness or spectator of Nature's activities, feeling that they are not the doer. This removes the binding nature of actions. Action in inaction happens when one has the idea of agency or doership even while being idle.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: यस्य सर्वे समारम्भाः कामसङ्कल्पवर्जिताः | ज्ञानाग्निदग्धकर्माणं तमाहुः पण्डितं बुधाः
english: He whose undertakings are all devoid of desires and (selfish) purposes and whose actions have been burnt by the fire of knowledge, him the wise call a sage.
brief_explanation: A sage, whose undertakings are devoid of desires and purposes, whose actions have been burnt by the fire of knowledge, is called a wise or learned individual. This person performs actions only to set an example for others as they have no selfish interests. The fire of wisdom, or BrahmaJnana, consumes all results of actions, making the enlightened sage free from the bonds of action.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: त्यक्त्वा कर्मफलासङ्गं नित्यतृप्तो निराश्रयः | कर्मण्यभिप्रवृत्तोऽपि नैव किञ्चित्करोति सः
english: Having abandoned attachment to the fruits of the action, ever content, depending on nothing, he does not do anything though engaged in activity.
brief_explanation: The passage emphasizes the concept of 'inaction in action.' One who performs actions without egoism and attachment to results, works for the world's wellbeing, and identifies with the Self beyond activity, effectively does nothing despite being constantly engaged. This is because such a person, identified with Brahman (the Absolute), is self-contained and experiences fulfillment of all desires. They are ever satisfied and do not depend on anything else, similar to a person favored by a king not needing assistance from officials.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: निराशीर्यतचित्तात्मा त्यक्तसर्वपरिग्रहः | शारीरं केवलं कर्म कुर्वन्नाप्नोति किल्बिषम्
english: Without hope and with the mind and the self controlled, having abandoned all covetousness, doing mere bodily action, he incurs no sin.
brief_explanation: The liberated sage renounces all but necessary actions for bodily maintenance, abandoning possessions and incurring no sin. For the seeker of liberation, even righteous acts can be a bondage to Samsara as they are golden fetters, binding him to both good and evil. (Cf.III.7)

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: यदृच्छालाभसन्तुष्टो द्वन्द्वातीतो विमत्सरः | समः सिद्धावसिद्धौ च कृत्वापि न निबध्यते
english: Content with what comes to him without effort, free from the pairs of opposites and envy, even-minded in success and failure, though acting, he is not bound.
brief_explanation: The sage is content with chance occurrences, unaffected by dualities, free from envy, and even-minded. In success or failure, they act but feel no bind as their actions are consumed by self-knowledge, like a burned seed cannot germinate. From an external perspective, they appear to act, but in truth, they do nothing; nature performs everything.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: गतसङ्गस्य मुक्तस्य ज्ञानावस्थितचेतसः | यज्ञायाचरतः कर्म समग्रं प्रविलीयते
english: To one who is devoid of attchment, who is liberated, whose mind is established in knowledge, who works for the sake of sacrifice (for the sake of God), the whole action is dissolved.
brief_explanation: The liberated individual, whose mind is established in knowledge and free from attachment, performs actions for the sake of sacrifice. Their actions, along with their results, dissolve and effectively cease to exist.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: ब्रह्मार्पणं ब्रह्म हविर्ब्रह्माग्नौ ब्रह्मणा हुतम् | ब्रह्मैव तेन गन्तव्यं ब्रह्मकर्मसमाधिना
english: Brahman is the oblation; Brahman is the melted butter (ghee); by Brahman is the oblation poured into the fire of Brahman; Brahman verily shall be reached by him who always sees Brahman in action.
brief_explanation: The verse describes JnanaYajna, a wisdom sacrifice where the performer, instrument, and goal are all considered as Brahman. When one achieves Self-realization, their whole life becomes a sacrifice offering only Brahman. A sage who knows the Self recognizes that all elements of action (oblation, fire, instrument) have no existence apart from Brahman, even if they appear to perform actions.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: दैवमेवापरे यज्ञं योगिनः पर्युपासते | ब्रह्माग्नावपरे यज्ञं यज्ञेनैवोपजुह्वति
english: Some Yogies perform sacrifice to the gods alone; while others (who have realised the Self) offer the self as sacrifice by the Self in the fire of Brahman alone.
brief_explanation: The text describes two types of sacrificial rites (Yajnas): 1. Karma Yoga practitioners offer sacrifices to Devas (gods) while performing rituals. 2.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: श्रोत्रादीनीन्द्रियाण्यन्ये संयमाग्निषु जुह्वति | शब्दादीन्विषयानन्य इन्द्रियाग्निषु जुह्वति
english: Some again offer the organ of hearing and other senses as sacrifice in the fire of restraint; others offer sound and other objects of the senses as sacrifice in the fire of the senses.
brief_explanation: The Yogis restrain their senses, gathering them under the guidance of the Self, avoiding contact with sensual objects. This is considered an act of self-sacrifice. Alternatively, others direct their senses only towards pure and unforbidden sense objects, which is also a form of sacrifice.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: सर्वाणीन्द्रियकर्माणि प्राणकर्माणि चापरे | आत्मसंयमयोगाग्नौ जुह्वति ज्ञानदीपिते
english: Others again sacrifice all the functions of the senses and those of the breath (vital energy or Prana) in the fire of the Yoga of self-restraint kindled by knowledge.
brief_explanation: The fire of Yoga of self-restraint, similar to a lamp lit by oil, is kindled by knowledge. In this state, the functions of senses and breath cease, being absorbed into their cause.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: द्रव्ययज्ञास्तपोयज्ञा योगयज्ञास्तथापरे | स्वाध्यायज्ञानयज्ञाश्च यतयः संशितव्रताः
english: Others again offer wealth, austerity and Yoga as sacrifice, while the ascetics of self-restraint and rigid vows offer study of scriptures and knowledge as sacrifice.
brief_explanation: The text describes various forms of sacrifice: wealth offering, austerity, Yoga practice, and study/knowledge offering. Some are also referred to as ascetics or anchorites with rigid vows. The eight limbs of Raja Yoga include Yama (vows), Niyama (conduct), Asana (posture), Pranayama (breath control), Pratyahara (sense withdrawal), Dharana (concentration), Dhyana (meditation), and Samadhi (superconscious state).

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: अपाने जुह्वति प्राणं प्राणेऽपानं तथापरे | प्राणापानगती रुद्ध्वा प्राणायामपरायणाः
english: Others offer as sacrifice the outgoing breath in the incoming, and the incoming in the outgoing, restraining the course of the outgoing and the incoming breaths, solely absorbed in the restraint of the breath.
brief_explanation: The verse describes various practices related to breath control (Pranayama). Some Yogis focus on inhalation (Puraka), some on exhalation (Rechaka), and some on retention of breath (Kumbhaka). By practicing Pranayama, the sub-Pranas and other Pranas are merged into the chief Prana.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: अपरे नियताहाराः प्राणान्प्राणेषु जुह्वति | सर्वेऽप्येते यज्ञविदो यज्ञक्षपितकल्मषाः
english: Others who regulate their diet offer life-breaths in life-breaths. All these are knowers of sacrifice, whose sins are destroyed by sacrifice.
brief_explanation: Yogis, who have regulated their diet, offer their lifereaths (prana) as a sacrifice within the lifereaths, leading to purification of the mind and the destruction of sins. This refers to individuals who control their passions and appetites by limiting their food intake, thus weakening the organs of action.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: यज्ञशिष्टामृतभुजो यान्ति ब्रह्म सनातनम् | नायं लोकोऽस्त्ययज्ञस्य कुतोऽन्यः कुरुसत्तम
english: Those who eat the remnants of the sacrifice, which are like nectar, go to the eternal Brahman. This world is not for the man who does not perform sacrifice; how then can he have the other, O Arjuna?
brief_explanation: The best of the Kurus are informed that those who partake in the remnants of sacrifice, attaining knowledge of the Self through purified minds, ultimately reach the eternal Brahman. One who does not perform any sacrifices is unfit for even this world; therefore, how could they hope for a better world? (Reference to III.13)

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: एवं बहुविधा यज्ञा वितता ब्रह्मणो मुखे | कर्मजान्विद्धि तान्सर्वानेवं ज्ञात्वा विमोक्ष्यसे
english: Thus, manifold sacrifices are spread out before Brahman (literally) at the mouth or face of Brahman). Know them all as born of action and thus knowing, thou shalt be liberated.
brief_explanation: The verse suggests various sacrifices, interpreted as those found in the Vedas, are spread out. Recognize they are born from action because the Self transcends actions. By understanding these actions do not concern oneself and thus one is inactive, liberation from Samsara can be achieved.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: श्रेयान्द्रव्यमयाद्यज्ञाज्ज्ञानयज्ञः परन्तप | सर्वं कर्माखिलं पार्थ ज्ञाने परिसमाप्यते
english: Swami Sivananda did not comment on this sloka
brief_explanation: The text suggests that sacrifices with material objects result in material benefits and reincarnation, while the wisdom sacrifice leads to Moksha, making it superior. All actions eventually merge into knowledge, purifying the heart and leading to Self-realization. Actions offered to the Lord are part of Brahman's knowledge.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: तद्विद्धि प्रणिपातेन परिप्रश्नेन सेवया | उपदेक्ष्यन्ति ते ज्ञानं ज्ञानिनस्तत्त्वदर्शिनः
english: Know That by long prostration, by estion and by service; the wise who have realised the Truth will instruct thee in (that) knowledge.
brief_explanation: Prostrate or serve the wise, those who have realized Truth, for instruction on knowledge. A teacher well-versed in scriptures but lacking Self-realization won't help. One with both scriptural knowledge and Self-realization can instruct and aid in Self-realization.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: यज्ज्ञात्वा न पुनर्मोहमेवं यास्यसि पाण्डव | येन भूतान्यशेषेण द्रक्ष्यस्यात्मन्यथो मयि (var अशेषाणि)
english: Knowing ï1thatï1 thou shalt not, O Arjuna, again get deluded like this; and by that thou shalt see all beings in thy Self and also in Me.
brief_explanation: Acquiring the knowledge of the Self as mentioned earlier is attained through a Brahmanishtha Guru via prostration and service. Once gained, one will no longer be subject to delusion or error. One will perceive the underlying basic unity in all beings, including oneself and God, existing within one's own Self and also in the divine.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: अपि चेदसि पापेभ्यः सर्वेभ्यः पापकृत्तमः | सर्वं ज्ञानप्लवेनैव वृजिनं सन्तरिष्यसि
english: Even if thou art the most sinful of all sinners, yet thou shalt verily cross all sins by the raft of knowledge.
brief_explanation: The verse implies that even if one is considered a sinner among all, they can still transcend sin using the raft of self-knowledge.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: यथैधांसि समिद्धोऽग्निर्भस्मसात्कुरुतेऽर्जुन | ज्ञानाग्निः सर्वकर्माणि भस्मसात्कुरुते तथा
english: As the blazing fire reduces fuel to ashes, O Arjuna, so does the fire of knowledge reduce all actions to ashes.
brief_explanation: The fire of knowledge burns all actions, preventing them from producing future effects. This is like fuel being burned by a fire. When knowledge of the Self arises, actions lose their potency.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: न हि ज्ञानेन सदृशं पवित्रमिह विद्यते | तत्स्वयं योगसंसिद्धः कालेनात्मनि विन्दति
english: Verily, there is no purifier in this world like knowledge. He who is perfected in Yoga finds it in the Self in time.
brief_explanation: The text indicates that there is no purifier equal to self-knowledge. One who has achieved perfection through persistent practice of both action-oriented (Karma) and meditation-focused (Dhyana) Yoga will, over time, discover self-knowledge within themselves.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: श्रद्धावाँल्लभते ज्ञानं तत्परः संयतेन्द्रियः | ज्ञानं लब्ध्वा परां शान्तिमचिरेणाधिगच्छति
english: The man who is full of faith, who is devoted to it, and who has subdued the senses obtains (this) knowledge; and having obtained the knowledge he attains at once to the supreme peace.
brief_explanation: The man with faith obtains knowledge, one who has subdued the senses also gains knowledge, and both eventually achieve supreme peace or salvation (Moksha). These three qualities - faith, serving the Guru, subduing the senses - are essential for an aspirant to attain the supreme peace of the Eternal. One quality alone is not sufficient.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: अज्ञश्चाश्रद्दधानश्च संशयात्मा विनश्यति | नायं लोकोऽस्ति न परो न सुखं संशयात्मनः
english: The ignorant the faithless, the doubting self goes to destruction; there is neither this world nor the other, nor happiness for the doubting.
brief_explanation: The ignorant, faithless, and doubting self will perish. This refers to a person lacking knowledge of the Self, doubtful about the next world, and finding no happiness in either this or the next life due to their lack of faith and constant doubts.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: योगसंन्यस्तकर्माणं ज्ञानसञ्छिन्नसंशयम् | आत्मवन्तं न कर्माणि निबध्नन्ति धनञ्जय
english: He who has renounced actions by Yoga, whose doubts are rent asunder by knowledge, and who is self-possessed actions do not bind him, O Arjuna.
brief_explanation: The term "Atmavantam" refers to one who has attained self-realization, always vigilant over oneself. Through Yoga or the knowledge of Brahman, they renounce all actions as their doubts are resolved and actions no longer bind them due to being burned by wisdom. (Reference: II.48, III.9, IV.20)

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: तस्मादज्ञानसम्भूतं हृत्स्थं ज्ञानासिनात्मनः | छित्त्वैनं संशयं योगमातिष्ठोत्तिष्ठ भारत
english: Therefore with the sword of the knowledge (of the Self) cut asunder the doubt of the self born of ignorance, residing in thy heart, and take refuge in Yoga. Arise, O Arjuna.
brief_explanation: Doubt, born out of ignorance, causes mental distress and is sinful. Use the sword of self-knowledge to eliminate it. Stand up and fight against it, O Arjuna.

speaker: Arjuna
sanskrit: अर्जुन उवाच | संन्यासं कर्मणां कृष्ण पुनर्योगं च शंससि | यच्छ्रेय एतयोरेकं तन्मे ब्रूहि सुनिश्चितम्
english: Arjuna said Renunciation of actions, O Krishna, Thou praisest, and again Yoga. Tell me conclusively that which is the better of the two.
brief_explanation: Krishna teaches that one can either engage in renunciation of actions or their performance through Karma Yoga, but not both simultaneously. When asked which is better, he does not provide a definitive answer as it depends on the individual's spiritual progress and capabilities. However, the focus on selfless action (Karma Yoga) is emphasized in this discourse.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: श्रीभगवानुवाच | संन्यासः कर्मयोगश्च निःश्रेयसकरावुभौ | तयोस्तु कर्मसंन्यासात्कर्मयोगो विशिष्यते
english: The Blessed Lord said Renunciation and the Yoga of action both lead to the highest bliss; but of the two, the Yoga of action is superior to the renunciation of action.
brief_explanation: Both Sannyasa (renunciation) and Karma Yoga (action) lead to the highest bliss (Moksha). However, Karma Yoga, which involves performing actions with knowledge of the Self, is superior to mere renunciation of action without this self-knowledge. Additionally, Karma Yoga is considered easier and thus suitable for all.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: ज्ञेयः स नित्यसंन्यासी यो न द्वेष्टि न काङ्क्षति | निर्द्वन्द्वो हि महाबाहो सुखं बन्धात्प्रमुच्यते
english: He should be known as a perpertual Sannyasi who neither hates nor desires; for, free from the pairs of opposites, O mighty-armed Arjuna, he is easily set free from bondage.
brief_explanation: A true Sannyasi is not merely one who abandons actions due to circumstances, but one who transcends attachments and aversions towards sense objects and rises above dualities like pleasure and pain, success and failure. One need not have formally taken Sannyasa but should possess the mental attitude of renunciation and purity of heart for true sannyasis status. Physical renunciation is meaningless without inner transformation.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: साङ्ख्ययोगौ पृथग्बालाः प्रवदन्ति न पण्डिताः | एकमप्यास्थितः सम्यगुभयोर्विन्दते फलम्
english: Children, not the wise, speak of knowledge and the Yoga of action or the performance of action as though they are distinct and different; he who is truly established in one obtains the fruits of both.
brief_explanation: The children, or ignorant people, claim that knowledge and action are distinct with opposite results. However, the wise who have self-knowledge assert they lead to the same outcome - liberation. One who is established in either Sankhya or Yoga obtains the fruits of both, implying no diversity in the result or fruit.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: यत्साङ्ख्यैः प्राप्यते स्थानं तद्योगैरपि गम्यते | एकं साङ्ख्यं च योगं च यः पश्यति स पश्यति
english: That place which is reached by the Sankhyas or the Jnanis is reached by the Yogis (Karma Yogis). He sees, who sees knowledge and the performance of action (Karma Yoga) as one.
brief_explanation: The Sankhyas, through hearing, reflection, and deep meditation on Vedantic texts, reach Moksha directly by renouncing the world. Karma Yogis, who perform selfless actions without expecting fruits, indirectly reach the same state as Sankhyas through purification of heart, renunciation, and the eventual realization of Self. The one who perceives both Sankhya (knowledge) and Yoga (performance of action) as leading to the same result, sees correctly.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: संन्यासस्तु महाबाहो दुःखमाप्तुमयोगतः | योगयुक्तो मुनिर्ब्रह्म नचिरेणाधिगच्छति
english: But renunciation, O mighty-armed Arjuna, is hard to attain without Yoga; the Yoga-harmonised sage ickly goes to Brahman.
brief_explanation: The Muni, or sage of meditation, performs action harmonized with Yoga (selfless action), which leads to the attainment of Brahman, representing true renunciation and devotion to Self-knowledge. Karma Yoga, being easier for beginners, prepares one's mind for higher forms of yoga by purification.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: योगयुक्तो विशुद्धात्मा विजितात्मा जितेन्द्रियः | सर्वभूतात्मभूतात्मा कुर्वन्नपि न लिप्यते
english: He who is devoted to the path of action, whose mind is ite pure, who has conered the self, who has subdued his senses and who realises his Self as the Self in all beings, though acting, is not tainted.
brief_explanation: The practitioner, harmonized by Yoga, is one who has purified their mind through devotion to action, conquered the self, subdued the senses, and recognizes their Self as the Self in all beings. Despite performing actions, they will not be bound by them, serving as an example for others. (Referencing verse 17 from chapter 18)

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: नैव किञ्चित्करोमीति युक्तो मन्येत तत्त्ववित् | पश्यञ्शृण्वन्स्पृशञ्जिघ्रन्नश्नन्गच्छन्स्वपञ्श्वसन्
english: "I do nothing at all," thus would the harmonised knower of Truth think seeing, hearing, touching, smelling, eating, going, sleeping, breathing.
brief_explanation: The text suggests a list of activities: seeing, hearing, touching, smelling, eating, going, sleeping, and breathing. It questions whether one who is centered in the Self should think that a knower of Truth engages in these activities. No commentary is provided.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: प्रलपन्विसृजन्गृह्णन्नुन्मिषन्निमिषन्नपि | इन्द्रियाणीन्द्रियार्थेषु वर्तन्त इति धारयन्
english: Speaking, letting go, seizing, opening and closing the eyes convinced that the senses move among the sense-objects.
brief_explanation: The liberated sage identifies with the Self or Brahman and witnesses the activities of the senses without participating. He thinks as an observer, "I do not see the eyes perceive, I do not hear the ears hear," etc., experiencing inaction within action due to wisdom's fire. (Cf.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: ब्रह्मण्याधाय कर्माणि सङ्गं त्यक्त्वा करोति यः | लिप्यते न स पापेन पद्मपत्रमिवाम्भसा
english: He who does actions, offering them to Brahman, and abandoning attachment, is not tainted by sin, just as a lotus-leaf is not tainted by water.
brief_explanation: The Yogi who performs actions without egoism or attachment to results, viewing them as offerings to the Lord, remains untainted by actions. He has no desire for liberation and perceives inaction within action. All his actions are purified through wisdom, freeing him from the cycle of birth and death, achieving a pure heart, gaining Self-knowledge, and ultimately attaining liberation.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: कायेन मनसा बुद्ध्या केवलैरिन्द्रियैरपि | योगिनः कर्म कुर्वन्ति सङ्गं त्यक्त्वात्मशुद्धये
english: Yogis, having abandoned attachment, perform actions only by the body, mind, intellect, and even by the senses, for the purification of the self.
brief_explanation: Yogis, referring to Karma Yogis, perform action through the body, mind, intellect, and senses, but they do so without egoism or selfishness. Their actions are aimed at purifying their self, and they offer all actions to the Lord. The term "only" (Kevalam) applies to being free from egoism and selfishness in relation to the body, mind, intellect, and senses.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: युक्तः कर्मफलं त्यक्त्वा शान्तिमाप्नोति नैष्ठिकीम् | अयुक्तः कामकारेण फले सक्तो निबध्यते
english: The united one (the well poised or the harmonised) having abandoned the fruit of action attains to the eternal peace: the non-united only (the unsteady or the unbalanced) impelled by desire, attached to the fruit, is bound.
brief_explanation: The harmonious individual, performing actions for the Lord without attachment to their results, attains peace born of devotion (santim naishthikim). This path involves four stages: purity of mind, attainment of knowledge, renunciation of actions, and steadiness in wisdom. Conversely, an unbalanced individual driven by desire and focused on the fruits of their actions remains bound.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: सर्वकर्माणि मनसा संन्यस्यास्ते सुखं वशी | नवद्वारे पुरे देही नैव कुर्वन्न कारयन्
english: Mentally renouncing all actions and self-controlled, the embodied one rests happily in the nine-gated city, neither acting nor causing others (body and senses) to act.
brief_explanation: The renounced one, having controlled the senses, rests happily within the nine-gated city, also known as the body. He recognizes inaction in action and is free from worries. In this city, the Self is the ruler, while the senses, mind, subconscious mind, and intellect are the inhabitants.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: न कर्तृत्वं न कर्माणि लोकस्य सृजति प्रभुः | न कर्मफलसंयोगं स्वभावस्तु प्रवर्तते
english: Neither agency nor actions does the Lord create for the world, nor union with the fruits of actions. But it is Nature that acts.
brief_explanation: The Lord doesn't create agency, actions, or bind people to the fruits of their actions. Instead, it is Prakriti or nature that leads to action. (Referring to III.33 for further explanation.)

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: नादत्ते कस्यचित्पापं न चैव सुकृतं विभुः | अज्ञानेनावृतं ज्ञानं तेन मुह्यन्ति जन्तवः
english: The Lord takes neither the demerit nor even the merit of any; knowledge is enveloped by ignorance, thery beings are deluded.
brief_explanation: Knowledge is enveloped by ignorance, causing beings to be deluded. This leads them to believe they are the doer, enjoyer, and reaper of merits or demerits. However, identifying with the mortal aspects such as body, mind, lifeforce, and senses binds one.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: ज्ञानेन तु तदज्ञानं येषां नाशितमात्मनः | तेषामादित्यवज्ज्ञानं प्रकाशयति तत्परम्
english: But to those whose ignorance is destroyed by the knowledge of the Self, like the sun, knowledge reveals the Supreme (Brahman).
brief_explanation: The annihilation of ignorance by wisdom leads to the destruction of suffering for the self, revealing the Highest (Brahman) in a manner similar to how the sun illuminates physical objects.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: तद्बुद्धयस्तदात्मानस्तन्निष्ठास्तत्परायणाः | गच्छन्त्यपुनरावृत्तिं ज्ञाननिर्धूतकल्मषाः
english: Their intellect absorbed in That, their self being That, established in That, with That for their supreme goal, they go whence there is no return, their sins dispelled by knowledge.
brief_explanation: Individuals who concentrate their intellect on Brahman, the Supreme Self, perceive it as their own self. Through persistent meditation, they become established in Brahman, losing awareness of the world of forms and names. Their sole focus becomes Brahman, which provides them with ultimate joy, satisfaction, and contentment.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: विद्याविनयसम्पन्ने ब्राह्मणे गवि हस्तिनि | शुनि चैव श्वपाके च पण्डिताः समदर्शिनः
english: Sages look with an eal eye on a Brahmana endowed with learning and humility, on a cow, on an elephant, and even on a dog and an outcaste.
brief_explanation: The verse describes a liberated sage or Jivanmukta, who has a transcendent vision that perceives the Self everywhere, beyond the influence of limiting adjuncts like learning, humility, caste, or species. This vision is compared to the sun's reflection falling on various bodies of water, not being affected by them. The Brahmana, being Sattvic, is among those perceived by the sage as the immortal Self, unaffected by the three gunas (qualities) and their tendencies.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: इहैव तैर्जितः सर्गो येषां साम्ये स्थितं मनः | निर्दोषं हि समं ब्रह्म तस्माद् ब्रह्मणि ते स्थिताः
english: Even here (in this world) birth (everything) is overcome by those whose minds rest in eality; Brahman is spotless indeed and eal; therefore they are established in Brahman.
brief_explanation: The mind, when established in equanimity or evenness, attains balance and overcomes creation/destruction, achieving liberation. In a state of perfect balance, the individual realizes Brahman, who dwells equally within all beings, being spotless and eternal despite dwelling in various forms.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: न प्रहृष्येत्प्रियं प्राप्य नोद्विजेत्प्राप्य चाप्रियम् | स्थिरबुद्धिरसम्मूढो ब्रह्मविद् ब्रह्मणि स्थितः
english: Resting in Brahman, with steady intellect and undeluded, the knower of Brahman neither rejoiceth on obtaining what is pleasant nor grieveth on obtaining what is unpleasant.
brief_explanation: The verse describes the state of a liberated sage or Jivanmukta. They are established in Brahman, have steady intellect and are undeluded, not swayed by pleasure or pain upon obtaining pleasant or unpleasant objects. This contrasts with those who identify with the body and mind, who experience exhilaration or grief accordingly.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: बाह्यस्पर्शेष्वसक्तात्मा विन्दत्यात्मनि यत्सुखम् | स ब्रह्मयोगयुक्तात्मा सुखमक्षयमश्नुते
english: With the self unattached to external contacts he finds happiness in the Self; with the self engaged in the meditation of Brahman he attains to the endless happiness.
brief_explanation: The one whose mind is detached from external contacts finds undying happiness within, when deeply engaged in the meditation of Brahman. To experience the endless bliss of the Self within, one must withdraw the senses from their objects and immerse oneself in deep contemplation of the Self.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: ये हि संस्पर्शजा भोगा दुःखयोनय एव ते | आद्यन्तवन्तः कौन्तेय न तेषु रमते बुधः
english: The enjoyments that are born of contacts are only generators of pain, for they have a beginning and an end, O Arjuna; the wise man does not rejoice in them.
brief_explanation: The text suggests that a person seeks temporary happiness from external, perishable objects but encounters sorrow instead due to their transient nature. It's advised to withdraw the senses from these objects and focus on the immortal and blissful Self within. The senseobjects have beginnings and ends, causing pain upon separation, with any pleasure experienced being fleeting and illusory, often due to ignorance.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: शक्नोतीहैव यः सोढुं प्राक्शरीरविमोक्षणात् | कामक्रोधोद्भवं वेगं स युक्तः स सुखी नरः
english: He who is able, while still here (in this world) to withstand, before the liberation from the body, the impulse born out of desire and anger he is a Yogi, he is a happy man.
brief_explanation: The term "shaknoti" refers to one's ability to withstand powerful enemies such as desire and anger before liberation from the body. A harmonized or steadfast individual (yukta) who has controlled these impulses is considered the happiest man in this world, not one with immense wealth, a beautiful wife, or children. Desire and anger are powerful impediments to eternal bliss, so it's crucial to make strong efforts to eradicate them.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: योऽन्तःसुखोऽन्तरारामस्तथान्तर्ज्योतिरेव यः | स योगी ब्रह्मनिर्वाणं ब्रह्मभूतोऽधिगच्छति
english: He who is happy within, who rejoices within, and who is illuminated within, that Yogi attains absolute freedom or Moksha, himself becoming Brahman.
brief_explanation: The individual referred to is one whose happiness resides within, who finds joy internally, and who is illuminated from within. This person is a Yogi who achieves absolute freedom (Brahmanirvana) or Moksha while still alive, becoming a Jivanmukta.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: लभन्ते ब्रह्मनिर्वाणमृषयः क्षीणकल्मषाः | छिन्नद्वैधा यतात्मानः सर्वभूतहिते रताः
english: The sages (Rishis) obtain absolute freedom or Moksha they whose sins have been destroyed, whose dualities (perception of dualities or experience of the pairs of opposites) are torn asunder, who are self-controlled, and intent on the welfare of all beings.
brief_explanation: The Rishis who have destroyed their sins, torn apart dualities through constant meditation on nondual Brahman, and are self-controlled, rejoice in the welfare of all beings. This occurs when they perform rituals like Agnihotra without expecting results and through other selfless services. They never harm others in thought, word, or deed, as they perceive all beings as their own Self (similar to XII.4).

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: कामक्रोधवियुक्तानां यतीनां यतचेतसाम् | अभितो ब्रह्मनिर्वाणं वर्तते विदितात्मनाम्
english: Absolute freedom (or Brahmic bliss) exists on all sides for those self-controlled ascetics who are free from desire and anger, who have controlled their thoughts and who have realised the Self.
brief_explanation: Renouncing desire and anger, practicing self-control, and mastering thoughts on all sides, the self-realized ascetics who are deeply engrossed in Brahman or the Self experience instant liberation (Kaivalya Moksha). Gradual purification of the mind, attainment of knowledge, renunciation of actions, and eventually Moksha is achieved through Karma Yoga (Krama Mukti).

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: स्पर्शान्कृत्वा बहिर्बाह्यांश्चक्षुश्चैवान्तरे भ्रुवोः | प्राणापानौ समौ कृत्वा नासाभ्यन्तरचारिणौ
english: Shutting out (all) external contacts and fixing the gaze between the eyrow, ealising the outgoing and incoming breaths moving within the nostrils.
brief_explanation: The verses discuss meditation Yoga, focusing on shutting out external objects like sounds and sense objects by steady gazing between eyebrows and regulating breaths for mental and bodily harmony. (Reference: VI.10-14, VIII.10)

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: यतेन्द्रियमनोबुद्धिर्मुनिर्मोक्षपरायणः | विगतेच्छाभयक्रोधो यः सदा मुक्त एव सः
english: With the senses, the mind and the intellect (ever) controlled, having liberation as his supreme goal, free from desire, fear and anger the sage is verily liberated for ever.
brief_explanation: The sage, always aiming for liberation, achieves perpetual peace when free from desires, fear, and anger as their absence subjugates his senses, mind, and intellect. When the mind moves beyond modifications of desire and fear, it naturally gravitates towards self-realization or Moksha. The sage, through constant reflection and contemplation (Manana), attains perpetual freedom.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: भोक्तारं यज्ञतपसां सर्वलोकमहेश्वरम् | सुहृदं सर्वभूतानां ज्ञात्वा मां शान्तिमृच्छति
english: He who knows Me as the enjoyer of sacrifices and austerities, the great Lord of all the worlds and the friend of all beings, attains to peace.
brief_explanation: The text explains that Krishna is the Lord of all sacrifices and austerities, their goal and God. He is a friend to all beings and the dispenser of the fruits of actions. On knowing Him, one attains peace and liberation.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: श्रीभगवानुवाच | अनाश्रितः कर्मफलं कार्यं कर्म करोति यः | स संन्यासी च योगी च न निरग्निर्न चाक्रियः
english: The Blessed Lord said He who performs his bounden duty without depending on the fruits of his actions he is a Sannyasi and a Yogi; not he who is without fire and without action.
brief_explanation: Actions performed without expecting their fruits lead to Dhyana Yoga, or the Yoga of Meditation. This applies to a Sannyasi and a Yogi, but they are used in a secondary sense only. The Sannyasi has renounced daily rituals like Agnihotra and other meritorious acts.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: यं संन्यासमिति प्राहुर्योगं तं विद्धि पाण्डव | न ह्यसंन्यस्तसङ्कल्पो योगी भवति कश्चन
english: Do thou, O Arjuna, know Yoga to be that which they call renunciation; no one verily becomes a Yogi who has not renounced thoughts.
brief_explanation: The term Yam refers to renunciation, and they call this practice as Yoga. One who has not abandoned thoughts and plans for future actions cannot become a steady-minded yogi. Lord Krishna praises Karma Yoga here as it serves as an external means leading to Meditation Yoga (Dhyana Yoga).

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: आरुरुक्षोर्मुनेर्योगं कर्म कारणमुच्यते | योगारूढस्य तस्यैव शमः कारणमुच्यते
english: For a sage who wishes to attain to Yoga, action is said to be the means; for the same sage who has attained to Yoga, inaction (iescence) is said to be the means.
brief_explanation: The passage explains that for those struggling with long-term meditation, action can help purify the mind and lead to steady concentration and meditation, ultimately aiding in Yoga. For a sage already enthroned in Yoga, renunciation of actions is said to be the means for more steady and peaceful mind, and eventual fixation in the Self. Additionally, for a Brahmana, virtues such as knowledge of oneness, truthfulness, good character, steadiness, harmlessness, straightforwardness, and renunciation of all actions are considered valuable.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: यदा हि नेन्द्रियार्थेषु न कर्मस्वनुषज्जते | सर्वसङ्कल्पसंन्यासी योगारूढस्तदोच्यते
english: When a man is not attached to the sense-objects or to actions, having renounced all thoughts, then he is said to have attained to Yoga.
brief_explanation: The yogi who has control over their mind, withdrawing it from the sense objects and actions, is said to have attained Yoga. By renouncing all thoughts and desires for worldly or otherworldly objects, one can become a Yogarudha. This implies the renunciation of all actions as well, since actions are born of thoughts.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: उद्धरेदात्मनात्मानं नात्मानमवसादयेत् | आत्मैव ह्यात्मनो बन्धुरात्मैव रिपुरात्मनः
english: One should raise oneself by one's Self alone; let not one lower oneself; for the Self alone is the friend of oneself, and the Self alone is the enemy of oneself.
brief_explanation: Practice Yoga, discipline the senses and mind. Elevate yourself to become a Yogarudha (yogi on a lofty seat). Rise above worldliness and become divine.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: बन्धुरात्मात्मनस्तस्य येनात्मैवात्मना जितः | अनात्मनस्तु शत्रुत्वे वर्तेतात्मैव शत्रुवत्
english: The Self is the friend of the self of him by whom the self has been conered by the Self, but to the unconered self, this Self stands in the position of an enemy, like an (external) foe.
brief_explanation: The lower mind, representing Rajas and Tamas, functions as an enemy for the individual. Conversely, the higher mind, embodying Sattva, serves as a friend. By aligning with the higher mind, one can effectively subdue the lower mind.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: जितात्मनः प्रशान्तस्य परमात्मा समाहितः | शीतोष्णसुखदुःखेषु तथा मानापमानयोः
english: The Supreme Self of him who is self-controlled and peaceful is balanced in cold and heat, pleasure and pain, as also in honour and dishonour.
brief_explanation: The self-controlled Yogi, rooted in the Supreme Self, maintains balance amidst cold and heat, pleasure and pain, honor and dishonor. When his senses are subdued, his mind peaceful, unaffected by opposites, and has renounced actions, he attains Self-realization, remaining serene and unchanged in the face of nature's varying conditions.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: ज्ञानविज्ञानतृप्तात्मा कूटस्थो विजितेन्द्रियः | युक्त इत्युच्यते योगी समलोष्टाश्मकाञ्चनः
english: The Yogi who is satisfied with the knowledge and the wisdom (of the Self), who has conered the senses, and to whom a clod of earth, a piece of stone and gold are the same, is said to be harmonied (i.e., is said to have attained Nirvikalpa Samadhi).
brief_explanation: The yogi who is satisfied with both theoretical knowledge and spiritual experience, unshaken like an anvil amidst sense objects, is referred to as Kutastha, which signifies a changeless state similar to Brahman, the silent witness of the mind.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: सुहृन्मित्रार्युदासीनमध्यस्थद्वेष्यबन्धुषु | साधुष्वपि च पापेषु समबुद्धिर्विशिष्यते
english: He who is of the same mind to the good-hearted, friends, enemies, the indifferent, the neutral, the hateful, the relatives, the righteous and the unrighteous, excels.
brief_explanation: The term "suhyan" refers to a goodhearted individual who performs good deeds without expecting anything in return. "Mitra" denotes friends, "aryudasinam" signifies being indifferent, "adhya" means enemies, "dveshya bandhusu" indicates relatives, "sahdbuddhi" refers to having an even or impartial mind, and "vishishyate" implies excelling. In this context, a yogi with an even mind treats everyone equally regardless of caste, creed, or color.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: योगी युञ्जीत सततमात्मानं रहसि स्थितः | एकाकी यतचित्तात्मा निराशीरपरिग्रहः
english: Let the Yogi try constantly to keep the mind steady, remaining in solitude, alone, with the mind and the body controlled, and free from hope and covetousness.
brief_explanation: The Yogi is one with a controlled mind and body, free from hope and noncovetousness, who practices meditation constantly in solitude. A householder can also practice meditation in a solitary room or near a holy river. Constant practice is essential for Self-realization.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: शुचौ देशे प्रतिष्ठाप्य स्थिरमासनमात्मनः | नात्युच्छ्रितं नातिनीचं चैलाजिनकुशोत्तरम्
english: In a clean spot, having established a firm seat of his own, neither too high nor too low, made of a cloth, a skin and Kusa-grass, one over the other.
brief_explanation: The verse describes an ideal seat for meditation, prescribed by the Lord. It suggests placing a cloth over skin and grass as the seat. One can sit on a naturally clean spot like a riverbank or make any other spot clean.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: तत्रैकाग्रं मनः कृत्वा यतचित्तेन्द्रियक्रियः | उपविश्यासने युञ्ज्याद्योगमात्मविशुद्धये
english: There, having made the mind one-pointed, with the actions of the mind and the senses controlled, let him, seated on the seat, practise Yoga for the purification of the self.
brief_explanation: Make the mind one-pointed by practicing Yoga for the purification of the self, which is the mind in a secondary sense. Withdraw it from all sense objects, focusing on a single point of meditation. Regular practice and introspection can help control the wandering mind and purify the subconscious.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: समं कायशिरोग्रीवं धारयन्नचलं स्थिरः | सम्प्रेक्ष्य नासिकाग्रं स्वं दिशश्चानवलोकयन्
english: Let him firmly hold his body, head and neck erect and still, gazing at the tip of his nose, without looking around.
brief_explanation: The verse describes a steady posture (Asana) and gaze (Drishti) for meditation. Maintaining a still body helps keep the mind steady. The recommended pose is either lotus or adept pose, with the gaze focused on the tip of the nose (Nasikagra Drishti).

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: प्रशान्तात्मा विगतभीर्ब्रह्मचारिव्रते स्थितः | मनः संयम्य मच्चित्तो युक्त आसीत मत्परः
english: Serene-minded, fearless, firm in the vow of a Brahmachari, having controlled the mind, thinking of Me and balanced in mind, let him sit, having Me as his supreme goal.
brief_explanation: The spiritual aspirant should have a serene mind, achieved through the eradication of desires and fears. A fearless individual is crucial for self-realization. The aspirant should follow the vow of Brahmacharya (celibacy) and control their mind, balancing pleasure and pain, while thinking of the Lord as the supreme goal.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: युञ्जन्नेवं सदात्मानं योगी नियतमानसः | शान्तिं निर्वाणपरमां मत्संस्थामधिगच्छति
english: Thus always keeping the mind balanced, the Yogi, with the mind controlled, attains to the peace abiding in Me, which culminates in liberation.
brief_explanation: The Yogi who maintains a controlled mind in balance attains to the eternal peace, which culminates in liberation (Moksha), while abiding in the Supreme Self.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: नात्यश्नतस्तु योगोऽस्ति न चैकान्तमनश्नतः | न चातिस्वप्नशीलस्य जाग्रतो नैव चार्जुन
english: Verily Yoga is not possible for him who eats too much, nor for him who does not eat at all, nor for him who sleeps too much, nor for him who is (always) awake, O Arjuna.
brief_explanation: This verse suggests moderation in eating and sleeping for those practicing Yoga. Eating too much may cause indigestion, flatulence, and diseases of the bowels and liver. Eating too little leads to weakness and inability to meditate for long periods.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: युक्ताहारविहारस्य युक्तचेष्टस्य कर्मसु | युक्तस्वप्नावबोधस्य योगो भवति दुःखहा
english: Yoga becomes the destroyer of pain for him who is moderate in eating and recreation (such as walking, etc.), who is moderate in exertion in actions, who is moderate in sleep and wakefulness.
brief_explanation: The verse 6.17 in the Bhagavad Gita describes Yoga as the destroyer of pain for one who adopts a moderate lifestyle, including diet, recreation, exertion in actions, sleep, and wakefulness. This implies the importance of maintaining a balanced approach to various aspects of life for spiritual growth. The Lord warns against extremes, such as excessive asceticism, which can hinder success in Yoga.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: यदा विनियतं चित्तमात्मन्येवावतिष्ठते | निःस्पृहः सर्वकामेभ्यो युक्त इत्युच्यते तदा
english: When the perfectly controlled mind rests in the Self only, free from longing for all the objects of desires, then it is said, 'He is united'.
brief_explanation: The mind achieves one-pointedness when it's perfectly controlled and free from all desires, resting in the Self. This state, known as Yukta, signifies union with the Self, where the yogi experiences harmony, balance, and Samadhi, which is unity with the Supreme Self. Without this union, harmony or balance is impossible.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: यथा दीपो निवातस्थो नेङ्गते सोपमा स्मृता | योगिनो यतचित्तस्य युञ्जतो योगमात्मनः
english: As a lamp placed in a windless spot does not flicker to such is compared the Yogi of controlled mind, practising Yoga in the Self (or absorbed in the Yoga of the Self).
brief_explanation: The simile suggests that a controlled and practiced mind, like a lamp placed in a windless place, illuminates the hidden spiritual treasures within the Self, symbolizing the power of focus in Yoga.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: यत्रोपरमते चित्तं निरुद्धं योगसेवया | यत्र चैवात्मनात्मानं पश्यन्नात्मनि तुष्यति
english: When the mind, restrained by the practice of Yoga attains to quietude and when seeing the Self by the self, he is satisfied in his own Self.
brief_explanation: The verses suggest that when the mind is completely withdrawn from sensory objects, a state of supreme peace arises. With constant practice of concentration, the Yogi perceives the Supreme Self through a purified and focused mind, achieving ultimate satisfaction within the Self.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: सुखमात्यन्तिकं यत्तद् बुद्धिग्राह्यमतीन्द्रियम् | वेत्ति यत्र न चैवायं स्थितश्चलति तत्त्वतः
english: When he (the Yogi) feels that Infinite Bliss which can be grasped by the (pure) intellect and which transcends the senses, and established wherein he never moves from the Reality.
brief_explanation: The Infinite Bliss that transcends the senses can be realized by the pure intellect, which functions independently during deep meditation as the senses cease to operate. This purity is achieved through self-restraint, observances, and consistent meditation as per Yama and Niyama practices.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: यं लब्ध्वा चापरं लाभं मन्यते नाधिकं ततः | यस्मिन्स्थितो न दुःखेन गुरुणापि विचाल्यते
english: Which, having obtained, he thinks there is no other gain superior to it; wherein estabished, he is not moved even by heavy sorrow.
brief_explanation: The passage discusses the attainment of Self-realization, which is considered the greatest acquisition. Once established in the Supreme Self, one becomes free from delusion and sorrow, as they are attributes of the physical body and mind. When identified with the sorrowless and painless Brahman, one cannot be affected by heavy sorrow or pain.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: तं विद्याद् दुःखसंयोगवियोगं योगसंज्ञितम् | स निश्चयेन योक्तव्यो योगोऽनिर्विण्णचेतसा
english: Let that be known by the name of Yoga, the severance from union with pain. This Yoga should be practised with determination and with an undesponding mind.
brief_explanation: The verse describes Yoga as a state of severance from union with pain, named as such. It should be practiced with determination by an individual with an undisturbed mind to achieve its benefits, which include infinite bliss, perfect satisfaction, and freedom from sorrow. A wavering mind may hinder success in Yoga.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: सङ्कल्पप्रभवान्कामांस्त्यक्त्वा सर्वानशेषतः | मनसैवेन्द्रियग्रामं विनियम्य समन्ततः
english: Abandoning without reserve all desires born of Sankalpa (thought and imagination) and completely restraining the whole group of the senses by the mind from all sides.
brief_explanation: Completely abandoning all desires without reserve is essential, as they are born of imagination. Control the senses from all sides by the mind through constant practice of abstraction to achieve a calm mind. Cultivate strong discrimination and dispassion for sensual pleasures.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: शनैः शनैरुपरमेद् बुद्ध्या धृतिगृहीतया | आत्मसंस्थं मनः कृत्वा न किञ्चिदपि चिन्तयेत्
english: Little by little let him attain to ietude by the intellect held firmly; having made the mind establish itself in the Self, let him not think of anything.
brief_explanation: Gradually, the practitioner attains tranquility through the intellect held firm and steady. By constant practice, the mind is placed in the Self, filling the heart with peace and bliss. Through ceaseless contemplation of the immortal Self within, the mind ceases to think of sense pleasures.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: यतो यतो निश्चरति मनश्चञ्चलमस्थिरम् | ततस्ततो नियम्यैतदात्मन्येव वशं नयेत्
english: From whatever cause the restless and unsteady mind wanders away, from that let him restrain it and bring it under the control of the Self alone.
brief_explanation: This verse suggests a method to control the restless and unsteady mind. Comparing it to a bull that needs to be dragged back home, the mind should be pulled towards one's internal focus or center (Atman). Offering temporary pleasures won't keep the bull at home, similarly, the mind must taste the eternal bliss of Self through concentration.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: प्रशान्तमनसं ह्येनं योगिनं सुखमुत्तमम् | उपैति शान्तरजसं ब्रह्मभूतमकल्मषम्
english: Supreme Bliss verily comes to this Yogi whose mind is ite peaceful, whose passion is ieted, who has become Brahman and who is free from sin.
brief_explanation: The verse describes benefits of Yoga: supreme bliss comes to the Yogi with a peaceful mind, calmed passions, destroyed attachments, self-knowledge, and a realization that all is Brahman. The Yogi is also taintless, unaffected by good or evil.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: युञ्जन्नेवं सदात्मानं योगी विगतकल्मषः | सुखेन ब्रह्मसंस्पर्शमत्यन्तं सुखमश्नुते
english: The Yogi, always engaging the mind thus (in the practice of Yoga), freed from sins, easily enjoys the Infinite Bliss of contact with Brahman (the Eternal).
brief_explanation: The yogi, through yoga practices like sense withdrawal and concentration, loses contact with sensory objects and connects with the immortal Self (Brahman). This connection brings infinite bliss, unlike transitory sensual pleasures. Therefore, one should aim to realize the Self within, as a Yogi removes obstacles towards union with the Lord and maintains a constant connection with the Self.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: सर्वभूतस्थमात्मानं सर्वभूतानि चात्मनि | ईक्षते योगयुक्तात्मा सर्वत्र समदर्शनः
english: With the mind harmonised by Yoga he sees the Self abiding in all beings and all beings in the Self; he sees the same everywhere.
brief_explanation: The Yogi, united with Yoga, perceives oneness of the Self everywhere, viewing all beings as one with the Brahman through an intuitive eye. This vision signifies a profound understanding that the Self and Brahman are indistinguishable.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: यो मां पश्यति सर्वत्र सर्वं च मयि पश्यति | तस्याहं न प्रणश्यामि स च मे न प्रणश्यति
english: He who sees Me everywhere and sees everything in Me, he never becomes separated from Me, nor do I become separated from him.
brief_explanation: The verse describes the vision of oneness, where one who perceives the self as present everywhere in all beings will not disappear from the Self or be lost to it. This union results in the seer and the Self becoming identical. The Self neither abandons nor is abandoned by the sage.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: सर्वभूतस्थितं यो मां भजत्येकत्वमास्थितः | सर्वथा वर्तमानोऽपि स योगी मयि वर्तते
english: He who, being established in unity, worships Me Who dwells in all beings, that Yogi abides in Me, whatever may be his mode of living.
brief_explanation: The yogi who perceives unity and abides in all beings by worshiping (or realizing) Me as the Self of all, remains in every way established within Me, is ever liberated. This refers to a person like Sadana, who despite being a butcher, lived in God because his mind was constantly fixed on the Lord's lotus feet.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: आत्मौपम्येन सर्वत्र समं पश्यति योऽर्जुन | सुखं वा यदि वा दुःखं स योगी परमो मतः
english: He who, through the likeness of the Self, O Arjuna, sees eality everywhere, be it pleasure or pain, he is regarded as the highest Yogi.
brief_explanation: The yogi who perceives that whatever is pleasure or pain for himself is also so for all other beings, causing no harm to anyone, is considered the highest. He sees everywhere the likeness of the Self and is established in the unity of the Self.

speaker: Arjuna
sanskrit: अर्जुन उवाच | योऽयं योगस्त्वया प्रोक्तः साम्येन मधुसूदन | एतस्याहं न पश्यामि चञ्चलत्वात्स्थितिं स्थिराम्
english: Arjuna said This Yoga of eanimity taught by Thee, O Krishna, I do not see its steady continuance, because of the restlessness (of the mind).
brief_explanation: The speaker finds it challenging to maintain steadiness in Yoga, taught by You, due to the restless nature of the mind. Despite its constant fluctuation, the speaker is unable to achieve a steady focus.

speaker: Unknown
sanskrit: चञ्चलं हि मनः कृष्ण प्रमाथि बलवद् दृढम् | तस्याहं निग्रहं मन्ये वायोरिव सुदुष्करम्
english: The mind verily is restless, turbulent, strong and unyielding, O Krishna: I deem it as difficult to control it as to control the wind.
brief_explanation: The mind, being constantly changeable, is inherently restless. Krishna, meaning 'scraper,' removes sins and evil causes from devotees' hearts. The mind is also turbulent, strong, and obstinate, causing agitation in the body and senses.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: श्रीभगवानुवाच | असंशयं महाबाहो मनो दुर्निग्रहं चलम् | अभ्यासेन तु कौन्तेय वैराग्येण च गृह्यते
english: The Blessed Lord said Undoubtedly, O mighty-armed Arjuna, the mind is difficult to control and restless; but by practice and by dispassion it may be restrained.
brief_explanation: The constant practice of meditation on the self or God helps to steady the restless mind, as it diminishes the mind's vacillation and desires. Dispassion, or indifference towards worldly objects, can also help in this restraint of the mind. This is achieved by continuously contemplating the flaws of worldly pleasures, encouraging the mind to seek enjoyment within the immortal and changeless self instead.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: असंयतात्मना योगो दुष्प्राप इति मे मतिः | वश्यात्मना तु यतता शक्योऽवाप्तुमुपायतः
english: I think Yoga is hard to be attained by one of uncontrolled self, but the self-controlled and striving one can attain to it by the (proper) means.
brief_explanation: The uncontrolled self refers to an individual who hasn't mastered control over their senses and mind through consistent practice of detachment and meditation. On the other hand, a self-controlled person has achieved such control. They can attain Self-realization through proper means and persistent effort.

speaker: Arjuna
sanskrit: अर्जुन उवाच | अयतिः श्रद्धयोपेतो योगाच्चलितमानसः | अप्राप्य योगसंसिद्धिं कां गतिं कृष्ण गच्छति
english: Arjuna said He who is unable to control himself though he has the faith, and whose mind wanders away from Yoga, what end does he, having failed to attain perfection in Yoga, mee,t O Krishna?
brief_explanation: The individual has faith in Yoga but lacks control over senses and mind, causing his mind to wander even at death and loss of memory. Failing to attain perfection in Yoga (Self-realization or knowledge of the Self), they are uncertain about the path and end they will meet.

speaker: Unknown
sanskrit: कच्चिन्नोभयविभ्रष्टश्छिन्नाभ्रमिव नश्यति | अप्रतिष्ठो महाबाहो विमूढो ब्रह्मणः पथि
english: Swami Sivananda did not comment on this sloka
brief_explanation: No comment provided by Swami Sivananda for the given sloka.

speaker: Unknown
sanskrit: एतन्मे संशयं कृष्ण छेत्तुमर्हस्यशेषतः | त्वदन्यः संशयस्यास्य छेत्ता न ह्युपपद्यते
english: This doubt of mine, O Krishna, do Thou dispel completely; because it is not possible for any but Thee to dispel this doubt.
brief_explanation: Krishna, as the omniscient Lord, is the best teacher for dispelling this doubt since no Rishi, Deva, or Muni can eradicate it completely.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: श्रीभगवानुवाच | पार्थ नैवेह नामुत्र विनाशस्तस्य विद्यते | न हि कल्याणकृत्कश्चिद् दुर्गतिं तात गच्छति
english: The Blessed Lord said O Arjuna, neither in this world, nor in the next world is there destruction for him; none, verily, who does good, O My son, ever comes to grief.
brief_explanation: In verse 6.40, Krishna tells Arjuna that one who does not achieve spiritual perfection in this life will neither be destroyed in this world nor the next. Instead, they may be reborn into a lower state or experience grief.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: प्राप्य पुण्यकृतां लोकानुषित्वा शाश्वतीः समाः | शुचीनां श्रीमतां गेहे योगभ्रष्टोऽभिजायते
english: Having attained to the worlds of the righteous and having dwelt there for everlasting years, he who fell from Yoga is rorn in a house of the pure and wealthy.
brief_explanation: The one fallen from Yoga is either one who could not achieve perfection or slackened in practice, becoming vulnerable to worldly desires. The righteous are those following truth, performing virtuous acts like charity, rituals, and worship, and adhering to scriptural guidelines. Everlasting years refer to a long but finite period, not absolute eternity.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: अथवा योगिनामेव कुले भवति धीमताम् | एतद्धि दुर्लभतरं लोके जन्म यदीदृशम्
english: Or he is born in a family of even the wise Yogis; verily a birth like this is very difficult to obtain in this world.
brief_explanation: A birth in the family of wise Yogis is very difficult to obtain in the world, similar to the one described earlier.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: तत्र तं बुद्धिसंयोगं लभते पौर्वदेहिकम् | यतते च ततो भूयः संसिद्धौ कुरुनन्दन
english: Thee he comes in touch with the knowledge acired in his former body and strives more than before for perfection, O Arjuna.
brief_explanation: The son of the Kurus obtains union with knowledge acquired in his former body, and this prior exertion and practice in Yoga accelerate his moral and spiritual evolution. Previous Samskaras (impressions) from thoughts and actions are revived and reenergized in the next birth, including those related to Yogic practices and meditation. These will drive the spiritual aspirant to strive more vigorously for greater spiritual experiences and higher planes of realization in the new life.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: पूर्वाभ्यासेन तेनैव ह्रियते ह्यवशोऽपि सः | जिज्ञासुरपि योगस्य शब्दब्रह्मातिवर्तते
english: By that very former practice he is borne on in spite of himself. Even he who merely wishes to know Yoga goes beyond the Brahmic word.
brief_explanation: The individual who previously practiced Yoga and subsequently falls from it is driven towards its goal due to the force of Samskaras, regardless of conscious awareness or willingness. If not overwhelmed by strong evil Karma, they will resume Yogic practices in this life with great vigor. An inquirer sparks an interest in Yoga transcends the effects of Vedic rituals and ceremonies, seeking a higher satisfaction than sensual objects.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: प्रयत्नाद्यतमानस्तु योगी संशुद्धकिल्बिषः | अनेकजन्मसंसिद्धस्ततो याति परां गतिम्
english: But the Yogi who strives with assiduity, purified of sins and perfected gradually through many births, reaches the highest goal.
brief_explanation: The Yogi, purified from sins after striving assiduously through many lives, eventually reaches the highest path towards the ultimate realization of self and attainment of supreme beatitude.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: तपस्विभ्योऽधिको योगी ज्ञानिभ्योऽपि मतोऽधिकः | कर्मिभ्यश्चाधिको योगी तस्माद्योगी भवार्जुन
english: The Yogi is thought to be superior to the ascetics and even superior to men of knowledge (obtained through the study of scriptures); he is also superior to men of action; therefore be thou a Yogi, O Arjuna.
brief_explanation: The Yogi, who attains direct knowledge of the Self through intuition or Nirvikalpa Samadhi, is superior to ascetics, the wise, and those who perform Vedic rituals. This is because their knowledge comes from austerities, scriptures, or actions, while the Yogi's knowledge is direct and unmediated. (Cf.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: योगिनामपि सर्वेषां मद्गतेनान्तरात्मना | श्रद्धावान्भजते यो मां स मे युक्ततमो मतः
english: And among all the Yogis he who, full of faith and with his inner self merged in Me, worships Me is deemed by Me to be the most devout.
brief_explanation: Among all Yogis, he who worships Me (the Absolute) is deemed most devout. The inner self merged in Me is superior to those who worship lesser gods like Vasus, Rudra, Aditya, etc. This chapter, known as Atmasamyama Yoga or Adhyatma Yoga, concludes the sixth discourse of the Bhagavad Gita, a scripture of Yoga and the dialogue between Sri Krishna and Arjuna.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: श्रीभगवानुवाच | मय्यासक्तमनाः पार्थ योगं युञ्जन्मदाश्रयः | असंशयं समग्रं मां यथा ज्ञास्यसि तच्छृणु
english: The Blessed Lord said O Arjuna, hear how you shall without doubt know Me fully, with the mind intent on Me, practising Yoga and taking refuge in Me.
brief_explanation: The Yogi practices Yoga, fixing their mind steadfastly on the Lord's lofty attributes such as omnipotence, omniscience, omnipresence, infinite love, beauty, grace, strength, mercy, inexhaustible wealth, ineffable splendor, pristine glory, and purity. Fix your mind on Me, the all-pervading one, and take refuge in Me alone to achieve full knowledge of the Self without any doubt.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: ज्ञानं तेऽहं सविज्ञानमिदं वक्ष्याम्यशेषतः | यज्ज्ञात्वा नेह भूयोऽन्यज्ज्ञातव्यमवशिष्यते
english: I shall declare to thee in full this knowledge combined with realisation, after knowing which nothing more here remains to be known.
brief_explanation: The verse refers to two types of knowledge: Jnanam, indirect knowledge from scriptures, and Vijnanam, direct Self-realization. The Lord promises Arjuna a complete understanding of the Self after knowing which there's nothing more to learn. Acquiring self-knowledge means knowing everything else as well, similar to Saunaka's inquiry to Angirasa (referenced in Bhagavad Gita 13.11).

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: मनुष्याणां सहस्रेषु कश्चिद्यतति सिद्धये | यततामपि सिद्धानां कश्चिन्मां वेत्ति तत्त्वतः
english: Among thousands of men, one perchance strives for perfection; even among those successful strivers, only one perchance knows Me in essence.
brief_explanation: The verse discusses the rarity of individuals striving for self-perfection, with those knowing the Truth in essence being particularly scarce. It compares this to the scarcity of valuable objects such as diamonds or pearls. The knowledge of the Self offers immense benefits, including immortality, eternal bliss, perennial joy, and everlasting peace, but it is challenging to attain.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: भूमिरापोऽनलो वायुः खं मनो बुद्धिरेव च | अहंकार इतीयं मे भिन्ना प्रकृतिरष्टधा
english: Earth, water, fire, air, ether, mind, intellect and egoism thus is My Nature divided eightfold.
brief_explanation: The eightfold Nature includes earth, water, fire, air, ether, mind, intellect, and egoism. These represent subtle elements that form the five gross elements. Mind corresponds to its cause, Ahamkara (egoism), while intellect represents its cause, Mahat.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: अपरेयमितस्त्वन्यां प्रकृतिं विद्धि मे पराम् | जीवभूतां महाबाहो ययेदं धार्यते जगत्
english: This is the inferior Prakriti, O mighty-armed (Arjuna); know thou as different from it My higher Prakriti (Nature), the very life-element, by which this world is upheld.
brief_explanation: The inferior Nature, as described in the previous verse, refers to the eightfold material nature that generates evil and causes bondage. In contrast, the superior Nature is the pure Self or Kshetrajna (knower of the field or Spirit) that upholds the world and sustains the universe, representing the principle of Self-consciousness.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: एतद्योनीनि भूतानि सर्वाणीत्युपधारय | अहं कृत्स्नस्य जगतः प्रभवः प्रलयस्तथा
english: Know that these two (Natures) are the womb of all beings. So I am the source and dissolution of the whole universe.
brief_explanation: The two Natures (Prakritis) are the birthplace of all beings, implying that I am the source of these Prakritis and thus the creator of the entire world. This is similar to the Brahma Sutras, which state that Brahman is the omniscient and omnipotent cause from which the universe originates, subsists, and dissolves. Just as the mind serves as both material cause and seer in dreams, Isvara functions as both the material cause of the world and its seer.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: मत्तः परतरं नान्यत्किञ्चिदस्ति धनञ्जय | मयि सर्वमिदं प्रोतं सूत्रे मणिगणा इव
english: There is nothing whatsoever higher than Me, O Arjuna. All this is strung on Me, as clusters of gems on a string.
brief_explanation: The Gita states that everything in the universe originates from the self (Me). All beings and the world are like gems strung on a thread, with the Lord as the thread, not the cause. Nothing is higher than the self, as it encompasses all.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: रसोऽहमप्सु कौन्तेय प्रभास्मि शशिसूर्ययोः | प्रणवः सर्ववेदेषु शब्दः खे पौरुषं नृषु
english: I am the sapidity in water, O Arjuna; I am the light in the moon and the sun; I am the syllable Om in all the Vedas, sound in ether and virility in men.
brief_explanation: The term "rasah" refers to the sapidity present in all things, including water. The sun, moon, syllable Om, and all Vedas are part of the Lord's manifestations, as are light, virility, and men. This interconnectedness is compared to a cloth woven from various threads.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: पुण्यो गन्धः पृथिव्यां च तेजश्चास्मि विभावसौ | जीवनं सर्वभूतेषु तपश्चास्मि तपस्विषु
english: I am the sweet fragrance in the earth and the brilliance in the fire, the life in all beings, and I am the austerity in ascetics.
brief_explanation: Krishna is the fragrance in the earth, the brilliance in fire, life in all beings, and austerity among ascetics. He is the source of everything, providing support and power for their existence and self-control.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: बीजं मां सर्वभूतानां विद्धि पार्थ सनातनम् | बुद्धिर्बुद्धिमतामस्मि तेजस्तेजस्विनामहम्
english: Know Me, O Arjuna, as the eternal seed of all beings; I am the intelligence of the intelligent; the splendour of the splendid objects am I.
brief_explanation: The seed refers to a cause. In response to Arjuna's question about the seed of the Lord, the Lord states that He is the causeless cause and the primeval Being. Tejas also signifies splendour or bravery.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: बलं बलवतां चाहं कामरागविवर्जितम् | धर्माविरुद्धो भूतेषु कामोऽस्मि भरतर्षभ
english: Of the strong, I am the strength devoid of desire and attachment, and in (all) beings, I am the desire unopposed to Dharma, O Arjuna.
brief_explanation: The strength referred to is necessary for the basic survival of the body, distinct from the strength that fosters desires and attachments towards sensual objects, common among worldly individuals. In contrast, I am the desire that aligns with the scriptures' teachings or duty-based code, such as moderate eating and drinking, essential for bodily sustenance and Yoga practice.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: ये चैव सात्त्विका भावा राजसास्तामसाश्च ये | मत्त एवेति तान्विद्धि न त्वहं तेषु ते मयि
english: Whatever beings (and objects) that are pure, active and inert, know that they proceed from Me. They are in Me, yet I am not in them.
brief_explanation: The Bhagavad Gita describes a world of three natures: Sattvic (pure), Rajasic (active), and Tamasic (inert). Each object's predominant nature determines its characteristics. For instance, Sattva is dominant in gods, sages, milk, and green gram; Rajas in Gandharvas, kings, warriors, and chillies; and Tamas in demons, Sudras, garlic, onion, and meat.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: त्रिभिर्गुणमयैर्भावैरेभिः सर्वमिदं जगत् | मोहितं नाभिजानाति मामेभ्यः परमव्ययम्
english: Deluded by these Natures (states or things) composed of the three alities of Nature all this world does not know Me as distinct from them and immutable.
brief_explanation: Persons in this world are deluded by three natural alities, or Maya. Attachment, affection, and infatuated love are all forms of these alities. Due to this delusion, they are unable to break free from worldly ties and turn their minds towards the Supreme Soul, the Lord of the three alities.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: दैवी ह्येषा गुणमयी मम माया दुरत्यया | मामेव ये प्रपद्यन्ते मायामेतां तरन्ति ते
english: Verily, this divine illusion of Mine, made up of the (three) alities (of Nature) is difficult to cross over; those who take refuge in Me alone, cross over this illusion.
brief_explanation: Maya, the illusory power, is the causal body of Isvara, the Lord. It's made up of the three qualities: Sattva, Rajas, and Tamas. Those who completely devote themselves to Isvara, renouncing formal religion, can cross over this illusion that deceives all beings, attaining liberation or Moksha.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: न मां दुष्कृतिनो मूढाः प्रपद्यन्ते नराधमाः | माययापहृतज्ञाना आसुरं भावमाश्रिताः
english: The evil-doers and the deluded who are the lowest of men do not seek Me; they whose knowledge is destroyed by illusion follow the ways of demons.
brief_explanation: Evildoers, deluded individuals, and those who identify with the material body are seeking solace in worldly pleasures instead of turning to the divine Self. They are deprived of true knowledge, acting against righteousness and indulging in atrocious actions such as murder, theft, and false speech. Such individuals follow demonic ways and worship their physical bodies, leading to further ignorance.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: चतुर्विधा भजन्ते मां जनाः सुकृतिनोऽर्जुन | आर्तो जिज्ञासुरर्थार्थी ज्ञानी च भरतर्षभ
english: Four kinds of virtuous men worship Me, O Arjuna, and they are the distressed, the seekr of knowledge, the seekr of wealth and the wise, O lord of the Bharatas.
brief_explanation: The four types of worshippers are: the distressed, seeker of knowledge, seeker of wealth, and the wise. Examples of the distressed include those suffering from diseases or natural disasters. Janaka and Uddhava were seekers of knowledge, while Sugriva, Vibhishana, Upamanyu, and Dhruva were seekers of wealth.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: तेषां ज्ञानी नित्ययुक्त एकभक्तिर्विशिष्यते | प्रियो हि ज्ञानिनोऽत्यर्थमहं स च मम प्रियः
english: Of them the wise, ever steadfast and devoted to the One, excels (is the best); for I am exceedingly dear to the wise and he is dear to Me.
brief_explanation: The Jnani Bhakta, characterized by unswerving devotion to the Supreme Being, transcends all religions and creeds. Being constantly harmonized with the One, they are considered superior among devotees. As the wise man is my very Self, they hold a special affection for me, similar to the love everyone has for their own self.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: उदाराः सर्व एवैते ज्ञानी त्वात्मैव मे मतम् | आस्थितः स हि युक्तात्मा मामेवानुत्तमां गतिम्
english: Noble indeed are all these; but I deem the wise man as My very Self; for, steadfast in mind he is established in Me alone as the supreme goal.
brief_explanation: The other three kinds of devotees are dear to the Lord, but the wise man is particularly dear due to his steadfast mind fixed on Brahman. He seeks only the supreme goal and practices Ahamgraha Upasana, identifying himself with the Supreme Self. Thus, a wise man is considered as the Lord's own Self.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: बहूनां जन्मनामन्ते ज्ञानवान्मां प्रपद्यते | वासुदेवः सर्वमिति स महात्मा सुदुर्लभः
english: At the end of many births the wise man comes to Me, realising that all this is Vaasudeva (the innermost Self); such a great soul (Mahatma) is very hard to find.
brief_explanation: The term "Vaasudeva" refers to Lord Krishna, being the son of Vasudeva. He is the all-pervading Brahman. Through Yogic practices, selfless service, devotion, and constant meditation in numerous births, an individual may eventually attain the inner Self and recognize all as Vaasudeva.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: कामैस्तैस्तैर्हृतज्ञानाः प्रपद्यन्तेऽन्यदेवताः | तं तं नियममास्थाय प्रकृत्या नियताः स्वया
english: Those whose wisdom has been rent away by this or that desire, go to other gods, following this or that rite, led by their own nature.
brief_explanation: Those who are driven by desires for wealth, children, or minor Siddhis are often devoid of discernment. They may seek the favor of other gods like Indra, Mitra, Varuna, and so on, influenced by their nature or past Samskaras. These individuals follow certain rites to please these lower deities as dictated by their own natures.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: यो यो यां यां तनुं भक्तः श्रद्धयार्चितुमिच्छति | तस्य तस्याचलां श्रद्धां तामेव विदधाम्यहम्
english: Whatsoever form any devotee desires to worship with faith that (same) faith of his I make firm and unflinching.
brief_explanation: The text refers to a devotee who worships lesser divinities with unwavering faith. The Lord, as the indweller of all beings, makes this steadfast faith of the devotee, which originates from their past life's samskaras, firm and unshaken. (This is similar to the concepts in IV.11, IX.22, and IX.23.)

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: स तया श्रद्धया युक्तस्तस्याराधनमीहते | लभते च ततः कामान्मयैव विहितान्हि तान्
english: Endowed with that faith, he engages in the worship of that (form) and from it he obtains his desire, these being verily ordained by Me (alone).
brief_explanation: The devotee who worships lesser gods obtains the objects of their desires, which are ordained by the Lord. This is because the Lord knows the relation between actions and their rewards, being the Inner Ruler of all beings. Unfortunately, undiscriminating individuals focus on finite rewards, lacking power of enquiry or right understanding.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: अन्तवत्तु फलं तेषां तद्भवत्यल्पमेधसाम् | देवान्देवयजो यान्ति मद्भक्ता यान्ति मामपि
english: Verily the reward (fruit) that accrues to those men of small intelligence is finite. The worshippers of the gods go to them, but My devotees come to Me.
brief_explanation: The exertion in both kinds of worship is equal, but people often neglect seeking infinite rewards through the Supreme Being for temporary benefits. Worshippers of minor deities with limited understanding receive transient and perishable rewards. Only liberation provides eternal bliss and peace.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: अव्यक्तं व्यक्तिमापन्नं मन्यन्ते मामबुद्धयः | परं भावमजानन्तो ममाव्ययमनुत्तमम्
english: The foolish think of Me, the Unmanifest, as having manifestation, knowing not My higher, immutable and most excellent nature.
brief_explanation: The foolish consider Krishna as an ordinary mortal, assuming he came from the unmanifested state due to Karma of previous life. They are unaware of his higher, immutable, most excellent nature beyond manifestation, being self-existent, eternal, beginningless, endless, birthless, deathless, changeless, infinite and unmanifest.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: नाहं प्रकाशः सर्वस्य योगमायासमावृतः | मूढोऽयं नाभिजानाति लोको मामजमव्ययम्
english: I am not manifest to all (as I am) veiled by the Yoga-Maya. This deluded world does not know Me, the unborn and imperishable.
brief_explanation: The text explains that I am not visible to everyone, but to my devotees who have taken refuge in me alone.
