This is due to YogaMaya, the creative illusion of Nature that veils the understanding of worldly-minded people. However, YogaMaya is under the perfect control of the Lord and cannot obstruct his knowledge or deceive him.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: वेदाहं समतीतानि वर्तमानानि चार्जुन | भविष्याणि च भूतानि मां तु वेद न कश्चन
english: I know, O Arjuna, the beings of the past, the present and the future, but no one knows Me.
brief_explanation: The deluded by Nature's three alities do not comprehend the true nature of the Lord. Lacking such knowledge, they fail to recognize Him. Conversely, the Lord, possessing omniscience, is aware of past, present, and future beings.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: इच्छाद्वेषसमुत्थेन द्वन्द्वमोहेन भारत | सर्वभूतानि सम्मोहं सर्गे यान्ति परन्तप
english: By the delusion of the pairs of opposites arising from desire and aversion, O Bharata, all beings are subject to delusion at birth, O Parantapa.
brief_explanation: Desire and aversion, also known as the pairs of opposites, cause delusion in all beings, hindering the realization of one's true Self. Raga (attraction) and Dvesha (repulsion) induce confusion, preventing the adoration of the Self and impairing discrimination, causing the mind to crave for constant change due to its fluctuation.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: येषां त्वन्तगतं पापं जनानां पुण्यकर्मणाम् | ते द्वन्द्वमोहनिर्मुक्ता भजन्ते मां दृढव्रताः
english: But those men of virtuous deeds whose sins have come to an end, and who are freed from the delusion of the pairs of opposites, worship Me, steadfast in their vows.
brief_explanation: The verse (7.28) refers to those who have purified their hearts through good deeds, becoming free from the delusion of dualities and worshiping the Self with unwavering resolve. According to Sivananda's commentary, forgetting one's identity with the Supreme Soul is considered the greatest sin, as is perceiving difference or considering the body as the self. Steadfast in vows signifies having a firm conviction that Brahman is the only reality and seeking self-realization without wavering from this resolve.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: जरामरणमोक्षाय मामाश्रित्य यतन्ति ये | ते ब्रह्म तद्विदुः कृत्स्नमध्यात्मं कर्म चाखिलम्
english: Those who strive for liberation from old age and death, taking refuge in Me, realise in full ï1thatï1 Brahman, the whole knowledge of the Self and all action.
brief_explanation: The individuals who strive, having taken refuge in Me (God), attain the full knowledge of the Self or perfect knowledge of Brahman, realizing that all is Vaasudeva and ultimately Brahman. This enlightenment leads to their liberation from old age and death.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: साधिभूताधिदैवं मां साधियज्ञं च ये विदुः | प्रयाणकालेऽपि च मां ते विदुर्युक्तचेतसः
english: Those who know Me with the Adhibhuta (pertaining to the elements), Adhidaiva (pertaining to the gods) and the Adhiyajna (pertaining to the sacrifice) know Me even at the time of death, steadfast in mind.
brief_explanation: They who maintain a steady mind, recognizing Me as the knowledge in physical (Adhibhuta), celestial (Adhidaiva), and sacrificial (Adhiyajna) planes, continue to remember Me at the time of death. Even at this crucial moment, those who know Me in this manner are unaffected by death and retain consciousness of Me. Those who worship Me with this understanding, recognize Me during their final moments.

speaker: Arjuna
sanskrit: अर्जुन उवाच | किं तद् ब्रह्म किमध्यात्मं किं कर्म पुरुषोत्तम | अधिभूतं च किं प्रोक्तमधिदैवं किमुच्यते
english: Swami Sivananda did not comment on this sloka
brief_explanation: Commentary on the sloka is not provided in the Sivananda edition.

speaker: Unknown
sanskrit: अधियज्ञः कथं कोऽत्र देहेऽस्मिन्मधुसूदन | प्रयाणकाले च कथं ज्ञेयोऽसि नियतात्मभिः
english: Who and how is Adhiyajna here in this body, O destroyer of Madhu (Krishna)? And how at the time of death, art Thou to be known by the self-controlled?
brief_explanation: Adhiyajna refers to that which is associated with Yajnas or Vedic rituals. It can be either the Para Brahman or a specific deity, and it may or may not be the same form as the Lord. At the time of death, the self-controlled individual can know Adhiyajna, demonstrating the Lord's mercy and omniscience.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: श्रीभगवानुवाच | अक्षरं ब्रह्म परमं स्वभावोऽध्यात्ममुच्यते | भूतभावोद्भवकरो विसर्गः कर्मसंज्ञितः
english: The Blessed Lord said Brahman is the Imperishable, the Supreme; Its essential nature is called Self-knowledge; the offering (to the gods) which causes existence and manifestation of beings and which also sustains them is called action.
brief_explanation: Brahman, the Supreme Being, is referred to as Akshara, meaning imperishable, eternal, and unchanging. Its nature (Svabhava) is Adhyatma, or self-knowledge. The essence of all beings that originate and grow is rooted in it.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: अधिभूतं क्षरो भावः पुरुषश्चाधिदैवतम् | अधियज्ञोऽहमेवात्र देहे देहभृतां वर
english: Adhibhuta (knowledge of the elements) pertains to My perishable Nature and the Purusha or the Soul is the Adhidaiva; I alone am the Adhiyajna here in this body, O best among the embodied (men).
brief_explanation: The Adhibhuta refers to the perishable, changing universe of material objects, including the five elements and everything born from them. Adhidaiva is the universal soul or sustainer within the body, serving as the witnessing consciousness. Adhiyajna is the presiding deity in all acts of sacrifice, identified with Vishnu, who resides within the body, overseeing all sacrificial acts performed by it.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: अन्तकाले च मामेव स्मरन्मुक्त्वा कलेवरम् | यः प्रयाति स मद्भावं याति नास्त्यत्र संशयः
english: And whosoever, leaving the body, goes forth remembering Me alone, at the time of death, he attains My Being: there is no doubt about this.
brief_explanation: Sivananda does not provide a specific commentary on Bhagavad Gita verse 8.5 (Chapter 8, Verse 5). The verse reads: "A person who neither hates those who are enemies nor honors those who are friends, but treats friends and enemies equally, attains peace from the self." Sivananda's focus in this chapter is on meditation and yoga, not on commenting specifically on individual verses.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: यं यं वापि स्मरन्भावं त्यजत्यन्ते कलेवरम् | तं तमेवैति कौन्तेय सदा तद्भावभावितः
english: Whosoever at the end leaves the body, thinking of any being, to that being only does he go, O son of Kunti (Arjuna), because of his constant thought of that being.
brief_explanation: The last thoughts determine one's next birth, as the predominant idea in life occupies the mind at death. The force of past actions (Samskaras) causes remembrance of them at death. Those who constantly remember their tutelary deity become identical with that deity, like the caterpillar becoming a wasp.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: तस्मात्सर्वेषु कालेषु मामनुस्मर युध्य च | मय्यर्पितमनोबुद्धिर्मामेवैष्यस्यसंशयः (orसंशयम्)
english: Therefore at all times remember Me only and fight. With mind and intellect fixed (or absorbed) in Me, thou shalt doubtessly come to Me alone.
brief_explanation: The passage suggests that one should dedicate their entire mental faculties to the Lord, performing duties according to their caste and order of life (Upalakshanas). This is done by fighting (performing one's duties) with a mind and intellect fixed on the Lord. The ultimate goal is to come to the Lord alone, doubtless.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: अभ्यासयोगयुक्तेन चेतसा नान्यगामिना | परमं पुरुषं दिव्यं याति पार्थानुचिन्तयन्
english: With the mind not moving towards any other thing, made steadfast by the method of habitual meditation, and constantly meditating, one goes to the Supreme Person, the Resplendent, O Arjuna.
brief_explanation: The practice of meditation, Abhyasa, involves constant repetition of thoughts about God, leading to a continuous flow of thoughts about the Self or the Absolute alone. This practice is Yoga and leads to Nirvikalpa Samadhi. Meditating regularly will help one attain the Supreme Purusha, the resplendent Being within the solar orb.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: कविं पुराणमनुशासितार- मणोरणीयंसमनुस्मरेद्यः | सर्वस्य धातारमचिन्त्यरूप- मादित्यवर्णं तमसः परस्तात्
english: Whosoever meditates on the Omniscient, the Ancient, the Ruler (of the whole world), minuter than an atom, the supporter of all, of inconceivable form, effulgent like the sun and beyond the darkness of ignorance.
brief_explanation: The sage refers to the omniscient Lord, who governs the world and dispenses actions' fruits for individual souls. His form is beyond comprehension, radiant like the sun, and transcends darkness.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: प्रयाणकाले मनसाऽचलेन भक्त्या युक्तो योगबलेन चैव | भ्रुवोर्मध्ये प्राणमावेश्य सम्यक् स तं परं पुरुषमुपैति दिव्यम्
english: At the time of death, with unshaken mind, endowed with devotio, by the power of Yoga, fixing the whole life-breath in the middle of the two eyrows, he reaches that resplendent Supreme Person.
brief_explanation: The yogi, through constant practice, gains inner strength and focus. His mind becomes unshaken due to concentration and meditation on lower Chakras - Muladhara, Svadhishthana, and Manipura. Further concentration is on the heart lotus (Anahata Chakra).

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: यदक्षरं वेदविदो वदन्ति विशन्ति यद्यतयो वीतरागाः | यदिच्छन्तो ब्रह्मचर्यं चरन्ति तत्ते पदं संग्रहेण प्रवक्ष्ये
english: That which is declared Imperishable by those who know the Vedas, that which the self-controlled (ascetics or Sannyasins) and passion-free enter, that desiring which celibacy is practised that goal I will declare to thee in brief.
brief_explanation: The Supreme Being, symbolized by the sacred monosyllable Om or Pranava, is the highest goal for man. This idea is shared in the Kathopanishad where Yama states that it is the goal all Vedas speak of, all penances proclaim, and is pursued through celibacy (Brahma-charyam). The Pranava is considered a means for realizing the Supreme Self for persons with dull or middling intellects.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: सर्वद्वाराणि संयम्य मनो हृदि निरुध्य च | मूध्न्यार्धायात्मनः प्राणमास्थितो योगधारणाम्
english: Having closed all the gates, confined the mind in the heart and fixed the life-breath in the head, engaged in the practice of concentration.
brief_explanation: The 'gates' refer to the senses of knowledge. Controlling them involves Pratyahara, which is the withdrawal of consciousness from these senses. Even with controlled senses, the mind may still dwell on sensual objects.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: ओमित्येकाक्षरं ब्रह्म व्याहरन्मामनुस्मरन् | यः प्रयाति त्यजन्देहं स याति परमां गतिम्
english: Uttering the one-syllabled Om the Brahman and remembering Me, he who departs, leaving the body, attains to the Supreme Goal.
brief_explanation: The yogi who controls thoughts ascends through the Sushumna, a subtle psychic nerve channel from the heart to the crown of the head. By uttering 'Om' and focusing on the self, he leaves the body and attains the supreme goal.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: अनन्यचेताः सततं यो मां स्मरति नित्यशः | तस्याहं सुलभः पार्थ नित्ययुक्तस्य योगिनः
english: I am easily attainable by that ever-steadfast Yogi who constantly and daily remembers Me (for a long time), not thinking of anything else (with a single mind or one-pointed mind), O Partha (Arjuna).
brief_explanation: The verse describes a Yogi who constantly and daily remembers Me (God), with no attachment to any other object, as easily attainable. This unwavering focus is maintained throughout the Yogi's life, not just for brief periods.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: मामुपेत्य पुनर्जन्म दुःखालयमशाश्वतम् | नाप्नुवन्ति महात्मानः संसिद्धिं परमां गताः
english: Having attained Me these great souls do not again take birth (here) which is the place of pain and is non-eternal: they have reached the highest perfection (liberation).
brief_explanation: The home of pain is birth, described in detail in Garbhopanishad. Mahatmas, free from Rajas and Tamas, attain KramaMukti, a gradual liberation leading to Brahmaloka or Satyaloka, enjoying divine wealth, then Kaivalya Moksha during cosmic dissolution. Once attaining Moksha, Mahatmas do not reincarnate, while others return to the world of pain (birth).

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: आब्रह्मभुवनाल्लोकाः पुनरावर्तिनोऽर्जुन | मामुपेत्य तु कौन्तेय पुनर्जन्म न विद्यते
english: (All) the worlds including the world of Brahma are subject to return again, O Arjuna; but he who reaches Me, O son of Kunti, has no rirth.
brief_explanation: Devotees practicing Daharopasana or reaching Brahmaloka through the path of the gods (Devayana) attain gradual liberation and will not reincarnate. However, those using Panchagni Vidya in Brahmaloka will experience life there temporarily and return to this world. All worlds are subject to return as they are limited by time.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: सहस्रयुगपर्यन्तमहर्यद् ब्रह्मणो विदुः | रात्रिं युगसहस्रान्तां तेऽहोरात्रविदो जनाः
english: Those people who know the day of Brahma which is of a duration of a thousand Yugas (ages) and the night which is also of a thousand Yugas duration, they know day and night.
brief_explanation: The term "day" refers to the evolution or manifestation of the universe, while "night" signifies its involution or Pralaya. Both are transient, including Brahma's world, which lasts for a thousand Yugas (ages). Those who can perceive day and night throughout Brahma's day and night are considered to truly understand the concept of time.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: अव्यक्ताद् व्यक्तयः सर्वाः प्रभवन्त्यहरागमे | रात्र्यागमे प्रलीयन्ते तत्रैवाव्यक्तसंज्ञके
english: From the Unmanifested all the manifested (worlds) proceed at the coming of the 'day'; at the coming of the 'night' they dissolve verily into ï1thatï1 alone which is called the Unmanifested.
brief_explanation: The unmanifested, or Avyakta, is the source from which all manifestations arise during the coming of the day. Conversely, during the cosmic night, all manifestations dissolve and merge back into the Unmanifested. This cycle reflects the commencement of creation and dissolution mentioned in Bhagavad Gita IX.7-8.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: भूतग्रामः स एवायं भूत्वा भूत्वा प्रलीयते | रात्र्यागमेऽवशः पार्थ प्रभवत्यहरागमे
english: This same multitude of beings, being born again and again, is dissolved, helplessly, O Arjuna (into the Unmanifested) at the coming of the night and comes forth at the coming of the day.
brief_explanation: The commentary explains that ignorance, desire, and action create a cycle of rebirth due to the individual's pursuit of desires. This cycle causes sorrow, misery, and pain as one is bound to Samsara (transmigration). The Lord states that all creatures involuntarily come into being again and dissolve based on their actions caused by desire born from ignorance.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: परस्तस्मात्तु भावोऽन्योऽव्यक्तोऽव्यक्तात्सनातनः | यः स सर्वेषु भूतेषु नश्यत्सु न विनश्यति
english: But verily there exists, higher than this Unmanifested, another unmanifested Eternal, which is not destroyed when all beings are destroyed.
brief_explanation: The Para Brahman, which is eternal and distinct from the unmanifested, is another form of higher existence. Unlike other beings that get destroyed when annihilated, it remains unaffected even when all other beings cease to exist. It is superior to both the Cosmic Creative Intelligence (Hiranyagarbha) and the Unmanifested Nature because it serves as their cause.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: अव्यक्तोऽक्षर इत्युक्तस्तमाहुः परमां गतिम् | यं प्राप्य न निवर्तन्ते तद्धाम परमं मम
english: What is called the Unmanifested and the Imperishable, That they say is the highest goal. They who reach It do not return (to this Samsara). That is My highest abode (place or state).
brief_explanation: Para Brahman, unperceivable by senses, is referred to as the Unmanifested and Imperishable. It pervades and interpenetrates all. The highest Goal, it surpasses any other state or region.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: पुरुषः स परः पार्थ भक्त्या लभ्यस्त्वनन्यया | यस्यान्तःस्थानि भूतानि येन सर्वमिदं ततम्
english: That highest Purusha, O Arjuna, is attainable by unswerving devotion to Him alone within Whom all beings dwell and by Whom all this is pervaded.
brief_explanation: The Purusha, being the supreme cause, contains all beings within itself, similar to a pot residing in clay. All aspects of the universe are pervaded by this high entity that is unattainable without exclusive devotion (unswerving). Sri Sankara explains exclusive devotion as Jnana or knowledge of the Self.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: यत्र काले त्वनावृत्तिमावृत्तिं चैव योगिनः | प्रयाता यान्ति तं कालं वक्ष्यामि भरतर्षभ
english: Now I will tell thee, O chief of Bharatas, the times departing at which the Yogis will return or not return.
brief_explanation: The passage describes two times for Yogis: non-return (anavritti) and return (avritti). If a Yogi leaves the body in anavritti, they will not be reborn; if they die in avritti, they will be reborn. This refers to when Yogis depart their bodies, and the specific times for these occurrences is explained further.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: अग्निर्जोतिरहः शुक्लः षण्मासा उत्तरायणम् | तत्र प्रयाता गच्छन्ति ब्रह्म ब्रह्मविदो जनाः
english: Fire, light daytime, the bright fortnight, the six months of the northern path of the sun (the northern solstice) departing then (by these) men who know Brahman go to Brahman.
brief_explanation: The UttaraMarga or Devayana, the northern path of light, is where Yogis go towards Brahman for salvation. This path leads through realms associated with deities such as Agni (fire), Vayu (air), Varuna (rain), Indra (king of gods), and Prajapati (Creator) before reaching Brahman. The six-month period from the northern solstice, often considered a better time for death, is part of this path.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: धूमो रात्रिस्तथा कृष्णः षण्मासा दक्षिणायनम् | तत्र चान्द्रमसं ज्योतिर्योगी प्राप्य निवर्तते
english: Attaining to the lunar light by smoke, night time, the dark fortnight also, the six months of the southern path of the sun (the southern solstice), the Yogi returns.
brief_explanation: The Pitriyana, or path of darkness, refers to a cycle leading to rebirth. This path is associated with sacrifices and charitable acts driven by reward expectation, guiding individuals towards the Chandraloka but returning them to earth when Karmic fruits are spent. Smoke, night, dark fortnight, six months of southern solstice symbolize increasing levels of ignorance, attachment, and passion on this path, shrouded in darkness due to ignorance.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: शुक्लकृष्णे गती ह्येते जगतः शाश्वते मते | एकया यात्यनावृत्तिमन्ययावर्तते पुनः
english: The bright and the dark paths of the world are verily thought to be eternal; by the one (the bright path) a man goes not to return and by the other (the dark path) he returns.
brief_explanation: The bright path refers to the path for devotees leading towards the world of gods, while the dark path is associated with those performing rituals with rewards in mind. These paths are not universal and are specific to their respective paths (devotion or rituals). They are as eternal as the cycle of existence (Samsara).

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: नैते सृती पार्थ जानन्योगी मुह्यति कश्चन | तस्मात्सर्वेषु कालेषु योगयुक्तो भवार्जुन
english: Knowing these paths, O Arjuna, no Yogi is deluded; therefore at all times be steadfast in Yoga.
brief_explanation: A Yogi who understands the nature of the two paths (of light and darkness) remains undeluded. Knowing the consequences they lead to, he navigates towards Moksha (gradual liberation) and away from Samsara (the world of birth and death). This knowledge serves as a guide for the Yogi, helping him stay steadfast in Yoga.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: वेदेषु यज्ञेषु तपःसु चैव दानेषु यत्पुण्यफलं प्रदिष्टम् | अत्येति तत्सर्वमिदं विदित्वा योगी परं स्थानमुपैति चाद्यम्
english: Whatever fruit of merit is declared (in the scriptures) to accrue from (the study of) the Vedas, (the performance of) sacrifices, (the practice of) austerities, and gifts beyond all this goes the Yogi, having known this; and he attains to the Supreme Primeval (first or ancient) Abode.
brief_explanation: The verse describes the supreme glory of yoga, stating that a Yogi who understands and follows Lord Krishna's teachings beyond study in Vedas, performance of sacrifices, practice of austerities, and gifts attains the primeval abode of Brahman, which is ancient or first. Having known this, one ends the eighth discourse in the Bhagavad Gita, titled "The Yoga of the Imperishable Brahman."

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: श्रीभगवानुवाच | इदं तु ते गुह्यतमं प्रवक्ष्याम्यनसूयवे | ज्ञानं विज्ञानसहितं यज्ज्ञात्वा मोक्ष्यसेऽशुभात्
english: The Blessed Lord said I shall now declare to thee who does not cavil, the greatest secret, the knowledge combined with experience (Self-realisation). Having known this thou shalt be free evil.
brief_explanation: Knowledge of the Self, either theoretical or intuitive, is the greatest secret that Lord Krishna will declare to Arjuna. This knowledge, when realized, leads to liberation from evil. The knowledge of the Self can only be attained through direct experience or spiritual intuition and not merely through words.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: राजविद्या राजगुह्यं पवित्रमिदमुत्तमम् | प्रत्यक्षावगमं धर्म्यं सुसुखं कर्तुमव्ययम्
english: This is the kingl science, the kingly secret, the supreme purifier, realisable by direct intuitional knowledge, according to righteousness, very easy to perform and imperishable.
brief_explanation: The Bhagavad Gita praises the knowledge of Brahman, referring to it as the "king of sciences," the "kingly secret," and the "supreme purifier." This knowledge, which can be directly realized by intuition, is considered the highest and most splendid of all sciences. It is in accord with righteousness, very easy to perform, and imperishable. The acquisition of this knowledge leads to the destruction of Avidya (ignorance) and all sins accumulated over numerous births.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: अश्रद्दधानाः पुरुषा धर्मस्यास्य परन्तप | अप्राप्य मां निवर्तन्ते मृत्युसंसारवर्त्मनि
english: Those who have no faith in this Dharma (knowledge of the Self), O Parantapa (Arjuna), return to the path of this world of death without attaining Me.
brief_explanation: People without faith return to the path of death as they lack the right means for attaining the knowledge of the Self, which is the highest and most beneficial. Faith is unshakable inner conviction in the supreme purifying power of this knowledge. The Lord praises this knowledge in both positive and negative terms: the benefits in the first two verses (Vidhi Mukhastuti) and the disastrous effects of not attaining it in the third verse (Nishedha Mukhastuti).

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: मया ततमिदं सर्वं जगदव्यक्तमूर्तिना | मत्स्थानि सर्वभूतानि न चाहं तेष्ववस्थितः
english: All this world is pervaded by Me in My unmanifest aspect; all beings exist in Me, but I do not dwell in them.
brief_explanation: The Supreme Unmanifested Being, Avyaktamurti, pervades all beings and the world, but does not have an independent existence within them. Instead, it is the support for everything, existing beyond any material object or form. It appears that beings dwell in Brahman, but this is an illusion; when ignorance disappears, so will the idea of their existence.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: न च मत्स्थानि भूतानि पश्य मे योगमैश्वरम् | भूतभृन्न च भूतस्थो ममात्मा भूतभावनः
english: Nor do beings exist in Me (in reality); behold My divine Yoga, supporting all beings, but not dwelling in them, is My Self, the efficient cause of beings.
brief_explanation: Brahman, the Self, has no direct connection with objects due to its subtle and formless nature, making it unattached. It supports all beings but does not dwell within them as there is no real link between matter and Spirit. This is a mystical concept, similar to the dreamer having no connection with dream objects or ether with a vessel.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: यथाकाशस्थितो नित्यं वायुः सर्वत्रगो महान् | तथा सर्वाणि भूतानि मत्स्थानीत्युपधारय
english: As the mighty wind, moving everywhere, rests always in the ether, even so, know thou that all beings rest in Me.
brief_explanation: The verse presents an illustration of how all beings, like air that pervades everywhere and is great, rest in Brahman without any attachment or contact. The relationship between Brahman and the objects of the universe is not Samyoga (direct contact), Samavaya (relationship through attributes), or Tadatmya Sambandha (oneness of qualities). Instead, it's a Kalpita Sambandha (superimposition) where objects exist in name only, and are not truly rooted or dwelling in Brahman.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: सर्वभूतानि कौन्तेय प्रकृतिं यान्ति मामिकाम् | कल्पक्षये पुनस्तानि कल्पादौ विसृजाम्यहम्
english: All beings, O Arjuna, go into My Nature at the end of a Kalpa; I send them forth again at the beginning of (the next) Kalpa.
brief_explanation: The verse 9.7 suggests that all beings return to Nature, known as Prakriti, composed of Sattva, Rajas, and Tamas during the end of a Kalpa (period of dissolution). Similar to how grass grows from the earth and disappears back into it, or dreams arise from the mind and cease when one awakes, beings are sent forth by I (God) and return to Nature at the end of each cycle. This cycle of dissolution and creation is repeated during the beginning of a new Kalpa.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: प्रकृतिं स्वामवष्टभ्य विसृजामि पुनः पुनः | भूतग्राममिमं कृत्स्नमवशं प्रकृतेर्वशात्
english: Animating My Nature, I again and again send forth all this multitude of beings, helpless by the force of the Nature.
brief_explanation: The Lord animates Nature, projecting the entire multitude of beings again and again. He is in control as they arise from dormancy after universal dissolution. Prakriti refers to the five afflictions: ignorance, egoism, likes, dislikes, and clinging to earthly life.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: न च मां तानि कर्माणि निबध्नन्ति धनञ्जय | उदासीनवदासीनमसक्तं तेषु कर्मसु
english: These acts do not bind Me, O Arjuna, sitting like one indifferent, unattached to those acts.
brief_explanation: The acts referred to are creation and dissolution of the universe. The speaker, as the only cause, remains indifferent and unattached in these actions, without feeling of agency or attachment to their fruits. This detachment results in freedom from good and evil actions, much like a neutral referee who is unaffected by the game's outcome.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: मयाध्यक्षेण प्रकृतिः सूयते सचराचरम् | हेतुनानेन कौन्तेय जगद्विपरिवर्तते
english: Under Me as supervisor, Nature produces the moving and the unmoving; because of this, O Arjuna, the world revolves.
brief_explanation: The Lord acts as a supervisor, not the doer, in the creation of the moving and unmoving world. Nature, with the help of the Lord's presence, initiates all actions. The primary cause of this creation is nature itself, despite the sun or Lord being indirectly involved.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: अवजानन्ति मां मूढा मानुषीं तनुमाश्रितम् | परं भावमजानन्तो मम भूतमहेश्वरम्
english: Fools disregard Me, clad in human form, not knowing My higher Being as the great Lord of (all) beings.
brief_explanation: Fools despise the divine nature of Me, just as someone with jaundice sees everything yellow. Similarly, those suffering from fever find milk bitter like neem. Those who see Me through physical eyes cannot comprehend My higher Self.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: मोघाशा मोघकर्माणो मोघज्ञाना विचेतसः | राक्षसीमासुरीं चैव प्रकृतिं मोहिनीं श्रिताः
english: Of vain hopes, of vain actions, of vain knowledge and senseless, they verily are possessed of the deceitful nature of demons and undivine beings.
brief_explanation: Vain hopes and actions arise from running after transient objects, ignoring the eternal. Vain knowledge comes from ignoring the Self that dwells within, instead focusing solely on the external human body. Those who neglect their own Self often commit atrocious crimes and partake in the nature of the demonic.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: महात्मानस्तु मां पार्थ दैवीं प्रकृतिमाश्रिताः | भजन्त्यनन्यमनसो ज्ञात्वा भूतादिमव्ययम्
english: But the great souls, O Arjuna, partaking of My divine nature, worship Me with a single mind (with the mind devoted to nothing else), knowing Me as the imperishable source of beings.
brief_explanation: The high-souled ones, those with divine or Sattvic nature, possess self-restraint, mercy, faith, and purity. Knowing Me to be the imperishable source of all beings, they worship Me with a mind devoted to nothing else. I dwell in their pure minds, making them my special abode.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: सततं कीर्तयन्तो मां यतन्तश्च दृढव्रताः | नमस्यन्तश्च मां भक्त्या नित्ययुक्ता उपासते
english: Always glorifying Me, striving,firm in vows, prostrating themselves before Me, they worship Me with devotion always steadfast.
brief_explanation: These great souls continually glorify Me, engage in spiritual practices such as Japa (repetition of Om), study Upanishads, reflect on the attributeless Absolute (Nirguna Brahman), and cultivate virtues like patience, mercy, and tolerance. They control their senses, are firm in vows of nonviolence, truthfulness, and purity, and worship Me with devotion. As a beginner cannot directly see God, they first worship their spiritual preceptor, regarding him as God or Brahman Himself.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: ज्ञानयज्ञेन चाप्यन्ये यजन्तो मामुपासते | एकत्वेन पृथक्त्वेन बहुधा विश्वतोमुखम्
english: Others also sacrificing with the wisdom-sacrifice worship Me, the All-faced, as one, as distinct, and as manifold.
brief_explanation: The others also engage in sacrifices through wisdom, perceiving the Self in all and worshiping Me, the One and the manifold, present everywhere. They consider all visible forms as manifestations of God, regarding all sounds they hear as divine names. Offerings are made to the Lord in various ways, with some embracing the Monistic view (identifying themselves with the Truth) and others adhering to the Dualistic School (distinguishing between self and the Lord).

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: अहं क्रतुरहं यज्ञः स्वधाहमहमौषधम् | मन्त्रोऽहमहमेवाज्यमहमग्निरहं हुतम्
english: I am the Kratu; I am the Yajna; I am the offering (food) to the manes; I am the medicinal herbs and all the plants; I am the Mantra; I am also the Ghee or the melted butter; I am the fire; I am the oblation.
brief_explanation: The verse suggests that the speaker is identified with various offerings and rituals, such as sacrifices (Kratu), worships (Yajna), offerings to ancestors (Svadha), medicinal herbs and plants (Aushadham), sacred syllables (Mantra), ghee or clarified butter (Aajyam), fire (Agni), and the act of offering (Hutam).

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: पिताहमस्य जगतो माता धाता पितामहः | वेद्यं पवित्रमोंकार ऋक्साम यजुरेव च
english: I am the father of this world, the mother, the dispenser of the fruits of actions and the grandfather; the (one) thing to be known, the purifier, the sacred monosyllable (Om), and also the Rik-, the Sama-and the Yajur-Vedas.
brief_explanation: The Dispenser of the fruits of actions is the supporter or sustainer, referred to as Isvara or the Saguna Brahman, who is likened to a father. MulaPrakriti, the primordial Nature, functions as the mother. The Supreme Being, the pure Satchidananda Para Brahman (Existence-Knowledge-Bliss Absolute), serves as the grandfather.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: गतिर्भर्ता प्रभुः साक्षी निवासः शरणं सुहृत् | प्रभवः प्रलयः स्थानं निधानं बीजमव्ययम्
english: I am the goal, the supporter, the Lord, the witness, the abode, the shelter, the friend, the origin, the dissolution, the foundation, the treasure-house and the seed which is imperishable.
brief_explanation: The Gita describes: 1. I (God) am the goal, the fruit of actions. 2.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: तपाम्यहमहं वर्षं निगृह्णाम्युत्सृजामि च | अमृतं चैव मृत्युश्च सदसच्चाहमर्जुन
english: (As the sun) I give heat; I withhold and send forth the rain; I am immortality and also death, existence and non-existence, O Arjuna.
brief_explanation: The text suggests that I (Brahman) am responsible for heat and rain. During the rainy season, I send forth rain like Indra, but during the rest of the year, I withhold it. Existence (Sat) refers to the manifested world, while nonexistence (Asat) refers to the unmanifested cause, which is not nothingness but a subtle, unmanifested state.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: त्रैविद्या मां सोमपाः पूतपापा यज्ञैरिष्ट्वा स्वर्गतिं प्रार्थयन्ते | ते पुण्यमासाद्य सुरेन्द्रलोक- मश्नन्ति दिव्यान्दिवि देवभोगान्
english: The knowers of the three Vedas, the drinkers of Soma, purified of all sins, worshipping Me by sacrifices, pray for the way to heaven; they reach the holy world of the Lord of the gods and enjoy in heavn the divine pleasures of the gods.
brief_explanation: Aspirants may reach higher planes through Yoga, but can be tempted by divine pleasures offered by celestial beings, leading to false contentment and loss of spiritual progress. Those who resist these temptations and maintain strong discrimination, dispassion, self-analysis, and yearning for liberation can achieve the highest goal of life. Soma drinkers are purified from sin, and perform sacrifices like Agnistoma and Jyotistoma to worship deities such as Vasus, Rudras, and Adityas.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: ते तं भुक्त्वा स्वर्गलोकं विशालं क्षीणे पुण्ये मर्त्यलोकं विशन्ति | एवं त्रयीधर्ममनुप्रपन्ना गतागतं कामकामा लभन्ते
english: They, having enjoyed the vast heaven, enter the world of mortals when their merit is exhausted; thus abiding by the injunctions of the ï1threeï1 (Vedas) and desiring (objects of) desires, they attain to the state of going and returning.
brief_explanation: Upon exhaustion of merit, they enter the mortal world after enjoying a vast heavenly realm. Their state is one of constant coming and going, not independent. This refers to those adhering to the Dharma of the three Vedas, characterized by desires for worldly pleasures.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: अनन्याश्चिन्तयन्तो मां ये जनाः पर्युपासते | तेषां नित्याभियुक्तानां योगक्षेमं वहाम्यहम्
english: For those men who worship Me alone, thinking of no other, for those ever-united, I secure what is not already possessed and preserve what they already possess.
brief_explanation: Devotees who perceive themselves as non-separate from the Supreme Being, viewing it as their own Self, have no personal desires or concerns for gain and safety. They find eternal satisfaction and possess all divine wealth due to their communion with the Lord. Their bodies become divine, as they have fulfilled all desires through their single-minded devotion.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: येऽप्यन्यदेवता भक्ता यजन्ते श्रद्धयान्विताः | तेऽपि मामेव कौन्तेय यजन्त्यविधिपूर्वकम्
english: Even those devotees who, endowed with faith, worship other gods, worship Me alone, O Arjuna, b the wrong method.
brief_explanation: The text describes that even though other deities are worshipped, their devotion is impure and vicarious. People should recognize and worship God, who is the root of all beings and the source of all gods, in His own nature.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: अहं हि सर्वयज्ञानां भोक्ता च प्रभुरेव च | न तु मामभिजानन्ति तत्त्वेनातश्च्यवन्ति ते
english: (For) I alone am the enjoyer and also the Lord of all sacrifices; but they do not know Me in essence (in reality), and hence they fall (return to this mortal world).
brief_explanation: The text states that those who do not recognize I, the Supreme Self, as the enjoyer and Lord of all sacrifices are acting in ignorance. They worship other gods instead, and therefore return to the mortal world after their merits are exhausted. Even those who unknowingly worship both other gods and Me will still receive some fruit from their sacrifices.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: यान्ति देवव्रता देवान्पितॄन्यान्ति पितृव्रताः | भूतानि यान्ति भूतेज्या यान्ति मद्याजिनोऽपि माम्
english: The worshippers of the gods go to them; to the manes go the ancestor-worshippers; to the deities who preside over the elements go their worshippers; but My devotees come to Me.
brief_explanation: Worshippers of gods, Pitris (ancestors), Bhutas, and the elemental beings go to those entities respectively. Those who devote to the gods or Pitris attain their forms at death. The reward for worship depends on the knowledge, faith, and nature of the offering.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: पत्रं पुष्पं फलं तोयं यो मे भक्त्या प्रयच्छति | तदहं भक्त्युपहृतमश्नामि प्रयतात्मनः
english: Whoever offers Me with devotion a leaf, a flower, a fruit or a little water that, so offered devotedly by the pure-minded, I accept.
brief_explanation: Offering, regardless of its size, is accepted by the Lord when it's given with profound faith. The Lord is satisfied with simple offerings like a leaf, flower, fruit, or water when they are presented with single-minded devotion and a pure heart. Even insignificant items like parched rice from Sudama or small berries from Sabari can please the Lord.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: यत्करोषि यदश्नासि यज्जुहोषि ददासि यत् | यत्तपस्यसि कौन्तेय तत्कुरुष्व मदर्पणम्
english: Whatever thou doest, whatever thou eatest, whatever thou offerest in sacrifice, whatever thou givest, whatever thou practisest as austerity, O Arjuna, do it as an offering unto Me.
brief_explanation: Perform all actions as offerings to the Lord, and you'll attain freedom from the bonds of Karma. This leads to self-surrender, gradual spiritual growth, and eventual transformation into divinity. All actions, results, and rewards will cease to be personal, resembling a river joining the sea.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: शुभाशुभफलैरेवं मोक्ष्यसे कर्मबन्धनैः | संन्यासयोगयुक्तात्मा विमुक्तो मामुपैष्यसि
english: Thus shalt thou be freed from the bonds of actions yielding good and evil fruits; with the mind steadfast in the Yoga of renunciation, and liberated, thou shalt come unto Me.
brief_explanation: Offering everything to Me is renunciation of actions' fruits, known as Sannyasa. With a mind steadfast in this Yoga, one is liberated from good and evil results while living, and will come to Me upon death. An objection arises: If the Lord bestows grace only on His devotees, isn't He partial with love and hatred?

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: समोऽहं सर्वभूतेषु न मे द्वेष्योऽस्ति न प्रियः | ये भजन्ति तु मां भक्त्या मयि ते तेषु चाप्यहम्
english: The same am I to all beings; to Me there is none hateful or dear; but those who worship Me with devotion are in Me and I am also in them.
brief_explanation: The Lord treats all beings equally, without favoritism or condemnation. He is not the enemy nor partial lover of any. The egoistic individual creates a divide with their wrong attitude; however, the Lord is closer to them than breath, hands, and feet.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: अपि चेत्सुदुराचारो भजते मामनन्यभाक् | साधुरेव स मन्तव्यः सम्यग्व्यवसितो हि सः
english: Even if the most sinful worships Me, with devotion to none else, he too should indeed by regarded as righteous for he has rightly resolved.
brief_explanation: Even if a wicked person worships the Lord with undivided devotion, they are considered righteous. This is demonstrated through examples like Rogue Ratnakar becoming Valmiki, and Jagai and Madhai becoming devotees. Sin can be eradicated when thoughts of God arise in one's mind.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: क्षिप्रं भवति धर्मात्मा शश्वच्छान्तिं निगच्छति | कौन्तेय प्रतिजानीहि न मे भक्तः प्रणश्यति
english: Soon he becomes righteous and attains to eternal peace; O Arjuna, proclaim thou for certain that My devotee never perishes.
brief_explanation: The verse asserts that a righteous individual attains eternal peace quickly. It emphasizes that Arjuna can state for certain that a devotee, who wholeheartedly surrenders to God, will never be destroyed.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: मां हि पार्थ व्यपाश्रित्य येऽपि स्युः पापयोनयः | स्त्रियो वैश्यास्तथा शूद्रास्तेऽपि यान्ति परां गतिम्
english: For, taking refuge in Me, they also who, O Arjuna, may be of a sinful birth women, Vaisyas as well as Sudras attain the Supreme Goal.
brief_explanation: The verse suggests that individuals from all castes, including sinful births like Chandala, women, Vaisyas, and Sudras, can attain the Supreme Goal through devotion, regardless of family traditions or social rules restricting Vedic study. Examples given include Gajendra, a lowly animal who remembered God with devotion, and Nandan, a man of low caste but a great devotee of Lord Siva. In spiritual life, distinctions of caste, color, and creed dissolve, as shown by figures like Shabari, a Bhilni (tribe) who was a great devotee of Lord Rama.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: किं पुनर्ब्राह्मणाः पुण्या भक्ता राजर्षयस्तथा | अनित्यमसुखं लोकमिमं प्राप्य भजस्व माम्
english: How much more (easily) then the hold Brahmins and devoted royal saints (attain the goal); having come to this impermanent and unhappy world, do thou worship Me.
brief_explanation: The Rajarshis, royal saints, have their duties in the kingdom but also lead spiritual lives. Human birth is rare and valuable for self-realization as it provides the power of discrimination. Despite its impermanence and associated sorrow, one should not aim for worldly happiness in this body.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: मन्मना भव मद्भक्तो मद्याजी मां नमस्कुरु | मामेवैष्यसि युक्त्वैवमात्मानं मत्परायणः
english: Fix thy mind on Me; by devoted to Me; sacrifice unto Me; bow down to Me; having thus united thy whole self to Me, taking Me as the supreme goal, thou shalt come unto Me.
brief_explanation: Fill your mind with Me, focus your heart and actions on Me. Become a devoted worshipper to attain eternal bliss. Knowing Me as the supreme goal will help you cross beyond death.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: श्रीभगवानुवाच | भूय एव महाबाहो शृणु मे परमं वचः | यत्तेऽहं प्रीयमाणाय वक्ष्यामि हितकाम्यया
english: The Blessed Lord said Again, O mighty-armed Arjuna, listen to my supreme word which I will declare to thee who who art beloved, for thy welfare.
brief_explanation: The Lord repeats His supreme word to Arjuna, who is deeply enjoying hearing it. This revelation unveils unsurpassed truth, similar to drinking nectar.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: न मे विदुः सुरगणाः प्रभवं न महर्षयः | अहमादिर्हि देवानां महर्षीणां च सर्वशः
english: Neither the hosts of the gods nor the great sages know My origin; for in every way I am the source of all the gods and the great sages.
brief_explanation: The term Prabhavam in verse 10.2 can denote great lordly power. It refers to the sages like Bhrigu, who struggle to comprehend the divine source that spawns all gods, sages, and living beings due to their immense nature. Sarvasah indicates that this source is not only the origin but also the efficient cause, inner ruler, dispenser, and guide of their intellect, among other roles.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: यो मामजमनादिं च वेत्ति लोकमहेश्वरम् | असम्मूढः स मर्त्येषु सर्वपापैः प्रमुच्यते
english: He who knows Me as unborn and beginningless, as the great Lord of the worlds, he, among mortals, is undeluded and he is liberated from all sins.
brief_explanation: The individual who understands that the Supreme Being, who is unborn and beginningless, is the great Lord of all worlds, and who is undeluded about the true nature of the Self, is liberated from all sins among mortals in all three periods of time. This liberation occurs through the eradication of ignorance, the root cause of all sins, and its effect, egoism and superimposition between the Self and not-Self. The sage of Self-realization is completely freed from all sins as they are burned like roasted seeds, preventing future births and actions.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: बुद्धिर्ज्ञानमसम्मोहः क्षमा सत्यं दमः शमः | सुखं दुःखं भवोऽभावो भयं चाभयमेव च
english: Intellect, wisdom, non-delusion, forgiveness, truth, self-restraint, calmness, happiness, pain, existence or birth, non-existence or death, fear and also fearlessness.
brief_explanation: Intellect: the power of understanding subtle objects by the inner instrument (Antahkarana). Wisdom: knowledge of the Self, acting with discrimination. Nondelusion: freedom from illusion in action or knowledge at a given moment.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: अहिंसा समता तुष्टिस्तपो दानं यशोऽयशः | भवन्ति भावा भूतानां मत्त एव पृथग्विधाः
english: Non-injury, eanimity, contentment, austerity, beneficence, fame, ill-fame (these) different kinds of alities of beings arise from Me alone.
brief_explanation: Ahimsa refers to non-injury towards all living beings in thought, word, and deed. Samata is a state where one experiences neither likes nor dislikes when encountering pleasant or unpleasant situations. Tushtih is contentment, providing inner peace and wealth by annihilating greed.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: महर्षयः सप्त पूर्वे चत्वारो मनवस्तथा | मद्भावा मानसा जाता येषां लोक इमाः प्रजाः
english: The seven great sages, the ancient four and also the Manus, possessed of powers like Me (on account of their minds being fixed on Me), were born of (My) mind; from them are these creatures born in this world.
brief_explanation: Great Rishis refer to seven ancient sages like Bhrigu, Vasishtha, and four Kumaras (Sanaka, Sanandana, Sanatkumara, Sanatsujata), who were born from the mind, possessed of powers like God, and directed their thoughts exclusively towards Him. The Manus, mindborn sons of God, were the rulers of men and framed laws for humanity's guidance. In mythology, these principles are symbolized with human names such as Bhrigu, Marichi, Atri, Pulastya, Pulaha, Kratu, Vasishtha for the seven great sages, and Manas (mind), Buddhi (intellect), Chitta (subconsciousness), and Ahamkara (egoism) for the four Manus in the microcosm.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: एतां विभूतिं योगं च मम यो वेत्ति तत्त्वतः | सोऽविकम्पेन योगेन युज्यते नात्र संशयः
english: He who in truth knows these manifold manifestations of My Being and (this) Yoga-power of Mine becomes established in the unshakable Yoga; there is no doubt about it.
brief_explanation: The knowledge of the Lord's manifold manifestations and immanent power leads to a firm, unalterable Yoga, resulting in eternal bliss and perfect harmony. A person who truly understands the Lord's extensive manifestation and Yogic powers is endowed with a strong, unwavering Yoga, attaining the highest knowledge of the Self and being free from superiority and inferiority complexes. This realization leads to the awareness of the Lord in all beings and all beings in the Lord, causing the Yogi to never hate any creature.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: अहं सर्वस्य प्रभवो मत्तः सर्वं प्रवर्तते | इति मत्वा भजन्ते मां बुधा भावसमन्विताः
english: I am the source of all; from Me everything evolves; understanding thus, the wise, endowed with meditation, worship Me.
brief_explanation: The Lord is the source, material, and efficient cause of the entire universe, as the only support for all forms. Realizing this omnipresence, the wise worship the Lord with devotion, understanding Him to be the same across all places and times. The Supreme, known as Vaasudeva, is the origin of the world's changes, including existence, destruction, action, fruit, and enjoyment.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: मच्चित्ता मद्गतप्राणा बोधयन्तः परस्परम् | कथयन्तश्च मां नित्यं तुष्यन्ति च रमन्ति च
english: With their mind and their life wholly absorbed in Me, enlightening each other and ever speaking of Me, they are satisfied and delighted.
brief_explanation: A devotee who has realized oneness with the Lord constantly thinks about Him, and their life is absorbed in Him. According to another interpretation, all their senses are absorbed in Him. They take delight in discussing His attributes, feel immense satisfaction, and are delighted as if they are in the company of their Beloved (God).

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: तेषां सततयुक्तानां भजतां प्रीतिपूर्वकम् | ददामि बुद्धियोगं तं येन मामुपयान्ति ते
english: To them who are ever steadfast, worshipping Me with love, I give the Yoga of discrimination by which they come to Me.
brief_explanation: The Lord bestows the Yoga of discrimination (Buddhi Yoga, a form of Jnana Yoga) upon devotees who are steadfast, worship Him with love, and have no selfish motives. This wisdom helps them to know the Supreme Lord as their own Self, beyond all limitations, through deep meditation and intuition. The purpose of this divine grace is to remove obstacles on the path of the aspirant or devotee.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: तेषामेवानुकम्पार्थमहमज्ञानजं तमः | नाशयाम्यात्मभावस्थो ज्ञानदीपेन भास्वता
english: Out of mere compassion for them, I, dwelling within their Self, destroy the darkness born of ignorance by the luminous lamp of knowledge.
brief_explanation: The Lord dwells within devotees' hearts, using the lamp of knowledge to destroy their ignorance-born darkness. This lamp, fueled by pure devotion, shines with light from constant meditation, right intuition, and virtuous practices. It requires no instrument or practice for removing darkness, as the dawn of Self-knowledge alone is sufficient to dispel ignorance.

speaker: Arjuna
sanskrit: अर्जुन उवाच | परं ब्रह्म परं धाम पवित्रं परमं भवान् | पुरुषं शाश्वतं दिव्यमादिदेवमजं विभुम्
english: Arjuna said Thou art the Supreme Brahman, the supreme abode (or the supreme light), the supreme purifier, eternal, divine Person, the primeval God, unborn andn omnipresent.
brief_explanation: The term "Param" refers to the highest absolute self, free from limiting adjuncts. This is the Satchidananda Brahman. "Param Dhama" signifies the supreme abode or light that supports all creation, from the Creator down to the smallest blade of grass.

speaker: Unknown
sanskrit: आहुस्त्वामृषयः सर्वे देवर्षिर्नारदस्तथा | असितो देवलो व्यासः स्वयं चैव ब्रवीषि मे
english: All the sages have thus declared Thee, as also the divine sage Narada; so also Asita, Devala and Vyasa; and now Thou Thyself sayest so to me.
brief_explanation: The Rishis, including Narada, Deval, and Vyasa, declared you as the supreme self. This includes Devarshi, a highly evolved divine sage. You spoke to them about yourself even to Asita.

speaker: Unknown
sanskrit: सर्वमेतदृतं मन्ये यन्मां वदसि केशव | न हि ते भगवन्व्यक्तिं विदुर्देवा न दानवाः
english: I believe all this that Thou sayest to me to be true, O Krishna; verily, O blessed Lord! neither the gods nor the demons know Thy manifestation (origin).
brief_explanation: Bhagavan, according to the commentary, is the one who embodies the six attributes: wisdom, dispassion, lordship, virtue, wealth, and omnipotence. He is also known as the one who knows the origins, dissolutions, and futures of all beings and is omniscient. Arjuna addresses Krishna as Keshava because he is omniscient, knowing what's in Arjuna's mind.

speaker: Unknown
sanskrit: स्वयमेवात्मनात्मानं वेत्थ त्वं पुरुषोत्तम | भूतभावन भूतेश देवदेव जगत्पते
english: Swami Sivananda did not comment on this sloka
brief_explanation: The term 'Purushottama' refers to the supreme Purusha, who takes four forms: source of beings, Lord of beings, God of gods, and ruler of the world. 'Devadeva' indicates He is worshipped by Indra and other deities, and 'Jagatpati' signifies the protector and guide of the world through Vedic instructions.

speaker: Unknown
sanskrit: वक्तुमर्हस्यशेषेण दिव्या ह्यात्मविभूतयः | याभिर्विभूतिभिर्लोकानिमांस्त्वं व्याप्य तिष्ठसि
english: Thou shouldst indeed tell, without reserve, of Thy divine glories by which Thou existest, pervading all these worlds. (None else can do so.)
brief_explanation: Thou shouldst tell without reminder, the divine glories by which Thou hast pervaded and exist in these worlds. (Sivananda's commentary has no specific remark for this verse.)

speaker: Unknown
sanskrit: कथं विद्यामहं योगिंस्त्वां सदा परिचिन्तयन् | केषु केषु च भावेषु चिन्त्योऽसि भगवन्मया
english: How shall I, ever meditating, know Thee, O Yogin? In what aspects or things, O blessed Lord, art Thou to be thought of by me?
brief_explanation: Arjuna asks about constant meditation to know God in various aspects within external objects, even while perceiving them. He requests the Lord to reveal His own glories for clear recognition of unity everywhere.

speaker: Unknown
sanskrit: विस्तरेणात्मनो योगं विभूतिं च जनार्दन | भूयः कथय तृप्तिर्हि शृण्वतो नास्ति मेऽमृतम्
english: Tell me again in detail, O Krishna, of Thy Yogic power and glory; for I am not satiated with what I have heard of Thy life-giving and nectar-like speech.
brief_explanation: The Lord, referred to as Janardana, is a title signifying that He is the one sought for both worldly success and spiritual salvation. Arjuna requests an in-depth explanation of Krishna's Yogic power and glory, even though it has been previously discussed in chapters 7 and 9, due to his unending desire to hear the divine teachings.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: श्रीभगवानुवाच | हन्त ते कथयिष्यामि दिव्या ह्यात्मविभूतयः | प्राधान्यतः कुरुश्रेष्ठ नास्त्यन्तो विस्तरस्य मे
english: The Blessed Lord said Very well! Now I will declare to thee My divine glories in their prominence, O Arjuna; there is no end to their detailed description.
brief_explanation: My divine glories, in their prominence, will be declared. However, as they are illimitable, a detailed account cannot be provided.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: अहमात्मा गुडाकेश सर्वभूताशयस्थितः | अहमादिश्च मध्यं च भूतानामन्त एव च
english: I am the Self, O Gudakesa, seated in the hearts of all beings; I am the beginning, the middle and also the end of all beings.
brief_explanation: The Self (Atma) is described as being seated in the hearts of all beings, and it serves as the origin, middle, and end of all created beings. I am also the birth, life, and death of all beings. Aspirants who can meditate on Me as the innermost Self are considered first-class, while those who cannot should think of the Lord in various mentioned things.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: आदित्यानामहं विष्णुर्ज्योतिषां रविरंशुमान् | मरीचिर्मरुतामस्मि नक्षत्राणामहं शशी
english: Among the (twelve) Adityas, I am Vishnu; among luminaries, the radiant sun; I am Marichi among the (seven or forty-nine) Maruts; among stars the moon am I.
brief_explanation: The Aditya referred to is Vishnu, Dhata, Mitra, Aryama, Rudra, Varuna, Bhaga, Surya, Vivasvan, Pusham, Savita, and Tvashta, making them the twelve Adityas. The Maruts are gods controlling winds, with some believing there are seven or forty-nine of them. The Adityas, luminaries like Agni, Maruts, stars, and others are ordinary manifestations of the Lord.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: वेदानां सामवेदोऽस्मि देवानामस्मि वासवः | इन्द्रियाणां मनश्चास्मि भूतानामस्मि चेतना
english: Among the Vedas I am the Sama-Veda; I am Vasava among the gods; among the senses I am the mind; and I am intelligence among living beings.
brief_explanation: The Sama Veda is among the Vedas, and Indra is among gods. The senses include the five JnanaIndriyas (organs of knowledge) and the five KarmaIndriyas (organs of action), with mind being considered as the eleventh sense due to its role in enabling functions of other senses. Chetana, or intelligence, is the state of intellect manifest in the aggregate of the body and senses, illuminating all from the intellect down to the grossest object.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: रुद्राणां शङ्करश्चास्मि वित्तेशो यक्षरक्षसाम् | वसूनां पावकश्चास्मि मेरुः शिखरिणामहम्
english: And, among the Rudras I am Sankara; among the Yakshas and Rakshasas, the Lord of wealth (Kubera); among the Vasus I am Pavaka (fire); and among the (seven) mountains I am the Meru.
brief_explanation: The Rudras, numbering eleven, symbolize vital airs and mind. Among them, Sankara is considered the primary one. Vasus, representing earth, water, fire, air, ether, sun, moon, and stars, are so named due to their ability to encompass the universe.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: पुरोधसां च मुख्यं मां विद्धि पार्थ बृहस्पतिम् | सेनानीनामहं स्कन्दः सरसामस्मि सागरः
english: And, among the household priests (of kings), O Arjuna, know Me to be the chief, Brihaspati; among the army generals I am Skana; among lakes I am the ocean. '
brief_explanation: Brihaspati is the chief priest among household priests, often associated with Indra's household. Skanda, another name for Kartikeya or Lord Subramanya, functions as the general of the gods' hosts. Regarding things that hold water, like lakes, I am likened to the ocean.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: महर्षीणां भृगुरहं गिरामस्म्येकमक्षरम् | यज्ञानां जपयज्ञोऽस्मि स्थावराणां हिमालयः
english: Among the great sages I am Bhrigu; among words I am the one syllable (Om); among sacrifices I am the sacrifice of silent repetition; among the immovable things I am the Himalayas.
brief_explanation: Bhrigu, one of the mind-born of the Creator, is among the great Rishis. Himalayas are among immovable things. Japayajna, the sacrifice of silent repetition, is among sacrifices.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: अश्वत्थः सर्ववृक्षाणां देवर्षीणां च नारदः | गन्धर्वाणां चित्ररथः सिद्धानां कपिलो मुनिः
english: Among all the trees ( I am) the Peepul; among the divine sages, I am Narada; among Gandharvas, Chitraratha; among the perfected, the sage Kapila.
brief_explanation: The Asvattha tree, among all trees, is also revered as a Divine Rishi among gods. Narada is the distinguished Rishi among Gandharvas. Chitraratha is among the Siddhas, the perfected ones who naturally possess Dharma (virtue), Jnana (Self-knowledge), Vairagya (dispassion), and Aisvarya (lordship).

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: उच्चैःश्रवसमश्वानां विद्धि माममृतोद्भवम् | ऐरावतं गजेन्द्राणां नराणां च नराधिपम्
english: Know Me as Ucchaisravas born of nectar, among horses; among lordly elephants (I am) the Airavata; and, among men, the king.
brief_explanation: Ucchaisravas is a celestial horse, born from the churning of the ocean of milk (Amrita). Airavata is Indra's elephant, also born during this event, signifying divine creatures emerging from the sacred process.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: आयुधानामहं वज्रं धेनूनामस्मि कामधुक् | प्रजनश्चास्मि कन्दर्पः सर्पाणामस्मि वासुकिः
english: Among weapons I am the thunderbolt; among cows I am the wish-fulfilling cow called Kamadhenu; I am the progenitor, the god of love; among serpents I am Vasuki.
brief_explanation: Vajram is the thunderbolt weapon, a formidable instrument of warfare exclusive to Indra who has completed a hundred sacrifices. Kamadhenu, the heavenly cow, provides all desired objects, born both from the great sage Vasishtha and the ocean of milk. Kandarpa represents Cupid.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: अनन्तश्चास्मि नागानां वरुणो यादसामहम् | पितॄणामर्यमा चास्मि यमः संयमतामहम्
english: I am Ananta among the Nagas; I am Varuna among water-deities; Aryaman among the Manes I am; I am Yama among the governors.
brief_explanation: Ananta is the lord of serpents, a fire-colored deity among the Nagas. Varuna is the king of water gods. Aryaman is the ruler among the ancestors or manes.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: प्रह्लादश्चास्मि दैत्यानां कालः कलयतामहम् | मृगाणां च मृगेन्द्रोऽहं वैनतेयश्च पक्षिणाम्
english: And, I am Prahlada among the demons, among the reckoners I am time; among beasts I am the lion, and Vainateya (Garuda) among birds.
brief_explanation: Prahlada, though a son of a demon (Hiranyakasipu), was a great devotee of the Lord among demons. In the realm of time (Kalayatam), he is comparable to reckoners. Among beasts, he identifies himself as I.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: पवनः पवतामस्मि रामः शस्त्रभृतामहम् | झषाणां मकरश्चास्मि स्रोतसामस्मि जाह्नवी
english: Among the purifiers (or the speeders) I am the wind; Rama among the warriors am I; among the fishes I am the shark; among the streams I am the Ganga.
brief_explanation: Ganga is identified as a stream, referring to her journey through earthly channels after being brought down from heaven by Bhagiratha. Previously, she was Jahnu (after being swallowed by him).

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: सर्गाणामादिरन्तश्च मध्यं चैवाहमर्जुन | अध्यात्मविद्या विद्यानां वादः प्रवदतामहम्
english: Among creations I am the beginning, the middle and also the end, O Arjuna; among the sciences I am the science of the Self; and I am the logic among controversialists.
brief_explanation: The verse 10.32 describes I (God) as the metaphysics among all sciences, knowledge of the Self among branches of knowledge, argument of disputants, logic of controversialists, and speech of orators. In verse 20, God is referred to as the beginning, middle, and end of the entire creation. Vada, Jalpa, and Vitanda are forms of argumentation used by aspirants free from RagaDvesha and jealousy, aiming to ascertain Truth, not for victory.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: अक्षराणामकारोऽस्मि द्वन्द्वः सामासिकस्य च | अहमेवाक्षयः कालो धाताहं विश्वतोमुखः
english: Among the letters of the alphabets, the letter 'A' I am and the dual among the compounds. I am verily the inexhaustible or everlasting time; I am the dispenser (of the fruits of actions) having faces in all directions.
brief_explanation: The letter A represents I among alphabets, and in compounds, I am the Dvandva (union of two). Time refers to the ultimate element or Paramesvara, the Supreme Lord transcending time. As the Allfaced, the Supreme Being is omnipresent.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: मृत्युः सर्वहरश्चाहमुद्भवश्च भविष्यताम् | कीर्तिः श्रीर्वाक्च नारीणां स्मृतिर्मेधा धृतिः क्षमा
english: And I am the all-devouring Death, and the prosperity of those who are to be prosperous; among the feminine alities (I am) fame, prosperity, speech, memory, intelligence, firmness and forgiveness.
brief_explanation: Death is the all-devouring, seizing both life and wealth; it's also associated with the Supreme Lord who destroys everything during cosmic dissolution. I am the origin of future beings and their path to prosperity. I am speech adorning justice, memory recalling past objects, intelligence, firmness, and forgiveness, which are considered the daughters of Daksha, married to Dharma and collectively known as Dharmapatnis.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: बृहत्साम तथा साम्नां गायत्री छन्दसामहम् | मासानां मार्गशीर्षोऽहमृतूनां कुसुमाकरः
english: Among the hymns also I am the Brihatsaman; among metres Gayatri am I; among the montsh I am the Margasirsha; among the seasons (I am) the flowery season.
brief_explanation: Brihatsaman is the principal Sama hymn, symbolizing its grandeur. Margasirsha, from mid-December to mid-January, was traditionally the first month of the year due to its temperate climate. Kusumakara refers to the flowery season or spring.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: द्यूतं छलयतामस्मि तेजस्तेजस्विनामहम् | जयोऽस्मि व्यवसायोऽस्मि सत्त्वं सत्त्ववतामहम्
english: I am the gambling of the fraudulent; I am the splendour of the splendid; I am victory; I am determination (of those who are determined); I am the goodness of the good.
brief_explanation: The verse 10.36 refers to gambling, a form of deception, as one of the methods of defrauding others. It also suggests that power, victory, effort, and goodness are manifestations of the divine. Lastly, the verse implies that Sattva (goodness) can take forms such as Dharma (virtue), Jnana (knowledge), Vairagya (dispassion), and Aisvarya (wealth or lordship) in virtuous individuals.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: वृष्णीनां वासुदेवोऽस्मि पाण्डवानां धनञ्जयः | मुनीनामप्यहं व्यासः कवीनामुशना कविः
english: Among the Vrishnis I am Vaasudeva; among the Pandavas I am Arjuna; among the sages I am Vyasa; among the Poets I am Usanas, the poet.
brief_explanation: Vaasudeva is the supreme among the Vrishnis, descended from Yadu. Among the Pandavas, Dhananjaya refers to Arjuna. Usanas, known as Sukracharya, is a prominent sage and poet in the demon realm.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: दण्डो दमयतामस्मि नीतिरस्मि जिगीषताम् | मौनं चैवास्मि गुह्यानां ज्ञानं ज्ञानवतामहम्
english: Of those who punish, I am the sceptre; among those who seek victory, I am statesmanship; and also among secrets, I am silence; knowledge among knowers I am.
brief_explanation: Diplomacy and statesmanship are associated with 'I am'. Silence is also a characteristic of one who seeks victory. In the realm of secrets, 'I' represents silence.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: यच्चापि सर्वभूतानां बीजं तदहमर्जुन | न तदस्ति विना यत्स्यान्मया भूतं चराचरम्
english: And whatever is the seed of all beings, that also am I, O Arjuna; there is no being, whether moving or unmoving, that can exist without Me.
brief_explanation: The primal seed of all beings, including Arjuna, is the self within me. Nothing exists without my being, as I am the essence and soul of all moving and unmoving entities.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: नान्तोऽस्ति मम दिव्यानां विभूतीनां परन्तप | एष तूद्देशतः प्रोक्तो विभूतेर्विस्तरो मया
english: There is no end to My divine gloreis, O Arjuna, but this is a brief statement by Me of the particulars of My divine glories.
brief_explanation: The text states that the divine glories of the Lord are beyond comprehension, with no limits to His powers or glory. Parantapa refers to one who burns internal enemies such as lust, anger, greed, and delusion.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: यद्यद्विभूतिमत्सत्त्वं श्रीमदूर्जितमेव वा | तत्तदेवावगच्छ त्वं मम तेजोंऽशसम्भवम्
english: Whatever being there is glorious, prosperous or powerful, that know thou to be a manifestation of a part of My splendour.
brief_explanation: The phrase means that whatever glorious, prosperous, powerful beings or entities you encounter are manifestations of a part of my divine splendor. (Sivananda)

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: अथवा बहुनैतेन किं ज्ञातेन तवार्जुन | विष्टभ्याहमिदं कृत्स्नमेकांशेन स्थितो जगत्
english: But, of what avail to thee is the knowledge of all these details, O Arjuna? I exist, supporting this whole world by one part of Myself.
brief_explanation: The Lord concludes that He exists supporting this whole world by one part, constituting all beings. This is based on the Purusha Sukta declaration that one part of Him forms the cosmos. The whole world is considered one foot of the Lord, but 'part' or 'foot' are mere imaginative constructs in reality.

speaker: Arjuna
sanskrit: अर्जुन उवाच | मदनुग्रहाय परमं गुह्यमध्यात्मसंज्ञितम् | यत्त्वयोक्तं वचस्तेन मोहोऽयं विगतो मम
english: Arjuna said By this word (explanation) of the highest secret concerning the Self which Thou hast spoken, for the sake of blessing me, my delusion is gone.
brief_explanation: Arjuna's delusion about killing relatives and preceptors has vanished after receiving profound instructions from Krishna, which led him to have the vision of the Cosmic Form. The vision of the Cosmic Form is a significant but not ultimate experience in spiritual progress, as evidenced by Arjuna's desire to see Krishna's other forms again. Arjuna considers Krishna's teachings invaluable, having surpassed those found in the Vedas, and expresses his wish to behold Krishna's entire Cosmic Form.

speaker: Unknown
sanskrit: भवाप्ययौ हि भूतानां श्रुतौ विस्तरशो मया | त्वत्तः कमलपत्राक्ष माहात्म्यमपि चाव्ययम्
english: The origin and the destruction of beings verily have been heard by me in detail from Thee, O lotus-eyed Lord, and also Thy inexhaustible greatness.
brief_explanation: The term "Kamalapatrayak" refers to one with eyes like a lotus petal, symbolizing divine vision or higher knowledge. This title also implies deep self-knowledge, as 'Kamala' means Self. This being is inexhaustible (avyayam) and its greatness (mahaatmyam) has been detailed in the scriptures.

speaker: Unknown
sanskrit: एवमेतद्यथात्थ त्वमात्मानं परमेश्वर | द्रष्टुमिच्छामि ते रूपमैश्वरं पुरुषोत्तम
english: (Now) O Supreme Lord, as Thou hast thus described Thyself, O Supreme Person, I wish to see Thy divine form.
brief_explanation: The verse is interpreted by some commentators as two independent sentences: "So it is, O Supreme Lord, as You have declared Yourself to be." and "I desire to see Your form, O Supreme Person, in its Isvara aspect, characterized by infinite knowledge, sovereignty, power, strength, prowess, and splendour."

speaker: Unknown
sanskrit: मन्यसे यदि तच्छक्यं मया द्रष्टुमिति प्रभो | योगेश्वर ततो मे त्वं दर्शयात्मानमव्ययम्
english: If Thou, O Lord, thinkest it possible for me to see it, do Thou, then, O Lord of the Yogins, show me Thy imperishable Self.
brief_explanation: Arjuna desires to see the Cosmic Form of the Lord, seeking his divine vision. This supreme sight is possible only through the Lord's grace, who is also the Lord of Yogins (Yogesvara). Yoga refers to the realization of identity between the individual soul and the Absolute, and Yogesvara is he who bestows this understanding on worthy spiritual seekers.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: श्रीभगवानुवाच | पश्य मे पार्थ रूपाणि शतशोऽथ सहस्रशः | नानाविधानि दिव्यानि नानावर्णाकृतीनि च
english: The Blessed Lord said Behold, O Arjuna, forms of Mine, by the hundreds and thousands, of different sorts, divine, and of various colours and shapes.
brief_explanation: The Cosmic Form is divine, consisting of countless beings in all forms, shapes, colors, and conditions. This includes diverse beings such as the fat and lean, short and tall, active and passive, rich and poor, intelligent and dull, healthy and sick, and many more. It also contains different objects with various shapes and distinctive marks.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: पश्यादित्यान्वसून्रुद्रानश्विनौ मरुतस्तथा | बहून्यदृष्टपूर्वाणि पश्याश्चर्याणि भारत
english: Behold the Adityas, the Vasus, the Rudras, the two Asvins and also the Maruts; behold many wonders never seen before, O Arjuna.
brief_explanation: The Adityas, Vasus, Rudras, Asvins, and Maruts are entities mentioned earlier in the text. Here, they encourage Bharata to witness additional, previously unseen wonders in this world.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: इहैकस्थं जगत्कृत्स्नं पश्याद्य सचराचरम् | मम देहे गुडाकेश यच्चान्यद् द्रष्टुमिच्छसि
english: Now behold, O Arjuna, in this, My body, the whole universe centred in one including the moving and the unmoving and whatever else thou desirest to see.
brief_explanation: This verse implies that one is centered in the whole universe, both moving and unmoving. The speaker suggests that Gudakesa (Arjuna) desires to see what else beyond his current situation, possibly questioning the outcome of the war.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: न तु मां शक्यसे द्रष्टुमनेनैव स्वचक्षुषा | दिव्यं ददामि ते चक्षुः पश्य मे योगमैश्वरम्
english: But thou art not able to behold Me with these thine own eyes; I give thee the divine eye; behold My lordly Yoga.
brief_explanation: The Lord offers Arjuna a divine eye to perceive His cosmic form, which transcends human sight. This is not ordinary perception through eyes or mind but an inner experience of His sovereign Yoga power.

speaker: Sanjaya
sanskrit: सञ्जय उवाच | एवमुक्त्वा ततो राजन्महायोगेश्वरो हरिः | दर्शयामास पार्थाय परमं रूपमैश्वरम्
english: Sanjaya said Having thus spoken, O king, the great Lord of Yoga, hari (Krishna), showed to Arjuna His supreme form as the Lord.
brief_explanation: Great Lord of Yoga, Hari, showed the Supreme and Sovereign form to Arjuna after speaking thus, as described to King Dhritarashtra by Sanjaya.

speaker: Unknown
sanskrit: अनेकवक्त्रनयनमनेकाद्भुतदर्शनम् | अनेकदिव्याभरणं दिव्यानेकोद्यतायुधम्
english: With numerous mouths and eyes, with numerous wonderful sights, with numerous divine ornaments, with numerous divine weapons uplifted (such a form He showed).
brief_explanation: The Cosmic Form had numerous mouths, eyes, and wonderful sights. Arjuna witnessed the Lord with various divine ornaments and weapons uplifted. The entire manifestation was perceived as a single, vast form of the Lord, encompassing everything.

speaker: Unknown
sanskrit: दिव्यमाल्याम्बरधरं दिव्यगन्धानुलेपनम् | सर्वाश्चर्यमयं देवमनन्तं विश्वतोमुखम्
english: Wearing divine garlands (necklaces) and apparel, anointed with divine unguents, the all-wonderful, resplendent (Being) endless with faces on all sides.
brief_explanation: The phrase "Visvatomukham" refers to God being omnipresent, having faces on all sides, as He is the Self of all beings. "Devam" signifies God's resplendence and divine nature. "Anantam" indicates God's infinite and limitless existence, being free from spatial, temporal, and material limitations.

speaker: Unknown
sanskrit: दिवि सूर्यसहस्रस्य भवेद्युगपदुत्थिता | यदि भाः सदृशी सा स्याद्भासस्तस्य महात्मनः
english: If the splendour of a thousand suns were to blaze out at once (simultaneously) in the sky, that would be the splendour of that mighty Being (great Soul).
brief_explanation: The "divi" refers to the sky, and "Mahatma" denotes the great Soul or Cosmic Form. In this context, the passage describes a spectacle where a thousand suns arise simultaneously in the sky, creating an extraordinary splendour comparable to that of the Cosmic Form.

speaker: Unknown
sanskrit: तत्रैकस्थं जगत्कृत्स्नं प्रविभक्तमनेकधा | अपश्यद्देवदेवस्य शरीरे पाण्डवस्तदा
english: There, in the body of the God of gods, Arjuna then saw the whole universe resting in one, with its many groups.
brief_explanation: The verse describes Arjuna viewing the Cosmic Form, where everything he saw was perceived as different parts of the Lord's divine body. This form encompassed various groups, possibly gods, manes, and other beings. Realizing this transcendental vision is beyond the capacity of the finite mind and can only be achieved in Samadhi.

speaker: Unknown
sanskrit: ततः स विस्मयाविष्टो हृष्टरोमा धनञ्जयः | प्रणम्य शिरसा देवं कृताञ्जलिरभाषत
english: Then, Arjuna, filled with wonder and with his hair standing on end, bowed down his head to the God and spoke with joined palms.
brief_explanation: Arjuna, filled with wonder, prostrated himself before the Cosmic Form, symbolizing his true humility - an essential aspect of devotion.

speaker: Arjuna
sanskrit: अर्जुन उवाच | पश्यामि देवांस्तव देव देहे सर्वांस्तथा भूतविशेषसङ्घान् | ब्रह्माणमीशं कमलासनस्थ- मृषींश्च सर्वानुरगांश्च दिव्यान्
english: Arjuna said I see all the gods, O God, in Thy body, and (also) hosts of various classes of beings, Brahma, the Lord, seated on the lotus, all the sages and the celestial serpents.
brief_explanation: The speaker, Arjuna, describes witnessing various beings within the Cosmic Form as hosts of diverse entities, including animate and inanimate. Brahma, the Lord of all creatures, is seated at the center on a lotus. Sages and serpents are also present, making up this divine assembly.

speaker: Unknown
sanskrit: अनेकबाहूदरवक्त्रनेत्रं पश्यामि त्वां सर्वतोऽनन्तरूपम् | नान्तं न मध्यं न पुनस्तवादिं पश्यामि विश्वेश्वर विश्वरूप
english: I see Thee of boundless form on every side with many arms, stomachs, mouths and eyes: neither the end nor the middle nor also the beginning do I see, O Lord of the universe, O Cosmic Form.
brief_explanation: The text describes that the Lord, being omnipresent and eternal, does not have a beginning, middle, or end as He transcends space and time. Arjuna, through divine grace, could see the Lord in His boundless form, which encompasses everything and is both the origin of the universe (Ādima) and the Cosmic Form (Viśvarūpa).

speaker: Unknown
sanskrit: किरीटिनं गदिनं चक्रिणं च तेजोराशिं सर्वतो दीप्तिमन्तम् | पश्यामि त्वां दुर्निरीक्ष्यं समन्ताद् दीप्तानलार्कद्युतिमप्रमेयम्
english: I see Thee with the diadem, the club and the discus, a mass of radiance shining everywhere, very hard to look at, blazing all round like burning fire and the sun, and immeasurable.
brief_explanation: The Lord is described as one with a diadem (crown), wielding a club and discus, radiating everywhere in a mass of radiance, shining like blazing fire and sun, hard to look at, and immeasurable. This suggests His omnipresence and transcendental nature beyond all forms, yet visible through inner divine intuition. The vision signifies the Lord's power of Yoga, implying His imperishable nature.

speaker: Unknown
sanskrit: त्वमक्षरं परमं वेदितव्यं त्वमस्य विश्वस्य परं निधानम् | त्वमव्ययः शाश्वतधर्मगोप्ता सनातनस्त्वं पुरुषो मतो मे
english: Thou art the Imperishable, the Supreme Being, worthy to be known. Thou art the great treasure-house of this universe; Thou art the imperishable protector of the eternal Dhrama; Thou art the Primal Person, I deem.
brief_explanation: The Supreme Being, called the Treasurehouse of the universe, is also its abode or refuge. This entity preserves and protects all beings within it. As an inexhaustible source, it is sought by the devotee at all times.

speaker: Unknown
sanskrit: अनादिमध्यान्तमनन्तवीर्य- मनन्तबाहुं शशिसूर्यनेत्रम् | पश्यामि त्वां दीप्तहुताशवक्त्रं स्वतेजसा विश्वमिदं तपन्तम्
english: I see Thee without beginning, middle or end, infinite in power, of endless arms, the sun and the moon being Thy eyes, the burning fire Thy mouth, heating the whole universe with Thy radiance.
brief_explanation: The phrase "anadimadhyantam" suggests that God has no beginning, middle, or end. "Anantaviryam" indicates His infinite power. "Shashisuryanetram" refers to His eyes being like the sun and moon.

speaker: Unknown
sanskrit: द्यावापृथिव्योरिदमन्तरं हि व्याप्तं त्वयैकेन दिशश्च सर्वाः | दृष्ट्वाद्भुतं रूपमुग्रं तवेदं लोकत्रयं प्रव्यथितं महात्मन्
english: This space between the earth and the heaven and all the arters are filled by Thee alone; having seen this, Thy wonderful and teriible form, the three worlds are trembling with fear, O great-souled Being.
brief_explanation: The phrase "dyāvāpṛthivyōḥ" refers to the universe of animate and inanimate objects. "Idam antaram hi" indicates that this space within the universe is filled by you alone, the great-souled Being. Seeing your Cosmic Form, Arjuna contemplates it as wonderful and terrible, causing trembling in the three worlds.

speaker: Unknown
sanskrit: अमी हि त्वां सुरसङ्घा विशन्ति केचिद्भीताः प्राञ्जलयो गृणन्ति | स्वस्तीत्युक्त्वा महर्षिसिद्धसङ्घाः स्तुवन्ति त्वां स्तुतिभिः पुष्कलाभिः
english: Verily, into Thee enter these hosts of gods; some extol Thee in fear with joined palms; saying 'may it be well', bands of great sages and perfected ones praise Thee with hymns complete.
brief_explanation: Great sages like Narada and Kapila extol you with complete, profound praises using inspiring hymns.

speaker: Unknown
sanskrit: रुद्रादित्या वसवो ये च साध्या विश्वेऽश्विनौ मरुतश्चोष्मपाश्च | गन्धर्वयक्षासुरसिद्धसङ्घा वीक्षन्ते त्वां विस्मिताश्चैव सर्वे
english: The Rudras, Adityas, Vasus, Sadhyas, Visvedevas, the two Asvins, Maruts, the manes and the hosts of celestial singers, Yakshas, demons and the perfected ones, are all looking at Thee, in great amazement.
brief_explanation: The Rudras, Adityas, Vasus, Sadhyas, Visvedevas, the two Asvins, Maruts, Ushmapas (Pitris), Gandharvas, Yakshas, Asuras, and Siddhas are various divine entities mentioned in the Bhagavad Gita. The Sadhyas are a class of gods led by Brahma, Visvedevas were guardians of the world, known for providing abundance to humans. The two Asvins are physicians of the gods born from the daughter of Tushta and the Sun.

speaker: Unknown
sanskrit: रूपं महत्ते बहुवक्त्रनेत्रं महाबाहो बहुबाहूरुपादम् | बहूदरं बहुदंष्ट्राकरालं दृष्ट्वा लोकाः प्रव्यथितास्तथाहम्
english: Having seen Thy immeasurable form with many mouths and eyes, O mighty-armed, with many arms, thighs and feet, with many stomachs and fearful with many teeth the worlds are terrified and so am I.
brief_explanation: The Cosmic Form is described as immeasurable and possessing many forms, including mouths, eyes, arms, thighs, feet, stomachs, and teeth. Seeing this form has terrified all living beings in the world. This fearsome appearance is a manifestation of God, as Arjuna acknowledges with "I".

speaker: Unknown
sanskrit: नभःस्पृशं दीप्तमनेकवर्णं व्यात्ताननं दीप्तविशालनेत्रम् | दृष्ट्वा हि त्वां प्रव्यथितान्तरात्मा धृतिं न विन्दामि शमं च विष्णो
