english: On seeing Thee (the Cosmic Form) touching the sky, shining in many colours, with mouths wide open, with large fiery eyes, I am terrified at heart and find neither courage nor peace, O Vishnu.
brief_explanation: The Cosmic Form is described as touching the sky, shining brightly in many colors, with wide-open mouths and fiery eyes. Seeing this form, Arjuna's inner self is terrified. However, he does not find courage or peace, but instead experiences distress.

speaker: Unknown
sanskrit: दंष्ट्राकरालानि च ते मुखानि दृष्ट्वैव कालानलसन्निभानि | दिशो न जाने न लभे च शर्म प्रसीद देवेश जगन्निवास
english: Having seen Thy mouths fearful with teeth (blazing) like the fires of cosmic dissolution, I know not the four arters, nor do I find peace. Have mercy, O Lord of the gods, O abode of the universe.
brief_explanation: The Lord of the gods, Jagannivasa (the substratum of the universe), is seen with fearful, blazing mouths like the fires that consume during the dissolution of worlds (Pralaya). However, I do not know the four directions as I cannot distinguish east from west nor north from south.

speaker: Unknown
sanskrit: अमी च त्वां धृतराष्ट्रस्य पुत्राः सर्वे सहैवावनिपालसङ्घैः | भीष्मो द्रोणः सूतपुत्रस्तथासौ सहास्मदीयैरपि योधमुख्यैः
english: All the sons of Dhritarashtra, with the hosts of kings of the earth, Bhishma, Drona and Karna, with the chief among our warriors.
brief_explanation: In this verse, Arjuna questions if Dhritarashtra's sons (including Bhishma, Drona, Karana, and warrior chiefs), despite being raised by others, are fighting with hosts of kings that are against them, even though Karna, although the son of Kunti, the mother of the Pandavas, was brought up as a charioteer's son.

speaker: Unknown
sanskrit: वक्त्राणि ते त्वरमाणा विशन्ति दंष्ट्राकरालानि भयानकानि | केचिद्विलग्ना दशनान्तरेषु सन्दृश्यन्ते चूर्णितैरुत्तमाङ्गैः
english: Some hurriedly enter Thy mouths with their terrible teeth, fearful to behold. Some are found sticking in the gaps between the teeth with their heads crushed to powder.
brief_explanation: The text describes fearsome creatures hurrying and entering the gap between terrible-toothed mouths, some of which stick there and are found crushed to powder along with their heads.

speaker: Unknown
sanskrit: यथा नदीनां बहवोऽम्बुवेगाः समुद्रमेवाभिमुखा द्रवन्ति | तथा तवामी नरलोकवीरा विशन्ति वक्त्राण्यभिविज्वलन्ति
english: Verily, just as many torrents of rivers flow towards the ocean, even so these heroes in the world of men enter Thy flaming mouths.
brief_explanation: These warriors, similar to numerous rivers flowing into one ocean, are now rushing towards death, their mouths flaming. Arjuna's delusion vanishes as he realizes this inevitable battle has the sanction of the Supreme Lord. He perceives himself as an instrument in the hands of the divine, free from sin, and serving a just cause.

speaker: Unknown
sanskrit: यथा प्रदीप्तं ज्वलनं पतङ्गा विशन्ति नाशाय समृद्धवेगाः | तथैव नाशाय विशन्ति लोकास्- तवापि वक्त्राणि समृद्धवेगाः
english: As moths hurriedly rush into a blazing fire for (their own) destruction, so also these creatures hurriedly rush into Thy mouths for (their own) destruction.
brief_explanation: The explanation is: Moths, drawn to a blazing fire, enter it quickly and are destroyed in the same way, creatures enter Thy mouths with increased speed. (Sivananda commentary)

speaker: Unknown
sanskrit: लेलिह्यसे ग्रसमानः समन्ताल्- लोकान्समग्रान्वदनैर्ज्वलद्भिः | तेजोभिरापूर्य जगत्समग्रं भासस्तवोग्राः प्रतपन्ति विष्णो
english: Thou lickest up, devouring all the worlds on every side with Thy flaming mouths. Thy fierce rays, filling the whole world with radiance, are burning, O Vishnu!
brief_explanation: Vishnu, as the all-pervading, is described as devouring the worlds on every side with flaming mouths and radiant power, filling the whole world and shining like rays, making them fierce and burning.

speaker: Unknown
sanskrit: आख्याहि मे को भवानुग्ररूपो नमोऽस्तु ते देववर प्रसीद | विज्ञातुमिच्छामि भवन्तमाद्यं न हि प्रजानामि तव प्रवृत्तिम्
english: Tell me, who Thou art, so fierce of form. Salutations to Thee, O God Supreme: have mercy. I desire to know Thee, the original Being. I know not indeed Thy working.
brief_explanation: The text is a prayer seeking to understand and be in the presence of the Supreme God, who is fierce in form. The speaker asks for mercy, wishes to know the original Being (Bhagavan) and acknowledges knowing Thy activities. No commentary is provided.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: श्रीभगवानुवाच | कालोऽस्मि लोकक्षयकृत्प्रवृद्धो लोकान्समाहर्तुमिह प्रवृत्तः | ऋतेऽपि त्वां न भविष्यन्ति सर्वे येऽवस्थिताः प्रत्यनीकेषु योधाः
english: The Blessed Lord said I am the full-grown world-destroying Time, now engaged in destroying the worlds. Even without thee, none of the warriors arrayed in the hostile armies shall live.
brief_explanation: The speaker, as Time itself, proclaims that these warriors are doomed to die in the war, regardless of Arjuna's participation. As the destroyer of worlds, they have already been slain by him. Thus, Arjuna's involvement is insignificant, and he should stand up to gain fame.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: तस्मात्त्वमुत्तिष्ठ यशो लभस्व जित्वा शत्रून् भुङ्क्ष्व राज्यं समृद्धम् | मयैवैते निहताः पूर्वमेव निमित्तमात्रं भव सव्यसाचिन्
english: Therefore, stand up and obtain fame. Coner the enemies and enjoy the unrivalled kingdom. Verily by Me have they been already slain; be thou a mere instrument, O Arjuna.
brief_explanation: Be an apparent cause, not the actual one; I've already defeated your enemies like Bhishma and Drona beforehand. Your fame will come from virtuous deeds. Enemies include Duryodhana.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: द्रोणं च भीष्मं च जयद्रथं च कर्णं तथान्यानपि योधवीरान् | मया हतांस्त्वं जहि मा व्यथिष्ठा युध्यस्व जेतासि रणे सपत्नान्
english: Drona, Bhishma, Jayadratha, Karna and other brave warriors these are already slain by Me: do thou kill; be not distressed with fear; fight and thou shalt coner thy enemies in battle.
brief_explanation: Drona, Bhishma, Jayadratha, Karna, and other brave warriors were previously slain by you, Arjuna. Therefore, you need not be distressed with fear about incurring sin by killing them again. Drona was your teacher in archery, while Bhishma had celestial weapons and could only die when he chose to.

speaker: Sanjaya
sanskrit: सञ्जय उवाच | एतच्छ्रुत्वा वचनं केशवस्य कृताञ्जलिर्वेपमानः किरीटी | नमस्कृत्वा भूय एवाह कृष्णं सगद्गदं भीतभीतः प्रणम्य
english: Sanjaya said Having heard that speech of Lord Krishna, Arjuna, with joined palms, trembling, prostrating himself, again addressed Krishna, in a choked voice, bowing down, overwhelmed with fear.
brief_explanation: Arjuna, overwhelmed with fear upon seeing the Cosmic Form, spoke in a choked voice. This indicates extreme terror or joy causing physical responses such as shedding tears and stammering. Sanjaya's words suggest a hope for peace between the Pandavas and Kauravas, but Dhritarashtra's obstinacy prevented this due to the force of destiny.

speaker: Arjuna
sanskrit: अर्जुन उवाच | स्थाने हृषीकेश तव प्रकीर्त्या जगत्प्रहृष्यत्यनुरज्यते च | रक्षांसि भीतानि दिशो द्रवन्ति सर्वे नमस्यन्ति च सिद्धसङ्घाः
english: Arjuna said It is meet, O Krishna, that the world delights and rejoices in Thy praise; demons fly in fear to all arters and the hosts of the perfected ones bow to Thee.
brief_explanation: The Lord, praised due to His glory as the Self and friend of all beings, is the object of adoration and delight. This is because He is the primordial cause, even for Brahma, the creator of the universe.

speaker: Unknown
sanskrit: कस्माच्च ते न नमेरन्महात्मन् गरीयसे ब्रह्मणोऽप्यादिकर्त्रे | अनन्त देवेश जगन्निवास त्वमक्षरं सदसत्तत्परं यत्
english: And why should they not, O great Soul, bow to Thee Who art greater (than all else), the primal cause even of the Creator (Brahma), O Infinite Being, O Lord of the gods, O Abode of the universe; Thou art the imperishable, the Being, the non-being and That which is the supreme (that which is beyond the Being and the non-being).
brief_explanation: The Lord is referred to as Mahatma, greater than all others. He is imperishable and the proper object of worship, love, and delight. Sat refers to what exists in the three periods of time, with Brahman being an example.

speaker: Unknown
sanskrit: त्वमादिदेवः पुरुषः पुराणस्- त्वमस्य विश्वस्य परं निधानम् | वेत्तासि वेद्यं च परं च धाम त्वया ततं विश्वमनन्तरूप
english: Thou art the primal God, the ancient Purusha, the supreme refuge of this universe, the knower, the knowable and the supreme Abode. By Thee is the universe pervaded, O Being of infinite forms.
brief_explanation: The primal God refers to the Lord as the creator of the universe (Purusha). He is also the supreme refuge (Nidhaanam) and Knower of all things (Vetta). As the material cause of the world, He is the Supreme Abode of Vishnu (Param Dhama), pervading the universe in infinite forms (Anantaroop).

speaker: Unknown
sanskrit: वायुर्यमोऽग्निर्वरुणः शशाङ्कः प्रजापतिस्त्वं प्रपितामहश्च | नमो नमस्तेऽस्तु सहस्रकृत्वः पुनश्च भूयोऽपि नमो नमस्ते
english: Thou art Vayu, Yama, Agni, Varuna, the moon, the Creator, and the great-grandfather. Salutations, salutations unto Thee, a thousand times, and again salutations, salutations unto Thee.
brief_explanation: Prajapati refers to Brahma, Marichi, Kasyapa, and others who are the mindborn sons of Brahma and the progenitors of various beings. Isvara is referred to as the greatgrandfather, being the cause for Brahma, and has Maya as the limiting adjunct in an undifferentiated state where the three Gunas (Brahma, Vishnu, Siva) manifest due to His will. Thou art the moon includes both the sun and signifies Arjuna's intense faith and boundless devotion towards Lord Krishna.

speaker: Unknown
sanskrit: नमः पुरस्तादथ पृष्ठतस्ते नमोऽस्तु ते सर्वत एव सर्व | अनन्तवीर्यामितविक्रमस्त्वं सर्वं समाप्नोषि ततोऽसि सर्वः
english: Salutations to Thee, in front and behind! Salutations to Thee on every side! O All!! Thou infinite in power and prowess, pervadest all; wherefore Thou art all.
brief_explanation: The salutation indicates the Lord's all-pervasive nature, as there are no front or back sides for the Self. Arjuna prostrated himself out of extreme faith and devotion, imagining the Lord to have such boundaries. All creation is pervaded by the Lord, who is infinite in power and courage.

speaker: Unknown
sanskrit: सखेति मत्वा प्रसभं यदुक्तं हे कृष्ण हे यादव हे सखेति | अजानता महिमानं तवेदं मया प्रमादात्प्रणयेन वापि
english: Whatever I have presumptuously said from carelessness or love, addressing Thee as O Krishna! O Yadava! O Friend! regarding Thee merely as a friend, unknowing of this, Thy greatness.
brief_explanation: Krishna, Yadava, friend - unknowingly presumptuously addressed you in this manner, O Krishna, out of carelessness or due to love, not knowing your greatness as I did this.

speaker: Unknown
sanskrit: यच्चावहासार्थमसत्कृतोऽसि विहारशय्यासनभोजनेषु | एकोऽथवाप्यच्युत तत्समक्षं तत्क्षामये त्वामहमप्रमेयम्
english: In whatever way I may have insulted Thee for the sake of fun, while at play, reposing, sitting or at meals, when alone (with Thee), O Krishna, or in company that I implore Thee, immeasurable one, to forgive.
brief_explanation: Arjuna admits his past disrespectful behavior towards Krishna, acknowledging his ignorance of Krishna's greatness. He feels he has treated Krishna as a friend due to misunderstanding, and apologizes for any inappropriate jokes or liberties taken. Despite Krishna being the creator of the universe, Arjuna admits to jesting with him, pleading for forgiveness.

speaker: Unknown
sanskrit: पितासि लोकस्य चराचरस्य त्वमस्य पूज्यश्च गुरुर्गरीयान् | न त्वत्समोऽस्त्यभ्यधिकः कुतोऽन्यो लोकत्रयेऽप्यप्रतिमप्रभाव
english: Thou art the Father of this world, moving and unmoving. Thou art to be adored by this world, Thou, the greatest Guru; (for) none there exists who is eal to Thee; how then could there be another superior to Thee in the three worlds, O Being of unealled power?
brief_explanation: The Lord, being the creator and sustainer of the world, is worthy of reverence as the supreme Guru. There is no equal to Him in any of the three worlds, making Him an unparalleled Being of immense power.

speaker: Unknown
sanskrit: तस्मात्प्रणम्य प्रणिधाय कायं प्रसादये त्वामहमीशमीड्यम् | पितेव पुत्रस्य सखेव सख्युः प्रियः प्रियायार्हसि देव सोढुम्
english: Therefore, bowing down, prostrating my body, I crave Thy forgiveness, O adorable Lord. As a father forgives his son, a friend his (dear) friend, a lover his beloved, even so shouldst Thou forgive me, O God.
brief_explanation: The passage suggests that, having recognized the Lord as the most adorable and beloved father (Arhasi Deva Sodhum), the devotee humbly salutes and bows before Him, seeking His forgiveness for any past mistakes or ignorance. In essence, the devotee requests to be embraced by the Lord like a child by its mother.

speaker: Unknown
sanskrit: अदृष्टपूर्वं हृषितोऽस्मि दृष्ट्वा भयेन च प्रव्यथितं मनो मे | तदेव मे दर्शय देव रूपं प्रसीद देवेश जगन्निवास
english: I am delighted, having seen what has never been seen before; and yet my mind is distressed with fear. Show me that (previous) form only, O God; have mercy, O God of gods, O Abode of the universe.
brief_explanation: The Cosmic Form, previously unseen by Arjuna, was overwhelming and terrifying for an ordinary man but uplifting and reassuring for a yogi. Arjuna requests to see only the divine form that God wears, acknowledging their friendship.

speaker: Unknown
sanskrit: किरीटिनं गदिनं चक्रहस्तं इच्छामि त्वां द्रष्टुमहं तथैव | तेनैव रूपेण चतुर्भुजेन सहस्रबाहो भव विश्वमूर्ते
english: I desire to see Thee as before, crowned, bearing a mace, with the discus in hand, in Thy former form only, having four arms, O thousand-armed, Cosmic Form (Being).
brief_explanation: Arjuna expresses fear and longing for the Universal Form, desiring to see God with specific attributes like a crown, mace, discus, and lotus. He seeks the same four-armed form as before instead of the cosmic one, suggesting impatience in spiritual pursuits. Patience is encouraged, as premature exposure to higher powers may be overwhelming.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: श्रीभगवानुवाच | मया प्रसन्नेन तवार्जुनेदं रूपं परं दर्शितमात्मयोगात् | तेजोमयं विश्वमनन्तमाद्यं यन्मे त्वदन्येन न दृष्टपूर्वम्
english: The Blessed Lord said O Arjuna, this Cosmic Form has graciously been shown to thee by Me by My own Yogic power; full of splendour, primeval, and infinite, this Cosmic Form of Mine has never been seen before by anyone other than thyself.
brief_explanation: The Cosmic Form, shown graciously to Arjuna by Krishna's own Yogic power, is supreme, full of splendour, universal, endless, primeval, and has not been seen before from anyone else, including Arjuna. This vision serves as a culmination of Arjuna's goals and an inspiration for spiritual aspirants. The Lord further explains the path to attain this vision in verses 53-55.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: न वेदयज्ञाध्ययनैर्न दानैर्- न च क्रियाभिर्न तपोभिरुग्रैः | एवंरूपः शक्य अहं नृलोके द्रष्टुं त्वदन्येन कुरुप्रवीर
english: Neither by the study of the Vedas and sacrifices, nor by gifts nor by rituals nor by severe austerities can I be seen in this form in the world of men by any other than thyself, O great hero of the Kurus (Arjuna).
brief_explanation: Study of Vedas, Yajnas, and understanding their meaning is necessary. Gifts like Tula Purusha, Kanyadana, gift of a cow, rice, etc., are forms of Dana. Rituals such as Agnihotra are Kriya.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: मा ते व्यथा मा च विमूढभावो दृष्ट्वा रूपं घोरमीदृङ्ममेदम् | व्यपेतभीः प्रीतमनाः पुनस्त्वं तदेव मे रूपमिदं प्रपश्य
english: Be not afraid, nor bewildered on seeing such a teriible form of Mine as this; with thy fear dispelled and with a gladdened heart, now behold again this former form of Mine.
brief_explanation: The Lord, who was previously in a terrifying cosmic form due to Arjuna's fear, returned to his original gentle form with four hands bearing a conch, discus, club or mace, and lotus. With the fear dispelled, Arjuna beheld the Lord again in his usual form.

speaker: Sanjaya
sanskrit: सञ्जय उवाच | इत्यर्जुनं वासुदेवस्तथोक्त्वा स्वकं रूपं दर्शयामास भूयः | आश्वासयामास च भीतमेनं भूत्वा पुनः सौम्यवपुर्महात्मा
english: Sanjaya said Having thus spoken to Arjuna, Krishna again showed His own form and the great Soul (Krishna), assuming His gentle form, consoled him (Arjuna) who was terrified.
brief_explanation: Arjuna refers to Arjuna, Vaasudeva refers to Vishnu. After speaking, Vishnu showed his divine form again to console Arjuna who was terrified upon becoming a great-souled being with a gentle form.

speaker: Arjuna
sanskrit: अर्जुन उवाच | दृष्ट्वेदं मानुषं रूपं तव सौम्यं जनार्दन | इदानीमस्मि संवृत्तः सचेताः प्रकृतिं गतः
english: Arjuna said Having seen this Thy gentle human form, O Krishna, now I am composed and am restored to my own nature.
brief_explanation: Arjuna perceives Krishna's human form and finds peace in his mind, ready to speak. His senses function properly, fear vanishes, and he feels loved like a child embraced by a mother. Just as a calf rejoices upon seeing its mother, Arjuna is elated by Krishna's gentle form.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: श्रीभगवानुवाच | सुदुर्दर्शमिदं रूपं दृष्टवानसि यन्मम | देवा अप्यस्य रूपस्य नित्यं दर्शनकाङ्क्षिणः
english: The Blessed Lord said Very hard indeed it is to see this form of Mine which thou hast seen. Even the gods are ever longing to behold it.
brief_explanation: The Cosmic Form, though desired by the gods, has never been seen by them as it was witnessed by Arjuna. This form is compared to a drop of rain longed for by a Chataka bird, which even the gods have not been able to behold in their dreams.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: नाहं वेदैर्न तपसा न दानेन न चेज्यया | शक्य एवंविधो द्रष्टुं दृष्टवानसि मां यथा
english: Neither by the Vedas nor by austerity, nor by gift, nor by sacrifice can I be seen in this form as thou hast seen Me (so easily).
brief_explanation: The Cosmic Form, which Arjuna has seen, cannot be attained through studying Vedas, various austerities, charity, or sacrifices. It requires a heart full of true devotion to the Lord.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: भक्त्या त्वनन्यया शक्य अहमेवंविधोऽर्जुन | ज्ञातुं द्रष्टुं च तत्त्वेन प्रवेष्टुं च परन्तप
english: But by single-minded devotion can I, of this Form, be known and seen in reality and also entered into, O Arjuna.
brief_explanation: Devotion, specifically singleminded devotion, is the means to realizing the Cosmic Form. This type of devotion eliminates egoism and dualism, as the devotee perceives only the Lord through all senses. One can not only know the Lord as described in scriptures but also realize Him, leading to liberation.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: मत्कर्मकृन्मत्परमो मद्भक्तः सङ्गवर्जितः | निर्वैरः सर्वभूतेषु यः स मामेति पाण्डव
english: He who does all actions for Me, who looks upon Me as the Supreme, who is devoted to Me, who is free from attachment, who bears enmity towards no creature, he comes to Me, O Arjuna.
brief_explanation: He who performs actions for the Lord, considers the Lord as supreme, is devoted to the Lord, is detached, has no enmity towards all creatures, is not attached to worldly possessions, and seeks only the Lord, realizes Him, and enters into His Being. This embodies the essence of the Gita's teachings leading to Supreme Bliss and Immortality.

speaker: Arjuna
sanskrit: अर्जुन उवाच | एवं सततयुक्ता ये भक्तास्त्वां पर्युपासते | ये चाप्यक्षरमव्यक्तं तेषां के योगवित्तमाः
english: Arjuna said Those devotees who, ever steadfast, thus worship Thee and those also who worship the imperishable and the unmanifested which of them are better versed in Yoga?
brief_explanation: The twelfth discourse emphasizes Bhakti Yoga as easier than Jnana Yoga, where devotees form a close relationship with the Lord through various attitudes like Santa, Dasya, Sakhya, Vatsalya, and Madhurya Bhava. Worship includes remembering, singing, speaking, repeating the Lord's name, praying, prostration, hearing His lilas, self-surrender, and eventual absorption in Him. Some worship idols, forms, or the all-pervading Brahman (Para Puja).

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: श्रीभगवानुवाच | मय्यावेश्य मनो ये मां नित्ययुक्ता उपासते | श्रद्धया परयोपेताः ते मे युक्ततमा मताः
english: The Blessed Lord said Those who, fixing their mind on Me, worship Me, ever steadfast and endowed with supreme faith, are the best in Yoga in My opinion.
brief_explanation: Devotees fixing their minds on the Cosmic Form of the Supreme Lord, worshipping with intense and supreme faith, and who are free from attachments - these, in Your opinion, are the best versed in Yoga. They spend their days and nights in worshipping You alone. Therefore, it is proper to say that they are the best Yogins.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: ये त्वक्षरमनिर्देश्यमव्यक्तं पर्युपासते | सर्वत्रगमचिन्त्यञ्च कूटस्थमचलन्ध्रुवम्
english: Swami Sivananda did not comment on this sloka
brief_explanation: Explanation of Sloka is not available in the provided Sivananda commentary text.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: सन्नियम्येन्द्रियग्रामं सर्वत्र समबुद्धयः | ते प्राप्नुवन्ति मामेव सर्वभूतहिते रताः
english: Having restrained all the senses, even-minded everywhere, intent on the welfare of all beings verily they also come unto Me.
brief_explanation: Those who restrain their senses everywhere and have an even mind, rejoicing in the welfare of all beings, obtain Me alone. By controlling the senses and focusing on the inner Self, those who meditate on the transcendental Brahman also come to Me.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: क्लेशोऽधिकतरस्तेषामव्यक्तासक्तचेतसाम् | अव्यक्ता हि गतिर्दुःखं देहवद्भिरवाप्यते
english: Greater is their trouble whose minds are set on the unmanifested; for the goal; the unmanifested, is very hard for the embodied to reach.
brief_explanation: The trouble for those with a strong attachment to the body is greater when seeking the unmanifested, attributeless Brahman. This path is challenging because it requires detachment from the physical form, a sharp intellect, and the four means: hearing from a learned Guru, reflection, meditation, and realization. Those who realize the Nirguna (attributeless) Brahman attain eternal bliss or self-realization, while those who worship the Saguna (alified) Brahman go to Brahmaloka and enjoy divine wealth and powers.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: ये तु सर्वाणि कर्माणि मयि संन्यस्य मत्परः | अनन्येनैव योगेन मां ध्यायन्त उपासते
english: But to those who worship Me, renouncing all actions in Me, regarding Me as the supreme gaol, meditating on Me with single-minded Yoga.
brief_explanation: Ananya Yoga refers to exclusive devotion where the practitioner has no other objects of worship or support apart from the Lord. In this state, one performs actions but dedicates their merits or fruits to the Lord. This is emphasized in both Jnana and Bhakti yoga (Cf.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: तेषामहं समुद्धर्ता मृत्युसंसारसागरात् | भवामि नचिरात्पार्थ मय्यावेशितचेतसाम्
english: To those whose minds are set on Me, O Arjuna, verily I become ere long the saviour out of the ocean of Samsara.
brief_explanation: The Lord is referred to as the savior for those who have unified their minds with Him, as He will soon lift them out of the cycle of birth and death (mortal Samsara). This redemption occurs without delay when a person surrenders completely to the Lord and abandons the idea of liberation.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: मय्येव मन आधत्स्व मयि बुद्धिं निवेशय | निवसिष्यसि मय्येव अत ऊर्ध्वं न संशयः
english: Fix thy mind in Me only, thy intellect in Me, (then) thou shalt no doubt live in Me alone hereafter.
brief_explanation: The verse indicates that one should fix their mind, thoughts, and intellect solely on the Lord in the Cosmic Form to eliminate desires for sensual objects. This will result in living within the Lord, with no doubt about it. This verse presents the practice of meditation in Bhagavad Gita.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: अथ चित्तं समाधातुं न शक्नोषि मयि स्थिरम् | अभ्यासयोगेन ततो मामिच्छाप्तुं धनञ्जय
english: If thou art unable to fix thy mind steadily on Me, then by the Yoga of constant practice do thou seek to reach Me, O Arjuna.
brief_explanation: Abhyasa Yoga refers to the practice of constantly focusing the mind on a single point, whether an object or the Self. It involves repeated withdrawal from sensual objects and identification with the Atman. If one cannot fix the mind on the Lord at all times, they should do so for as much time as possible.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: अभ्यासेऽप्यसमर्थोऽसि मत्कर्मपरमो भव | मदर्थमपि कर्माणि कुर्वन्सिद्धिमवाप्स्यसि
english: If thou art unable to practise even this Abhyasa Yoga, be thou intent on doing actions for My sake; even by doing actions for My sake, thou shalt attain perfection.
brief_explanation: Even if you perform actions for the Lord without practicing yoga, you will still attain perfection. This involves achieving purity of mind, concentration, knowledge, and ultimately liberation. Serving humanity with a sense of serving the Lord is also considered doing actions for the Lord.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: अथैतदप्यशक्तोऽसि कर्तुं मद्योगमाश्रितः | सर्वकर्मफलत्यागं ततः कुरु यतात्मवान्
english: If thou art unable to do even this, then, resorting to union with Me, renounce the fruits of all actions with the self controlled.
brief_explanation: The easiest path is described when one cannot perform actions for the Lord or practice Bhagavata Dharmas, instead resorting to My Yoga (surrendering all actions and their fruits to Me). A self-controlled individual should do actions while renouncing them all in the Lord and abandon the fruits of all actions. This verse eulogizes the renunciation of action's fruits to motivate aspirants towards the practice of the Yoga of such renunciation.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: श्रेयो हि ज्ञानमभ्यासाज्ज्ञानाद्ध्यानं विशिष्यते | ध्यानात्कर्मफलत्यागस्त्यागाच्छान्तिरनन्तरम्
english: Better indeed is knowledge than practice; than knowledge meditation is better; than meditation the renunciation of the fruits of actions: peace immediately follows renunciation.
brief_explanation: Knowledge gained from practice excels theoretical knowledge. Meditation surpasses knowledge. Renunciation of action's fruits exceeds meditation, leading directly to peace.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: अद्वेष्टा सर्वभूतानां मैत्रः करुण एव च | निर्ममो निरहङ्कारः समदुःखसुखः क्षमी
english: He who hates no creature, who is friendly and compassionate to all, who is free from attachment and egoism, balanced in pleasure and pain, and forgiving.
brief_explanation: The Bhagavata, or sage, is friendly, compassionate, and impartial towards all creatures. They are merciful, offering security to all beings, resembling a sun that shines on every dwelling. Mineness and egoism do not exist in their mind, as they are indifferent to pleasure and pain.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: सन्तुष्टः सततं योगी यतात्मा दृढनिश्चयः | मय्यर्पितमनोबुद्धिर्यो मद्भक्तः स मे प्रियः
english: Ever content, steady in meditation, self-controlled, possessed of firm conviction, with the mind and intellect dedicated to Me, he, My devtoee, is dear to Me.
brief_explanation: The Yogi is contented at all times, as they understand their current state is a result of past actions. They do not seek temporary or perishable objects. Their mind and intellect are dedicated to the Supreme Being.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: यस्मान्नोद्विजते लोको लोकान्नोद्विजते च यः | हर्षामर्षभयोद्वेगैर्मुक्तो यः स च मे प्रियः
english: He by whom the world is not agitated and who cannot be agitated by the world, and who is freed from joy, anger, fear and anxiety he is dear to Me.
brief_explanation: The passage describes a person who has attained liberation (muktah) - one who is not affected by joy, wrath, fear, and anxiety (harsa, marshana, bhaya, udvega). This individual does not harm any creature in thought, word, or deed and provides security to all beings. Due to this, no creature fears him.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: अनपेक्षः शुचिर्दक्ष उदासीनो गतव्यथः | सर्वारम्भपरित्यागी यो मद्भक्तः स मे प्रियः
english: He who is free from wants, pure, expert, unconcerned, and free from pain, renouncing all undertakings or commencements he who is (thus) devoted to Me, is dear to Me.
brief_explanation: Free from dependence, indifferent to body, senses, and their connections, with external and internal purity achieved through washing, bathing, and eradicating likes/dislikes/lust/anger/jealousy while cultivating friendship, compassion, and complacency towards others. Expert in all actions, swift and skilled in decision-making, indifferent to controversies, free from pain, and habitually renouncing all actions calculated for enjoyment. Such a devotee has merged their will with the cosmic will, allowing divine will to work through them, without preference or personal desire.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: यो न हृष्यति न द्वेष्टि न शोचति न काङ्क्षति | शुभाशुभपरित्यागी भक्तिमान्यः स मे प्रियः
english: He who neither rejoices, nor hates, nor grieves, nor desires, renouncing good and evil, and who is full of devotion, is dear to Me.
brief_explanation: The individual who does not rejoice over desirable objects, does not hate undesirable ones, does not grieve over parted beloved objects, and does not desire unattained ones, is a renouncer of both good and evil actions (Subhasubhaparityagi). This type of devotee, who has knowledge of the Self as the Lord's own Self, is dear to Me. (Cf.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: समः शत्रौ च मित्रे च तथा मानापमानयोः | शीतोष्णसुखदुःखेषु समः सङ्गविवर्जितः
english: Swami Sivananda did not comment on this sloka
brief_explanation: No comment provided by Swami Sivananda for the given sloka.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: तुल्यनिन्दास्तुतिर्मौनी सन्तुष्टो येन केनचित् | अनिकेतः स्थिरमतिर्भक्तिमान्मे प्रियो नरः
english: He to whom censure and praise are eal, who is silent, content with anything, homeless, of a steady mind, and full of devotion that man is dear to Me.
brief_explanation: The individual who remains unaffected by praise or censure, maintains a steady mind, and practices silence both in speech and thought, is content with the bare essentials of life, and has no fixed abode, is considered dear to Me (God). Such an individual, according to the Mahabharata, is regarded as a Brahmana, liberated sage, or Jivanmukta by the gods.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: ये तु धर्म्यामृतमिदं यथोक्तं पर्युपासते | श्रद्दधाना मत्परमा भक्तास्तेऽतीव मे प्रियाः
english: They verily who follow this immortal Dharma (law or doctrine) as described above, endowed with faith, regarding Me as their supreme goal, they, the devotees, are exceedingly dear to Me.
brief_explanation: The Blessed Lord's description of a devoted follower: They are endowed with faith, regarding Him as their supreme refuge, and practicing immortal Dharma (Law) as declared above. These devotees become exceedingly dear to the Lord. Therefore, every aspirant seeking salvation should follow this immortal Dharma with intense faith.

speaker: Arjuna
sanskrit: अर्जुन उवाच | प्रकृतिं पुरुषं चैव क्षेत्रं क्षेत्रज्ञमेव च | एतद्वेदितुमिच्छामि ज्ञानं ज्ञेयं च केशव
english: Arjuna said I wish to learn about Nature (matter) and the Spirit (soul), the field and the knower of the field, knowledge and that which ought to be known, O Kesava.
brief_explanation: The verse discusses the beginning of the third section, focusing on understanding the nature of the possessor of two Prakritis (Natures), described in Chapter VII verses 4 and 5. This discourse aims to explain what kind of knowledge of Truth should a devotee possess. Nature is composed of three qualities and transforms into body, senses, and objects for individual soul's purposes: enjoyment and liberation.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: श्रीभगवानुवाच | इदं शरीरं कौन्तेय क्षेत्रमित्यभिधीयते | एतद्यो वेत्ति तं प्राहुः क्षेत्रज्ञ इति तद्विदः
english: The Blessed Lord said This body, O Arjuna, is called the field; he who knows it is called the knower of the field, by those who know of them.
brief_explanation: The term "Kshetra" refers to the field, which encompasses the physical, mental, and causal bodies. It's called so because pleasures and pains, the fruits of actions, are reaped in it, like a harvest in a field. The one who knows and perceives the field as distinct from himself is known as the "Kshetrajna" or the knower of the field.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: क्षेत्रज्ञं चापि मां विद्धि सर्वक्षेत्रेषु भारत | क्षेत्रक्षेत्रज्ञयोर्ज्ञानं यत्तज्ज्ञानं मतं मम
english: Do thou also know Me as the knower of the field in all fields, O Arjuna. Knowledge of both the field and the knower of the field is considered by Me to be ï1the ï1 knowledge.
brief_explanation: The knower of the field is one, existing in all fields. This one knowledge is considered to be mine. Individual souls are different but the Supreme Soul is eternal and free from pleasure and pain, not bound to Samsara.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: तत्क्षेत्रं यच्च यादृक्च यद्विकारि यतश्च यत् | स च यो यत्प्रभावश्च तत्समासेन मे शृणु
english: What the field is and of what nature, what are its modifications and whence it is and also who He is and what His powers are hear all that from Me in brief.
brief_explanation: The body is referred to as the field, with the ten senses acting as the ten bulls. The mind serves as the supervisor, while the individual soul is the tenant. The five vital airs are the laborers.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: ऋषिभिर्बहुधा गीतं छन्दोभिर्विविधैः पृथक् | ब्रह्मसूत्रपदैश्चैव हेतुमद्भिर्विनिश्चितैः
english: Sages have sung in many ways, in various distinctive chants and also in the suggestive words indicative of the Absolute, full of reasoning and decisive.
brief_explanation: The Bhagavad Gita was sung by many Rishis in various ways, including through chants, distinct from each other. It has been explained using suggestive words indicative of Brahman, found in the Brahma Sutras. These sutras, also known as Sariraka Sutras, deal with the true nature of the field and its knower, offering reasoning, conviction, and decisiveness.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: महाभूतान्यहंकारो बुद्धिरव्यक्तमेव च | इन्द्रियाणि दशैकं च पञ्च चेन्द्रियगोचराः
english: The great elements, egoism, intellect, and also the Unmanifested Nature, the ten senses and one (mind), and the five objects of the senses.
brief_explanation: The verse describes the twenty-four principles of Sankhya philosophy, including the great elements (Earth, water, fire, air, and ether), egoism, intellect, and senses. The mind is the eleventh sense, responsible for thinking and doubting. The five objects of the senses are sound, touch, form, taste, and smell.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: इच्छा द्वेषः सुखं दुःखं संघातश्चेतना धृतिः | एतत्क्षेत्रं समासेन सविकारमुदाहृतम्
english: Desire, hatred, pleasure, pain, the aggregate (the body), intelligence, fortitude the field has thus been briefly described with its modifications.
brief_explanation: Desires, hatreds, pleasures, pains, aggregates, intelligence, fortitude are mental states forming the foundation of the world of forms. They are treated as properties of the Self by various schools of thought, and are described as modifications with a beginning and end. The unchanging knower of these modifications is the witness of the field and its changes.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: अमानित्वमदम्भित्वमहिंसा क्षान्तिरार्जवम् | आचार्योपासनं शौचं स्थैर्यमात्मविनिग्रहः
english: Humility, unpretentiousness, non-injury, forgiveness, uprightness, service of the teacher, purity, steadfastness, self-control.
brief_explanation: Humility is the absence of self-esteem or self-praise, negating vanity. A humble person dislikes respect, honor, and praise, shuns fame, and never praises themselves. Noninjury, Ahimsa, involves not causing harm to any living being in thought, word, or deed, and avoiding stepping on any living creature.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: इन्द्रियार्थेषु वैराग्यमनहंकार एव च | जन्ममृत्युजराव्याधिदुःखदोषानुदर्शनम्
english: Indifference to the objects of the senses and also absence of egoism; perception of (or reflection on) the evil in birth, death, old age, sickness and pain.
brief_explanation: The man of wisdom exhibits constant indifference toward sense objects, avoiding even discussion about them. This dispassion (vairagya) and absence of egoism (anahankara) are cultivated through contemplation on the evils of birth, old age, sickness, and pain. Reflection on these miseries leads to an aversion for bodily and sensual pleasures, guiding the mind toward self-realization.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: असक्तिरनभिष्वङ्गः पुत्रदारगृहादिषु | नित्यं च समचित्तत्वमिष्टानिष्टोपपत्तिषु
english: Non-attachment, non-identification of the Self with son, wife, home and the rest, and constant even-mindedness on the attainment of the desirable and the undesirable.
brief_explanation: Nonattachment (Asakti) refers to a lack of attachment to objects, characterized by an absence of liking for them. Nonidentification of the Self (Anabhishvangah) is a state where one does not fully identify with others like family members, feeling only happiness or sorrow when directly connected to them. Constant evenmindedness (Samachittatvam) is a steadiness that indicates wisdom and is demonstrated by remaining unaffected by the attainment of desirable or undesirable circumstances.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: मयि चानन्ययोगेन भक्तिरव्यभिचारिणी | विविक्तदेशसेवित्वमरतिर्जनसंसदि
english: Unswerving devotion unto Me by the Yoga of non-separation, resort to solitary places, distaste for the society of men.
brief_explanation: The man of wisdom firmly believes in the supremacy of Me (God) as his sole refuge, practicing unswerving devotion without thoughts for other objects, merging his mind into Me through Yoga of nonseparation. He lives in solitary places to maintain mental peace and avoid distractions. He shows distaste towards society of worldly-minded people but seeks association with the wise as a means to attain Self-knowledge.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: अध्यात्मज्ञाननित्यत्वं तत्त्वज्ञानार्थदर्शनम् | एतज्ज्ञानमिति प्रोक्तमज्ञानं यदतोऽन्यथा
english: Constancy in Self-knowledge, perception of the end of true knowledge this is declared to be knowledge, and what is opposed to it is ignorance.
brief_explanation: The liberated sage maintains constant awareness of Self-knowledge, recognizing it as the only permanent truth amidst all worldly learning, which is considered ignorance. The aspirant should focus on developing virtues conducive to Self-knowledge, as they are declared to be forms of knowledge due to their supporting role. Conversely, traits like lust, anger, greed, pride, hypocrisy, attachment, cunningness, diplomacy, and harming others represent ignorance and hinder salvation.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: ज्ञेयं यत्तत्प्रवक्ष्यामि यज्ज्ञात्वामृतमश्नुते | अनादिमत्परं ब्रह्म न सत्तन्नासदुच्यते
english: I will declare that which has to be known, knowing which one attains to immortality, the beginningless supreme Brahman, called neither being nor non-being.
brief_explanation: The Lord praises Brahman, which should be deeply understood to spark desire in Arjuna or listeners. Brahman transcends being or nonbeing, as it's not associated with any class, genus, or attributes. It's beyond the reach of mind and senses, actionless, and the great transcendental Absolute.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: सर्वतः पाणिपादं तत्सर्वतोऽक्षिशिरोमुखम् | सर्वतः श्रुतिमल्लोके सर्वमावृत्य तिष्ठति
english: With hands and feet everywhere, with eyes, heads and mouths everywhere, with ears everywhere, He exists in the worlds enveloping all.
brief_explanation: The knowable Brahman pervades everything in this world, filling and surrounding it completely. This affirmation refutes the misconception that Brahman is non-existent. It also suggests that the body, mind, senses, and lifeforce are moved by Brahman to action, despite being inherently insentient.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: सर्वेन्द्रियगुणाभासं सर्वेन्द्रियविवर्जितम् | असक्तं सर्वभृच्चैव निर्गुणं गुणभोक्तृ च
english: Shining by the functions of all the senses, yet without the senses; unattached, yet supporting all; devoid of alities, yet their experiencer.
brief_explanation: The verse describes Brahman as beyond the senses but still supporting them, being unattached yet experiencing the functions of all senses. It also implies that Brahman is the unseen seer, unheard hearer, and unthought thinker, transcending the need for physical senses. The term "all the senses" includes both the organs of action and knowledge, as well as the mind and intellect.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: बहिरन्तश्च भूतानामचरं चरमेव च | सूक्ष्मत्वात्तदविज्ञेयं दूरस्थं चान्तिके च तत्
english: Without and within (all) beings the unmoving and also the moving; because of Its subtlety, unknowable; and near and far away is That.
brief_explanation: Brahman, being extremely subtle like ether, is hard to comprehend for the unenlightened due to its subtlety. It is unknowable to those without the four means of salvation. For the wise, however, it is near as it is their very Self.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: अविभक्तं च भूतेषु विभक्तमिव च स्थितम् | भूतभर्तृ च तज्ज्ञेयं ग्रसिष्णु प्रभविष्णु च
english: And undivided, yet It exists as if divided in beings; It is to be known as the supporter of being; It devours and It generates.
brief_explanation: The commentary explains that Brahman, the supreme reality, supports, generates, and destroys all beings in three forms: Brahma (creator), Vishnu (preserver), and Rudra (destroyer). Although it appears to be divided among various beings, it is indivisible and all-pervading, like ether or space. Just as fire is hidden within wood, Brahman is hidden in all bodies.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: ज्योतिषामपि तज्ज्योतिस्तमसः परमुच्यते | ज्ञानं ज्ञेयं ज्ञानगम्यं हृदि सर्वस्य विष्ठितम्
english: That, the Light of all lights, is said to be beyond darkness: knowledge, the knowable and the goal of knowledge, seated in the hearts of all.
brief_explanation: The supreme Self, beyond darkness, is referred to as light. This light is knowledge that can be attained and is seated in the heart of all beings. This light illuminates the intellect, mind, sun, moon, stars, fire, and lightning, making everything shine after it.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: इति क्षेत्रं तथा ज्ञानं ज्ञेयं चोक्तं समासतः | मद्भक्त एतद्विज्ञाय मद्भावायोपपद्यते
english: Thus the field, as well as knowledge and the knowable have been briefly stated. My devotee, knowing this, enters into My Being.
brief_explanation: The field (kshetram) and knowledge (jnana) along with the knowable have been briefly stated, including one's own self as the Supreme Lord (Madbhakta). When this devotee understands these concepts and fixes his mind on the Lord, he enters into the Lord's Being or attains liberation from the cycle of birth and death.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: प्रकृतिं पुरुषं चैव विद्ध्यनादी उभावपि | विकारांश्च गुणांश्चैव विद्धि प्रकृतिसम्भवान्
english: Know thou that Nature (matter) and the Spirit are both beginningless; and know also that all modifications and alities are born of Nature.
brief_explanation: The Prakriti (matter) and Purusha (spirit) are both necessary and inseparable. They are beginingless and even modifications and alities come from Prakriti. Lord Krishna teaches Arjuna about them step by step, like a mother feeding a child.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: कार्यकारणकर्तृत्वे हेतुः प्रकृतिरुच्यते | पुरुषः सुखदुःखानां भोक्तृत्वे हेतुरुच्यते
english: In the production of the effect and the cause, Nature (matter) is said to be the cause; in the experience of pleasure and pain, the soul is said to be the cause.
brief_explanation: The verse describes Prakriti as the cause for the production of effects, such as physical bodies and experiences of pleasure and pain. Nature, including the five elements, senses, and their sensations, generates these effects. Purusha is said to be the enjoyer of these effects, just as a person enjoys the fruits of another's labor.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: पुरुषः प्रकृतिस्थो हि भुङ्क्ते प्रकृतिजान्गुणान् | कारणं गुणसङ्गोऽस्य सदसद्योनिजन्मसु
english: The soul seated in Nature experiences the alities born of Nature; attachment to the alities is the cause of its birth in good and evil wombs.
brief_explanation: The soul, residing in Nature, identifies with the body and senses, causing it to act through the alities of Nature and experience pleasure, pain, and delusion. This attachment to the alities is the cause of its birth in good and evil wombs, leading to Samsara (the cycle of rebirth).

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: उपद्रष्टानुमन्ता च भर्ता भोक्ता महेश्वरः | परमात्मेति चाप्युक्तो देहेऽस्मिन्पुरुषः परः
english: The Supreme Soul in this body is also called the spectator, the permitter, the supporter, the enjoyer, the great Lord and the Supreme Self.
brief_explanation: Upadrashta: A silent witness, a bystander who guides but does not participate. Anumanta: The Supreme Self gives consent or approval for the actions performed by senses, mind, and intellect. Bharta: The Self as the supporter of the body, mind, intellect, life force, and senses.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: य एवं वेत्ति पुरुषं प्रकृतिं च गुणैः सह | सर्वथा वर्तमानोऽपि न स भूयोऽभिजायते
english: He who thus knows the Spirit and Matter together with the alities, in whatever condition he may be, he is not born again.
brief_explanation: The one who understands the Soul and Nature along with its qualities, regardless of their actions, frees themselves from the cycle of births and deaths due to gaining discriminative knowledge of Spirit and Matter. They know they are eternal and unchanging while all changes come from Nature's modifications. Even in various conditions, whether engaged in prescribed or forbidden acts, one who knows Spirit and Matter is not reborn as their actions, burnt by the fire of self-knowledge, no longer produce new bodies or further births.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: ध्यानेनात्मनि पश्यन्ति केचिदात्मानमात्मना | अन्ये साङ्ख्येन योगेन कर्मयोगेन चापरे
english: Some by meditation behold the Self in the self by the self, others by the Yoga of knowledge, and still others by the Yoga of action.
brief_explanation: The Bhagavad Gita outlines multiple paths to self-realization, catering to an individual's nature and capacity. 1. Yoga of meditation, as taught by Patanjali, involves continuous thought of the Self, leading to the mind's withdrawal from sensory objects and its eventual abiding in the Self.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: अन्ये त्वेवमजानन्तः श्रुत्वान्येभ्य उपासते | तेऽपि चातितरन्त्येव मृत्युं श्रुतिपरायणाः
english: Others also, not knowing thus, worship, having heard of It from others; they, too, cross beyond death, regarding what they have heard as the Supreme refuge.
brief_explanation: The verse describes the Yoga of worship, where individuals, unaware of other methods, listen to and follow teachings about the Self from spiritual preceptors or scriptures, eventually achieving knowledge of the Self and liberation. This path is suitable for various temperaments and abilities. Crossing Samsara (the cycle of birth and death) is equivalent to attaining immortality, overcoming death, or obtaining release/salvation.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: यावत्सञ्जायते किञ्चित्सत्त्वं स्थावरजङ्गमम् | क्षेत्रक्षेत्रज्ञसंयोगात्तद्विद्धि भरतर्षभ
english: Wherever a being is born, whether unmoving or moving, know thou, O best of the Bharatas (Arjuna), that it is from the union between the field and its knower.
brief_explanation: The union between the body (field) and the Self (knower of the field) is not physical but illusory, arising from superimposition where attributes are mistakenly attributed to each other. This illusion will dissolve upon realizing the true nature of the Self as immortal and independent from limiting adjuncts, leading to liberation and reincarnation's avoidance.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: समं सर्वेषु भूतेषु तिष्ठन्तं परमेश्वरम् | विनश्यत्स्वविनश्यन्तं यः पश्यति स पश्यति
english: He sees, who sees the Supreme Lord, existing eally in all beings, the unperishing within the perishing.
brief_explanation: The text describes a realized soul as one who perceives the Supreme Lord, present in all beings, as the same entity that remains undestroyed amidst the perishing world. This realization occurs when one recognizes the indivisible Self, which is the same in all living entities regardless of form or state. The text also suggests that true perception arises from wisdom and distinguishes between those with proper vision who see the One Self and those with defective vision who see multiple selves erroneously.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: समं पश्यन्हि सर्वत्र समवस्थितमीश्वरम् | न हिनस्त्यात्मनात्मानं ततो याति परां गतिम्
english: Because he who sees the same Lord eally dwelling everywhere does not destroy the Self by the self; he goes to the highest goal.
brief_explanation: The vision of a liberated sage is the realization that the Supreme Self dwells everywhere, with nothing existing beyond it. An ignorant man, identifying himself with the body and mind, destroys his own Self through false knowledge. However, the sage, possessing true knowledge, perceives the one Self in all beings.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: प्रकृत्यैव च कर्माणि क्रियमाणानि सर्वशः | यः पश्यति तथात्मानमकर्तारं स पश्यति
english: He sees, who sees that all actions are performed by Nature alone and that the Self is actionless.
brief_explanation: The passage explains that Nature is responsible for all actions, and the Self is beyond action, serving as a silent witness. One who understands this perspective is considered a real seer or sage. Identifying oneself with the body or mind leads to ignorance, as the Self is actionless while Nature performs everything.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: यदा भूतपृथग्भावमेकस्थमनुपश्यति | तत एव च विस्तारं ब्रह्म सम्पद्यते तदा
english: When a man sees the whole variety of beings as resting in the One, and spreading forth from That alone, he then becomes Brahman.
brief_explanation: The man attains unity with the Supreme when he realizes through intuition that all beings are rooted in the One, comparable to waves in water, atoms in earth, etc. When he perceives diversity as one Self, he experiences the bliss of Self. This aligns with the Chhandogya Upanishad 7.26.1, where it is stated that life, desire, love, ether, light, waters, appearance, and disappearance are all from the Self.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: अनादित्वान्निर्गुणत्वात्परमात्मायमव्ययः | शरीरस्थोऽपि कौन्तेय न करोति न लिप्यते
english: Being without beginning and being devoid of (any) alities, the Supreme Self, imperishable, though dwelling in the body, O Arjuna, neither acts nor is tainted.
brief_explanation: The Supreme Self, being without a beginning and devoid of alities, is imperishable and dwells in the body. Despite this, it does not act or get tainted by the fruits of action as it is beyond the functions of Nature. It transcends the three types of differences: Sajatiyabheda, Vijatiyabheda, and Svagatabheda, making it indivisible and partless.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: यथा सर्वगतं सौक्ष्म्यादाकाशं नोपलिप्यते | सर्वत्रावस्थितो देहे तथात्मा नोपलिप्यते
english: As the all-pervading ether is not tainted, because of its subtlety, so the Self seated everywhere in the body is not tainted.
brief_explanation: The Self, like ether, pervades everywhere in the body and world due to its subtle nature. Despite this, it remains uncontaminated by anything, illustrating that the Self is pure and untouched by actions, virtuous or vicious.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: यथा प्रकाशयत्येकः कृत्स्नं लोकमिमं रविः | क्षेत्रं क्षेत्री तथा कृत्स्नं प्रकाशयति भारत
english: Just as the one sun illumines the whole world, so also the Lord of the field (Supreme Self) illumines the whole field, O Arjuna.
brief_explanation: The Supreme Self, like the sun, illuminates everything from the smallest blade of grass to the largest element, and it is untainted by any worldly contamination.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: क्षेत्रक्षेत्रज्ञयोरेवमन्तरं ज्ञानचक्षुषा | भूतप्रकृतिमोक्षं च ये विदुर्यान्ति ते परम्
english: They who, by the eye of knowledge, perceive the distinction between the field and its knower and also the liberation from the Nature of being, go to the Supreme.
brief_explanation: The text discusses the distinction between Kshetra (field or body) and Kshetrajna (knower of the field or Self). Those who perceive through the eye of intuition that the Self is pure consciousness, unchanging, and infinite, while the doer and the field are changing and finite, and who also understand the nonexistence of Nature (Prakriti), attain the Supreme. This realization liberates them from the influence of Maya (delusion) and grants Kaivalya Moksha, where they no longer take birth again.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: श्रीभगवानुवाच | परं भूयः प्रवक्ष्यामि ज्ञानानां ज्ञानमुत्तमम् | यज्ज्ञात्वा मुनयः सर्वे परां सिद्धिमितो गताः
english: The Blessed Lord said I will again declare (to thee) that supreme knowledge, the best of all knowledge, having known which all the sages have gone to the supreme perfection after this life.
brief_explanation: The verse discusses the best knowledge that leads to liberation, which surpasses the knowledge of sacrifices. All sages who understood this supreme knowledge achieved perfection and were freed from their physical bondage after this life.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: इदं ज्ञानमुपाश्रित्य मम साधर्म्यमागताः | सर्गेऽपि नोपजायन्ते प्रलये न व्यथन्ति च
english: They who, having taken refuge in this knowledge, have attained to unity with Me, are neither born at the time of creation nor are they disturbed at the time of dissolution.
brief_explanation: The sages, after taking refuge in knowledge, attain unity with the Lord and become identical with Him. At creation and dissolution, they neither are born nor die; instead, they achieve eternal and perfect existence by identifying with the Lord through the practice of self-knowledge.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: मम योनिर्महद् ब्रह्म तस्मिन्गर्भं दधाम्यहम् | सम्भवः सर्वभूतानां ततो भवति भारत
english: My womb is the great Brahma; in that I place the germ; thence, O Arjuna, is the birth of all beings.
brief_explanation: The great Brahma, or Nature, is the source and material cause of all beings. It is called the great Brahma because through it the whole manifestation takes place. The primordial nature is like a clay, giving birth to the Creator (Hiranyagarbha) who then creates all beings.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: सर्वयोनिषु कौन्तेय मूर्तयः सम्भवन्ति याः | तासां ब्रह्म महद्योनिरहं बीजप्रदः पिता
english: Whatever forms are produced, O Arjuna, in any womb whatsoever, the great Brahma is their womb and I am the seed-giving father.
brief_explanation: The Primordial Nature is the mother, and I am the father of all forms (bodies consisting of parts, limbs, organs, etc.) that appear in various species such as gods, men, cattle, beasts, birds, etc.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: सत्त्वं रजस्तम इति गुणाः प्रकृतिसम्भवाः | निबध्नन्ति महाबाहो देहे देहिनमव्ययम्
english: Purity, passion and inertia these alities, O Arjuna, born of Nature, bind fast in the body, the embodied, the indestructible.
brief_explanation: The Guna (aliity) refers to the three primary constituents of Nature: Sattva, Rajas, and Tamas. They manifest as purity, passion, and inertia respectively. These alities bind the embodied individual soul, causing attachment and delusion, limiting its freedom from Samsara (cycle of birth and death).

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: तत्र सत्त्वं निर्मलत्वात्प्रकाशकमनामयम् | सुखसङ्गेन बध्नाति ज्ञानसङ्गेन चानघ
english: Of these, Sattva, which from its stainlessness is luminous and healthy, binds by attachment to happiness and by attachment to knowledge, O sinless one.
brief_explanation: The purity or stainlessness of Sattva (one of the three gunas) can be likened to a crystal, drawing one towards happiness and knowledge, acting as a golden fetter. A Sattvic individual compares themselves with others, finds pride in superiority, and is bound by attachment to their knowledge and happiness, which are illusions and ignorance. Knowledge belongs to the inner instrument (Antahkarana) rather than the Self, and cannot produce bondage if it were an attribute of the Self.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: रजो रागात्मकं विद्धि तृष्णासङ्गसमुद्भवम् | तन्निबध्नाति कौन्तेय कर्मसङ्गेन देहिनम्
english: Know thou Rajas to be of the nature of passion, the source of thirst (for sensual enjoyment) and attachment; it binds fast, O Arjuna, the embodied one by attachment to action.
brief_explanation: Rajas is the embodiment of passion, characterized by activity, ambition, and insatiable desires. The Rajasic person gets attached to action, performing rituals, charitable acts, and pursuing sensual pleasures. Their self-perception becomes distorted, believing they are the doer, and their intellect is clouded by greed and pride.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: तमस्त्वज्ञानजं विद्धि मोहनं सर्वदेहिनाम् | प्रमादालस्यनिद्राभिस्तन्निबध्नाति भारत
english: But know thou Tamas to be born of ignorance, deluding all embodied beings; it binds fast, O Arjuna, by heedlessness, indolence and sleep.
brief_explanation: Tamas is a binding force with a tendency towards lethargy, causing delusion and nondiscrimination in all embodied beings. It binds one who associates the Self with the body, leading to slothful actions guided by instinct rather than reason. A person under its influence is thoughtless, ignorant, negligent, and indolent, often sleep-prone and forgetful.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: सत्त्वं सुखे सञ्जयति रजः कर्मणि भारत | ज्ञानमावृत्य तु तमः प्रमादे सञ्जयत्युत
english: Sattva attaches to happiness, Rajas to action, O Arjuna, while Tamas verily shrouding knowledge attaches to heedlessness.
brief_explanation: Tamas, the inertia or darkness, envelops knowledge like a cloud obscuring the sun. It leads to attachment towards heedlessness or negligence of duties.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: रजस्तमश्चाभिभूय सत्त्वं भवति भारत | रजः सत्त्वं तमश्चैव तमः सत्त्वं रजस्तथा
english: Now Sattva arises (prevails), O Arjuna, having overpowered Rajas and Tamas; nor Rajas, having overpowered Sattva and Tamas; and now Tamas, having overpowered Sattva and Rajas.
brief_explanation: When Rajas and Tamas are suppressed, Sattva arises, making people appear happy. Each ality takes control at different times, with only one dominating at a given time. Sattva produces knowledge and happiness, while Rajas leads to action, and Tamas causes the veiling of knowledge, inertia, error, indolence, or sleep.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: सर्वद्वारेषु देहेऽस्मिन्प्रकाश उपजायते | ज्ञानं यदा तदा विद्याद्विवृद्धं सत्त्वमित्युत
english: When through every gate (sense) in this body, the wisdom-light shines, then it may be known that Sattva is predominant.
brief_explanation: When a particular quality becomes predominant, it reveals its distinctive characteristics in man. Knowledge shines when Sattva, peace and harmony predominate. Introspection and control over Rajas and Tamas increase Sattva.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: लोभः प्रवृत्तिरारम्भः कर्मणामशमः स्पृहा | रजस्येतानि जायन्ते विवृद्धे भरतर्षभ
english: Greed, activity, the undertaking of actions, restlessness, longing these arise when Rajas is predominant, O Arjuna.
brief_explanation: Greed is the desire to possess more wealth, even when one has sufficient already. Pravritti refers to action in general, and Asamah denotes restlessness, characterized by continuous desires, will, and actions without end. Spriha represents longing for sensual objects.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: अप्रकाशोऽप्रवृत्तिश्च प्रमादो मोह एव च | तमस्येतानि जायन्ते विवृद्धे कुरुनन्दन
english: Darkness, inertness, heedlessness and delusion these arise when Tamas is predominant, O Arjuna.
brief_explanation: Darkness and inertness, accompanied by heedlessness and delusion, arise when Tamas becomes dominant, hindering spiritual progress and success. Tamas is often mistaken for peace or tranquility, leading people to confuse the Tamasic individual with a silent yogi. This state is not spirituality but rather a thick manifestation of Tamas.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: यदा सत्त्वे प्रवृद्धे तु प्रलयं याति देहभृत् | तदोत्तमविदां लोकानमलान्प्रतिपद्यते
english: If the embodied one meets with death when Sattva is predominant, then he attains to the spotless worlds of the knowers of the Highest.
brief_explanation: The embodied one meets death when Sattva, or purity, has become predominant. Then, the knowers of the Highest attain spotless worlds free from Rajas and Tamas, such as Brahmaloka inhabited by the Highest Deities like Hiranyagarbha.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: रजसि प्रलयं गत्वा कर्मसङ्गिषु जायते | तथा प्रलीनस्तमसि मूढयोनिषु जायते
english: Meeting death in Rajas, he is born among those who are attached to action; and dying in Tamas, he is born in the womb of the senseless.
brief_explanation: The text suggests that if a person dies with Rajas dominant, they are reborn among those attached to action. If Tamas predominates at death, they may be reborn in lower species like cattle, birds, or insects, or among the ignorant and dull-witted humans. However, some interpretations suggest that they might not necessarily take an animal's form.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: कर्मणः सुकृतस्याहुः सात्त्विकं निर्मलं फलम् | रजसस्तु फलं दुःखमज्ञानं तमसः फलम्
english: The fruit of good action, they say, is Sattvic and pure, verily the fruit of Rajas is pain, and ignorance is the fruit of Tamas.
brief_explanation: The fruit of Sattvic (good) action is happiness and knowledge, according to the wise. Rajasic action leads to pain, dissatisfaction, and greed. Tamasic action is unrighteous deeds or sin, characterized by a lack of knowledge and foresight.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: सत्त्वात्सञ्जायते ज्ञानं रजसो लोभ एव च | प्रमादमोहौ तमसो भवतोऽज्ञानमेव च
english: From Sattva arises knowledge, and greed from Rajas; heedlessness and delusion arise from Tamas, and also ignorance.
brief_explanation: From Sattva, knowledge arises, like daylight from the sun. Greed, causing misery and pain, comes from Rajas, which fosters insatiable desire and self-advancement. Tamas breeds shortsightedness, torpor, and ignorance, leading to disregard for future consequences and a lack of balance or poise.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: ऊर्ध्वं गच्छन्ति सत्त्वस्था मध्ये तिष्ठन्ति राजसाः | जघन्यगुणवृत्तिस्था अधो गच्छन्ति तामसाः
english: Those who are seated in Sattva go upwards; the Rajasic dwell in the middle; and the Tamasic, abiding in the function of the lowest Guna, go downwards.
brief_explanation: Those who abide in Sattva ascend to heaven, Rajasic remain on earth, and Tamasic descend (into lower forms of life). The attachment to the Gunas causes reincarnation, with humans born as brutes if Tamasic dominates. The nature, function, binding effects, and influence of each Guna are described in previous verses, while liberation comes when one knows the Lord above the three Gunas.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: नान्यं गुणेभ्यः कर्तारं यदा द्रष्टानुपश्यति | गुणेभ्यश्च परं वेत्ति मद्भावं सोऽधिगच्छति
english: When the seer beholds no agent other than the Gunas and knows That which is higher than they, he attains to My Being.
brief_explanation: The Supreme Self is distinct from the alities, not contaminated by them. A liberated sage realizes that he is neither the doer nor the enjoyer, but the witness of the alities. When a person understands that the Gunas are responsible for all actions and transcends them, they attain to the state of the Supreme Self (liberation), becoming one who has transcended the three Gunas (Gunatita).

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: गुणानेतानतीत्य त्रीन्देही देहसमुद्भवान् | जन्ममृत्युजरादुःखैर्विमुक्तोऽमृतमश्नुते
english: The embodied one having crossed beyond these three Gunas out of which the body is evolved, is freed from birth, death, decay and pain, and attains to immortality.
brief_explanation: The sage who has crossed over the three alities (gunas) behaves differently and attains immortality. He transcends the bodily qualities that form the seed of all bodies, including birth, death, decay, and pain. This sage is absorbed in the Lord and experiences eternal bliss, achieving release or Moksha and attaining to the Lord's Being.

speaker: Arjuna
sanskrit: अर्जुन उवाच | कैर्लिङ्गैस्त्रीन्गुणानेतानतीतो भवति प्रभो | किमाचारः कथं चैतांस्त्रीन्गुणानतिवर्तते
english: Arjuna said What are the marks of him who has transcended the three alities, O Lord? What is his conduct and how does he go beyond these three alities?
brief_explanation: The Trigunatita sage, one who has transcended the three Gunas, can be recognized by certain characteristics that others should cultivate. Like a king alleviating the grievances of his subjects, the Lord removes the sorrows of His devotees, highlighting His role as the reliever of distress. Arjuna addresses Sri Krishna as Prabhu, suggesting He is capable of easing his sorrows and pains.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: श्रीभगवानुवाच | प्रकाशं च प्रवृत्तिं च मोहमेव च पाण्डव | न द्वेष्टि सम्प्रवृत्तानि न निवृत्तानि काङ्क्षति
english: The Blessed Lord said When light, activity and delusion are present, he hates them not, nor does he long for them when they are absent.
brief_explanation: The sage, beyond the Gunas, does not hate activities originating from Sattva, Rajas, or Tamas when they are present. He does not experience pride during Sattva's manifestation, nor regret after completing actions. His work is like a child's play.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: उदासीनवदासीनो गुणैर्यो न विचाल्यते | गुणा वर्तन्त इत्येवं योऽवतिष्ठति नेङ्गते
english: He who, seated like one unconcerned, is not moved by the alities, and who, knowing that the alities are active, is self-centred and moves not.
brief_explanation: He is neutral, unaffected by the Gunas (qualities). Not moved by the operating Gunas. Remains self-centered, unmoved by their effects and the body's changes.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: समदुःखसुखः स्वस्थः समलोष्टाश्मकाञ्चनः | तुल्यप्रियाप्रियो धीरस्तुल्यनिन्दात्मसंस्तुतिः
english: Who is the same in pleasure and pain, who dwells in the Self, to whom a clod of earth, stone and gold are alike, who is the same to the dear and the unfriendly, who is firm, and to whom censure and praise are as one.
brief_explanation: The sage, dwelling in his own Self, is indifferent to pleasure and pain, viewing all things equally regardless of their value or status. He remains firm and unperturbed by any form of praise or censure. He abides in the absolute state of Existence-Knowledge-Bliss, maintaining an everlasting calm and serenity.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: मानापमानयोस्तुल्यस्तुल्यो मित्रारिपक्षयोः | सर्वारम्भपरित्यागी गुणातीतः स उच्यते
english: Who is the same in honour and dishonour, the same to friend and foe, abandoning all undertakings he is said to have transcended the alities.
brief_explanation: The individual who maintains equanimity in honor and dishonor, treats friend and foe alike, and transcends the gunas (qualities) is said to be Gunatita. This person keeps a balanced mind amidst changes and maintains equilibrium by abandoning all actions that bring visible or invisible fruits, but performing necessary ones for bodily maintenance. The attributes described in verses 23-25, such as indifference, serve as means for attaining liberation and represent the ideal to aspire for.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: मां च योऽव्यभिचारेण भक्तियोगेन सेवते | स गुणान्समतीत्यैतान्ब्रह्मभूयाय कल्पते
english: And he who serves Me with unswerving devotion, he, crossing beyond the alities, is fit for becoming Brahman.
brief_explanation: The devotee who serves the Isvara with unwavering devotion crosses beyond the three qualities (gunas) and becomes fit to become Brahman, attaining liberation or release from birth and death. This occurs through the grace of the Lord, who destroys ignorance by the shining lamp of wisdom in those dwelling within their Self. The constant meditation on the Lord results in a continuous flow of thoughts towards Him, abandoning thoughts of sensual objects, which is the means for crossing beyond the three qualities.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: ब्रह्मणो हि प्रतिष्ठाहममृतस्याव्ययस्य च | शाश्वतस्य च धर्मस्य सुखस्यैकान्तिकस्य च
english: For I am the abode of Brahman, the immortal and the immutable, of everlasting Dharma and of absolute bliss.
brief_explanation: The Self, which is immortal, immutable, and attainable by eternal Dharma or self-realization, resides in the Supreme Being. The innermost Self is the very Supreme Self. The Lord bestows grace through His energy or power, which cannot be distinct from Him.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: श्रीभगवानुवाच | ऊर्ध्वमूलमधःशाखमश्वत्थं प्राहुरव्ययम् | छन्दांसि यस्य पर्णानि यस्तं वेद स वेदवित्
english: The Blessed Lord said They (the wise) speak of the indestructible peepul tree having its root above and branches below, whose leaves are the metres or hymns: he who knows it is a knower of the Vedas.
brief_explanation: The Asvattha tree referred to as the universe is metaphorical, indestructible, and rooted above (Urdhva), with branches extending below (Adhahshakham). It is described as eternal and supreme over all things in Brahman. The peepul tree symbolizes the ever-changing worldly life or Samsara.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: अधश्चोर्ध्वं प्रसृतास्तस्य शाखा गुणप्रवृद्धा विषयप्रवालाः | अधश्च मूलान्यनुसन्ततानि कर्मानुबन्धीनि मनुष्यलोके
english: Below and above spread its branches, nourished by the Gunas; sense-objects are its buds; and below, in the world of men, stretch forth the roots, originating action.
brief_explanation: The tree of Samsara is nourished by the three Gunas (qualities) of Nature, with sense objects serving as buds and roots originating from past actions in the world of men. Roots grow downwards, strengthening bondage through further actions. The branches represent various realms, from the immovable objects to the realm of the Creator.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: न रूपमस्येह तथोपलभ्यते नान्तो न चादिर्न च सम्प्रतिष्ठा | अश्वत्थमेनं सुविरूढमूलं असङ्गशस्त्रेण दृढेन छित्त्वा
english: Its form is not perceived here as such, neither its end nor its origin, nor its foundation nor resting place: having cut asunder this firmly rooted peepul tree with the strong axe of non-attachment.
brief_explanation: The unreal nature of the Asvattha tree, symbolizing Samsara or the cycle of birth and death, is emphasized. It cannot be perceived in its entirety by anyone as it is like a dream or a mirage. To uproot this deeply rooted tree requires dispassion (Asanga), which is likened to a sharp axe that cuts through egoism, ignorance, and latent tendencies.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: ततः पदं तत्परिमार्गितव्यं यस्मिन्गता न निवर्तन्ति भूयः | तमेव चाद्यं पुरुषं प्रपद्ये | यतः प्रवृत्तिः प्रसृता पुराणी
english: Then That goal should be sought for, whither having gone none returns again. I seek refuge in that Primeval Purusha Whence streamed forth the ancient activity or energy.
brief_explanation: The supreme goal is the Primeval Purusha, the Absolute Existence-Knowledge-Bliss. The aspirant should seek refuge in it and strive to reach its immortal abode, never returning to the mortal world. This goal is analogous to illusory objects that emanate from a magician's jugglery, originating from the Primeval Purusha within the Samsara.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: निर्मानमोहा जितसङ्गदोषा अध्यात्मनित्या विनिवृत्तकामाः | द्वन्द्वैर्विमुक्ताः सुखदुःखसंज्ञैर्- गच्छन्त्यमूढाः पदमव्ययं तत्
english: Free from pride and delusion, victorious over the evil of attachment, dwelling constantly in the Self, their desires having completely turned away, freed from the pairs of opposites known as pleasure and pain, the undeluded reach the eternal goal.
brief_explanation: Free from pride and delusion, victorious over attachment's evils, constantly dwelling in the Self, with desires completely turned away, free from pairs of opposites, freed, known as pleasure and pain's realms, they reach the eternal goal. Engaged in contemplation of Brahman, all desires vanish, becoming Yatis or Sannyasins. The goal described is That.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: न तद्भासयते सूर्यो न शशाङ्को न पावकः | यद्गत्वा न निवर्तन्ते तद्धाम परमं मम
english: Neither doth the sun illumine there nor the moon, nor the fire; having gone thither they return not; that is My supreme abode.
brief_explanation: The supreme abode, also known as Para Brahman, is self-illuminating and existed before the sun, moon, and fire. It remains even after they dissolve during cosmic dissolution. The sun, moon, etc., derive their light from this self-luminous Supreme Being, and nothing else illumines it.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: ममैवांशो जीवलोके जीवभूतः सनातनः | मनःषष्ठानीन्द्रियाणि प्रकृतिस्थानि कर्षति
english: An eternal portion of Myself having become a living soul in the world of life, draws to (itself) the (five) senses with the mind for the sixth, abiding in Nature.
brief_explanation: The individual soul is a ray of the Supreme Being that enters Nature and draws the five senses, mind, and becomes an embodied soul by assuming a body. This is described as the subtle body entering the gross body. Though the individual soul is tainted by actions, it is not truly affected as it is a reflection of the Supreme Being.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: शरीरं यदवाप्नोति यच्चाप्युत्क्रामतीश्वरः | गृहीत्वैतानि संयाति वायुर्गन्धानिवाशयात्
english: When the Lord (as the individual soul) obtains a body and when He leaves it, He takes these and goes (with them) as the wind takes the scents from their seats (flowers, etc.).
brief_explanation: The subtle body, comprising mind and senses, is taken by the Lord upon obtaining a physical form and leaves at dissolution, similar to how wind carries fragrance from flowers. Regardless of where the Lord goes or the form He assumes, He continues to operate through these senses and mind.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: श्रोत्रं चक्षुः स्पर्शनं च रसनं घ्राणमेव च | अधिष्ठाय मनश्चायं विषयानुपसेवते
english: Presiding over the ear, the eye, touch, taste and smell, as well as the mind, it enjoys the objects of the senses.
brief_explanation: The soul enjoys objects of the senses through the mind, presiding over the ears, eyes, touch, taste, smell, and mind itself. It experiences various forms of music, soft objects, beautiful forms, tastes, scents, and more through these senses. Additionally, it gains experiences from the outer world via the mind, intellect, subconscious mind, egoism, ten senses, and five vital airs.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: उत्क्रामन्तं स्थितं वापि भुञ्जानं वा गुणान्वितम् | विमूढा नानुपश्यन्ति पश्यन्ति ज्ञानचक्षुषः
english: The deluded do not see Him Who departs, stays and enjoys; but they who possess the eye of knowledge behold Him.
brief_explanation: The deluded, united with the Gunas, do not see the Self who is nearest and comes easily within their vision. They are engrossed in external forms due to their constant pursuit of sensual objects and identification with the body. Contrarily, those with inner intuition can behold the Self, recognizing its separate existence from the body, similar to how an iron moves due to the presence of a magnet.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: यतन्तो योगिनश्चैनं पश्यन्त्यात्मन्यवस्थितम् | यतन्तोऽप्यकृतात्मानो नैनं पश्यन्त्यचेतसः
english: The Yogins striving (for perfection) behold Him dwelling in the Self; but, the unrefined and unintelligent, even though striving, see Him not.
brief_explanation: The Yogins, with steadfast determination, see the Self dwelling within their hearts. However, those with unrefined intellect and impure minds cannot recognize Him despite strenuous efforts. For Self-realization, one needs a calm and pure mind through constant meditation on the Self.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: यदादित्यगतं तेजो जगद्भासयतेऽखिलम् | यच्चन्द्रमसि यच्चाग्नौ तत्तेजो विद्धि मामकम्
english: That light which residing in the sun illumines the whole world, that which is in the moon and in the fire know that light to be Mine.
brief_explanation: The verse describes the Lord as the all-illuminating light of consciousness, present in the sun, moon, and fire. This higher manifestation is due to a concentration of Sattva, a brilliant and luminous quality, in these entities. Like a clear mirror reflecting a face better than a wall or stone, God's light shines more brightly in the pure heart of a devotee.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: गामाविश्य च भूतानि धारयाम्यहमोजसा | पुष्णामि चौषधीः सर्वाः सोमो भूत्वा रसात्मकः
english: Permeating the earth I support all beings by (My) energy; and having become the watery moon I nourish all herbs.
brief_explanation: The verse describes the immanence of the Lord, who sustains all beings through His energy (Ojas). This energy permeates and supports the earth, preventing it from falling apart. The Lord also nourishes all herbs as the watery moon, infusing sap into them to make them savory.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: अहं वैश्वानरो भूत्वा प्राणिनां देहमाश्रितः | प्राणापानसमायुक्तः पचाम्यन्नं चतुर्विधम्
english: Having become the fire Vaisvanara, I abide in the body of living beings and, associated with the Prana and the Apana, digest the fourfold food.
brief_explanation: The verse describes the Lord as the gastric fire (Vaisvanara) within living beings, responsible for digesting four types of food. This includes solid food for humans, watery food for birds, hot food for certain creatures, and air as food for serpents. The verse also suggests meditating on this concept before eating to avoid impurities in food.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: सर्वस्य चाहं हृदि सन्निविष्टो मत्तः स्मृतिर्ज्ञानमपोहनञ्च | वेदैश्च सर्वैरहमेव वेद्यो वेदान्तकृद्वेदविदेव चाहम्
english: And I am seated in the hearts of all; from Me are memory and knowledge, as well as their absence. I am verily That which has to be known by all the Vedas; I am indeed the author of the Vedanta and the knower of the Vedas am I.
brief_explanation: The text describes that the Supreme Being (I) resides in the hearts of all sentient beings as their innermost Self. This entity is responsible for memory, knowledge, and their loss. Righteous individuals have knowledge and memory due to virtuous deeds, while sinful ones experience their loss due to vicious deeds.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: द्वाविमौ पुरुषौ लोके क्षरश्चाक्षर एव च | क्षरः सर्वाणि भूतानि कूटस्थोऽक्षर उच्यते
english: Two Purushas there are in this world, the perishable and the imperishable. All beings are the perishable and the Kutastha the unchanging is called the imperishable.
brief_explanation: The text describes the three aspects of divine existence: the perishable (Kshara), the imperishable (Akshara), and the Purushottama (Supreme Being). The perishable comprises all changing forms in the world, from Brahma to a blade of grass. Akshara is the unchanging, while Kshara is the ever-changing form of matter.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: उत्तमः पुरुषस्त्वन्यः परमात्मेत्युधाहृतः | यो लोकत्रयमाविश्य बिभर्त्यव्यय ईश्वरः
english: But distinct is the Supreme Purusha called the highest Self, the indestructible Lord Who, pervading the three worlds, sustains them.
brief_explanation: The Supreme Purusha, Purushottama, transcends yet pervades the three worlds, maintaining their existence without being affected by them. Distinct from the perishable and imperishable beings, Purushottama is the incomparable, self-contained, and supreme Self. He is the innermost consciousness of all beings, independent, and known as the Supreme Self in Vedanta.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: यस्मात्क्षरमतीतोऽहमक्षरादपि चोत्तमः | अतोऽस्मि लोके वेदे च प्रथितः पुरुषोत्तमः
english: As I transcend the perishable and am even higher than the imperishable, I am declared to be the highest Purusha in the world and in the Vedas.
