brief_explanation: The Highest Purusha (Purushottama) is a well-known name for the Lord, as He is the supreme Purusha (supreme being). Kshara refers to the perishable tree of Samsara, while Akshara represents the imperishable seed of the same tree. Since the Lord transcends both the perishable and the imperishable, He is declared in the world and Vedas as the highest Purusha, known by devotees and poets alike.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: यो मामेवमसम्मूढो जानाति पुरुषोत्तमम् | स सर्वविद्भजति मां सर्वभावेन भारत
english: He who, undeluded, knows Me thus as the highest Purusha, he, knowing all, worships Me with his whole being (heart), O Arjuna.
brief_explanation: The undeluded knower realizes the Lord as the Supreme Purusha (Being), identifies himself with Brahman, and worships Him with his whole being. This devotee is also the Sarvavit, one who knows everything in detail, knowing that the Lord is the Inner Self of all beings. He beholds the One in the many and the many in the One, transcending dualities like high/low, pleasure/pain, good/evil, etc., and devotes himself wholly to the Self of all with his whole mind centered on the Supreme Self alone.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: इति गुह्यतमं शास्त्रमिदमुक्तं मयानघ | एतद्बुद्ध्वा बुद्धिमान्स्यात्कृतकृत्यश्च भारत
english: Thus, this most secret science has been taught by Me, O sinless one; on knowing this, a man becomes wise, and all his duties are accomplished, O Arjuna.
brief_explanation: The fifteenth discourse in the Bhagavad Gita is referred to as the most profound secret science, eulogizing knowledge of the Self that brings emancipation from the cycle of birth and death. Knowing this makes one wise, implying complete understanding of the Supreme Being and attainment of Brahma Jnana. Once accomplished, all duties are considered fulfilled, and the individual is liberated from Karma, becoming a Jivanmukta or illumined sage.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: श्रीभगवानुवाच | अभयं सत्त्वसंशुद्धिर्ज्ञानयोगव्यवस्थितिः | दानं दमश्च यज्ञश्च स्वाध्यायस्तप आर्जवम्
english: The Blessed Lord said Fearlessness, purity of heart, steadfastness in knowledge and Yoga, almsgiving, control of the senses, sacrifice, study of scriptures, austerity and straightforwardness.
brief_explanation: Fearlessness, purity of heart, steadfastness in knowledge and yoga, selfless giving, control of senses, sacrifice, and study of Sastras (scriptures) are the divine attributes described in this discourse. These qualities help an individual to attain the highest state of superconsciousness (Nirvikalpa Samadhi). The Lord emphasizes fearlessness as it is essential for the attainment of Moksha or salvation and is the chief characteristic of a liberated sage.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: अहिंसा सत्यमक्रोधस्त्यागः शान्तिरपैशुनम् | दया भूतेष्वलोलुप्त्वं मार्दवं ह्रीरचापलम्
english: Harmlessness, truth, absence of anger, renunciation, peacefulness, absence of crookedness, compassion towards beings, non-covetousness, gentleness, modesty, absence of fickleness.
brief_explanation: Ahimsa (noninjury) involves abstaining from harm in thought, word, and deed, curbing outgoing forces of Rajas. Satyam (truth) is speaking truth without lies or unpleasant words, demonstrating self-restraint, kindness, patience, and endurance. Akrodhah (absence of anger) requires not showing anger even under grave provocation.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: तेजः क्षमा धृतिः शौचमद्रोहो नातिमानिता | भवन्ति सम्पदं दैवीमभिजातस्य भारत
english: Vigour, forgiveness, fortitude, purity, absence of hatred, absence of pride these belong to the one born for a divine state, O Arjuna.
brief_explanation: Vigor refers to energy or brilliance that propels an aspirant towards self-realization, overcoming tamasic tendencies. Forgiveness is a virtue exhibited by not retaliating when insulted or harmed despite having the capacity for revenge. Fortitude involves absorbing all calamities and remaining steadfast in adverse conditions.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: दम्भो दर्पोऽभिमानश्च क्रोधः पारुष्यमेव च | अज्ञानं चाभिजातस्य पार्थ सम्पदमासुरीम्
english: Hypocrisy, arrogance and self-conceit, anger and also harshness and ignorance, belong to one who is born for a demoniacal state, O Partha (Arjuna).
brief_explanation: Hypocrisy, arrogance, self-conceit, wrath, harshness, ignorance are demoniacal qualities that obstruct liberation. Hypocrisy involves deceit and falsehood, while arrogance is pride in learning, wealth, or high connections. Arrogant individuals cannot endure the happiness of others and are often enraged at their prosperity.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: दैवी सम्पद्विमोक्षाय निबन्धायासुरी मता | मा शुचः सम्पदं दैवीमभिजातोऽसि पाण्डव
english: The divine nature is deemed conducive to liberation, and the demoniacal to bondage. Grieve not, O Arjuna, thou art born with divine endowments.
brief_explanation: The term 'divine state' refers to a nature that leads to liberation, while the 'demoniacal' leads to bondage. Arjuna, born with Sattvic tendencies, should not be alarmed by the description of Asuric qualities as they lead to grief and delusion. The Lord assures him that he is born with divine attributes, leading towards salvation.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: द्वौ भूतसर्गौ लोकेऽस्मिन्दैव आसुर एव च | दैवो विस्तरशः प्रोक्त आसुरं पार्थ मे शृणु
english: There are two types of beings in this world, the divine and the demoniacal; the divine has been described at length; hear from Me, O Arjuna, of the demoniacal.
brief_explanation: The text describes two types of beings, divine and demoniacal, present in the world as per their natural tendencies. Lord Krishna will detail the characteristics of the demoniacal nature for Arjuna to avoid it, with a more detailed description throughout the discourse. Previously, the divine nature was described in chapters II, XII, XIV, and the first three verses of this chapter.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: प्रवृत्तिं च निवृत्तिं च जना न विदुरासुराः | न शौचं नापि चाचारो न सत्यं तेषु विद्यते
english: The demoniacal know not what to do and what to refrain from; neither purity, nor right conduct nor truth is found in them.
brief_explanation: The demoniac do not comprehend the distinction between action (Pravritti) and inaction (Nivritti). Their conduct lacks purity, truth, and righteousness, as they prioritize personal desires over others' interests. Demoniacal individuals are ignorant of prescribed or prohibited actions, lacking understanding of virtue, vice, or scriptural guidelines.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: असत्यमप्रतिष्ठं ते जगदाहुरनीश्वरम् | अपरस्परसम्भूतं किमन्यत्कामहैतुकम्
english: They say, "This universe is without truth, without (moral) basis, without a God, brought about by mutual union, with lust for its cause; what else?"
brief_explanation: The opinion held by atheists like the Charvakas is that the universe lacks a substratum or support, and they reject the existence of Brahman, Isvara, or God. They believe the universe is caused solely by lust-driven mutual unions, and there is no concept of Karma, Dharma, or Adharma. This perspective views the world as one of chance, lacking introspection.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: एतां दृष्टिमवष्टभ्य नष्टात्मानोऽल्पबुद्धयः | प्रभवन्त्युग्रकर्माणः क्षयाय जगतोऽहिताः
english: Holding this view, these ruined souls of small intellect and fierce deeds, come forth as the enemies of the world for its destruction.
brief_explanation: The ruined souls with small intellects, engaged in fierce deeds like theft, murder, and deceit, become enemies of the world, causing harm and disrupting peace.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: काममाश्रित्य दुष्पूरं दम्भमानमदान्विताः | मोहाद्गृहीत्वासद्ग्राहान्प्रवर्तन्तेऽशुचिव्रताः
english: Filled with insatiable desires, full of hypocrisy, pride and arrogance, holding evil ideas through delusion, they work with impure resolves.
brief_explanation: Desire-driven individuals, driven by insatiable desire, pride, arrogance, and hypocrisy, perform evil actions with impure resolves. These desires persistently grow stronger, causing ruin and death to others. They falsely claim righteousness (hypocrisy), pride, and false dignity (Mana and Mada).

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: चिन्तामपरिमेयां च प्रलयान्तामुपाश्रिताः | कामोपभोगपरमा एतावदिति निश्चिताः
english: Giving themselves over to immeasurable cares ending only with death, regarding gratification of lust as their highest aim, and feeling sure that that is all.
brief_explanation: The individuals mentioned are deeply engrossed in seeking and preserving countless sensual objects, regarding gratification of lust as their highest aim. They believe this to be all that exists, dismissing the concept of eternal bliss beyond the senses or higher truths. Their dull and gross intellect limits their understanding to sensual enjoyment as the supreme source of happiness.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: आशापाशशतैर्बद्धाः कामक्रोधपरायणाः | ईहन्ते कामभोगार्थमन्यायेनार्थसञ्चयान्
english: Bound by a hundred ties of hope, given over to lust and anger, they strive to obtain by unlawful means hoards to wealth for sensual enjoyments.
brief_explanation: The text describes individuals bound by a hundred ties of hope, driven by lust and anger. They strive for sensual enjoyment through unlawful means and hoarding wealth, showing no mercy or righteousness. Their cravings are endless, even as they accumulate wealth, and they become victims of greed.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: इदमद्य मया लब्धमिमं प्राप्स्ये मनोरथम् | इदमस्तीदमपि मे भविष्यति पुनर्धनम्
english: "This has been gained by me today; this desire of mine I shall fuffil; this is mine and this wealth also shall be mine in future."
brief_explanation: Acquiring all the world's wealth will make one a lord of riches, acknowledged by others as a wealthy man. However, such individuals become arrogant due to their wealth, disregarding others, and their pride leads to a loss of discernment. This pride results in entanglement in Maya (illusion), binding them to sin and misery in this life and the next.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: असौ मया हतः शत्रुर्हनिष्ये चापरानपि | ईश्वरोऽहमहं भोगी सिद्धोऽहं बलवान्सुखी
english: "That enemy has been slain by me; and others also I shall slay. I am the lord. I enjoy. I am perfect, powerful and happy."
brief_explanation: The verse describes the arrogant self-perception of individuals with demonic tendencies, believing they are lords over all they survey, capable of killing enemies and enjoying immense wealth, health, and happiness. They consider themselves as powerful rulers beyond comparison, even superior to Indra.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: आढ्योऽभिजनवानस्मि कोऽन्योऽस्ति सदृशो मया | यक्ष्ये दास्यामि मोदिष्य इत्यज्ञानविमोहिताः
english: "I am rich and born in a noble family. Who else is equal to me? I shall perform sacrifices. I shall give (charity). I shall rejoice," thus deluded by ignorance.
brief_explanation: The text suggests that the speaker, as a divine being, surpasses others like Kubera or Vishnu in wealth and lineage. Even Brahma is considered inferior in comparison. No one is equal to the speaker in terms of birth, sacrifices, charity, or worldly pleasures as they indulge in them excessively.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: अनेकचित्तविभ्रान्ता मोहजालसमावृताः | प्रसक्ताः कामभोगेषु पतन्ति नरकेऽशुचौ
english: Bewildered by many a fancy, entangled in the snare of delusion, addicted to the gratification of lust, they fall into a foul hell.
brief_explanation: Diabolical individuals, entangled in delusion's snare, are addicted to sensual gratification and fall into a foul hell, such as Vaitarani. The multiple fancies and lack of discrimination between beneficial and harmful practices are indicative of delusion, compared to a net that causes bondage.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: आत्मसम्भाविताः स्तब्धा धनमानमदान्विताः | यजन्ते नामयज्ञैस्ते दम्भेनाविधिपूर्वकम्
english: Self-conceited, stubborn, filled with the pride and intoxication of wealth, they perform sacrifices in name out of ostentation, contrary to scriptural ordinances.
brief_explanation: They are self-conceited and filled with pride due to wealth. Their sacrifices are performed out of ostentation, contrary to scriptural ordinances. They lack humility, treat others with contempt, and have no genuine faith or sincerity in their performances.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: अहंकारं बलं दर्पं कामं क्रोधं च संश्रिताः | मामात्मपरदेहेषु प्रद्विषन्तोऽभ्यसूयकाः
english: Given over to egoism, power, haughtiness, lust and anger, these malicious people hate Me in their own bodies and in those of others.
brief_explanation: Egoism, power, haughtiness, lust, anger, and malice are traits possessed by these individuals in their own bodies and those of others. They harbor hatred and are malicious people who resent being belittled, prioritize their bodies above all else, and seek revenge on those who thwart their plans. Egoism is the source of all human perversities and evil actions, and it is difficult to overcome but can be annihilated through right enquiry.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: तानहं द्विषतः क्रुरान्संसारेषु नराधमान् | क्षिपाम्यजस्रमशुभानासुरीष्वेव योनिषु
english: Those cruel haters, worst among men in the world, I hurl those evil-doers into the wombs of demons only.
brief_explanation: The text describes those who are enemies of righteous individuals and hate virtuous persons as the worst among men, or Naradhaman. These individuals are also described as demoniacal and enjoy injuring others and killing animals. When they die, their souls are hurlled into the wombs of cruel creatures such as tigers or lions for an indefinite period until they purify their hearts.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: आसुरीं योनिमापन्ना मूढा जन्मनि जन्मनि | मामप्राप्यैव कौन्तेय ततो यान्त्यधमां गतिम्
english: Entering into demoniacal wombs and deluded, birth after birth, not attaining Me, they thus fall, O Arjuna, into a condition still lower than that.
brief_explanation: Deluded individuals, referred to as Asuras, enter into demoniacal wombs due to their satanic desires and actions, leading them to lower conditions or paths in each birth. These people, with impure minds, do not attain Me, and are stuck in a cycle of lower and yet lower births. To overcome this, one must cultivate divine qualities, practice regular meditation, and annihilate evil tendencies for liberation.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: त्रिविधं नरकस्येदं द्वारं नाशनमात्मनः | कामः क्रोधस्तथा लोभस्तस्मादेतत्त्रयं त्यजेत्
english: Triple is the gate of this hell, destructive of the self lust, anger and greed; therefore one should abandon these three.
brief_explanation: The passage describes 'lust, anger, and greed' as the gateway to the lowest level of hell, causing misery and self-destruction. These are the enemies of peace, devotion, and knowledge. When they arise, a person loses balance and commits evil actions.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: एतैर्विमुक्तः कौन्तेय तमोद्वारैस्त्रिभिर्नरः | आचरत्यात्मनः श्रेयस्ततो याति परां गतिम्
english: A man who is liberated from these three gates to darkness, O Arjuna, practises what is good for him and thus goes to the Supreme Goal.
brief_explanation: The passage explains that when one abandons the gates to darkness, they find a path to liberation. This involves getting the company of sages, receiving spiritual instructions, and practicing them through scriptural hearing, reflection, and meditation, ultimately leading to Self-realization.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: यः शास्त्रविधिमुत्सृज्य वर्तते कामकारतः | न स सिद्धिमवाप्नोति न सुखं न परां गतिम्
english: He who, having cast aside the ordinances of the scriptures, acts under the impulse of desire, attains not perfection, nor happiness nor the Supreme Goal.
brief_explanation: The individual who disregards the scriptural ordinance and acts under the influence of desire does not attain perfection, happiness, or the supreme goal. One who ignores prescribed actions in favor of following desires aroused by the senses does not reach God.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: तस्माच्छास्त्रं प्रमाणं ते कार्याकार्यव्यवस्थितौ | ज्ञात्वा शास्त्रविधानोक्तं कर्म कर्तुमिहार्हसि
english: Therefore, let the scripture be thy authority in determining what ought to be done and what ought not to be done. Having known what is said in the ordinance of the scriptures, thou shouldst act here in this world.
brief_explanation: The scriptures serve as authority for determining right and wrong actions in this world. One should respect them, renounce what they prohibit, and follow what they prescribe to attain eternal bliss. Scriptures are like a caring mother, guiding us away from evil and bestowing the greatest good.

speaker: Arjuna
sanskrit: अर्जुन उवाच | ये शास्त्रविधिमुत्सृज्य यजन्ते श्रद्धयान्विताः | तेषां निष्ठा तु का कृष्ण सत्त्वमाहो रजस्तमः
english: Arjuna said Those who, setting aside the ordinances of the scriptures, perform sacrifice with faith, what is their condition, O Krishna? Is is Sattva, Rajas or Tamas?
brief_explanation: The passage discusses three types of individuals, each following a path according to their inherent nature - Sattvic, Rajasic, or Tamasic. These individuals perform rituals with faith despite not fully understanding the scriptures, and their condition is described as a form of blind following. The fate of those without scriptural knowledge remains undisclosed in this excerpt.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: श्रीभगवानुवाच | त्रिविधा भवति श्रद्धा देहिनां सा स्वभावजा | सात्त्विकी राजसी चैव तामसी चेति तां शृणु
english: The Blessed Lord said Threefold is the faith of the embodied, which is inherent in their nature the Sattvic (pure), the Rajasic (passionate) and the Tamasic (dark). Do thou hear of it.
brief_explanation: The passage describes that faith, inherent in the embodied, is threefold due to the influence of the three qualities (Gunas) - Sattvic, Rajasic, and Tamasic. Sattvic faith leads to Self-realization, while Rajasic faith becomes active and Tamasic faith results in darkness or cruelty. Faith takes on these qualities based on a person's inherent nature shaped by their past actions (Samskaras).

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: सत्त्वानुरूपा सर्वस्य श्रद्धा भवति भारत | श्रद्धामयोऽयं पुरुषो यो यच्छ्रद्धः स एव सः
english: The faith of each is in accordance with his nature, O Arjuna. The man consists of his faith; as a man's faith is, so is he.
brief_explanation: The faith of every person aligns with their inherent nature or temperament, known as Svabhava in the last verse and Sattva in the present one. A man's character can be judged by his faith, and it shapes his conduct in life, reflecting his Nishtha (conviction). Each man's faith is influenced by their past actions' self-reproductive latent impressions (Samskaras), coloring their temperament or Sattva nature.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: यजन्ते सात्त्विका देवान्यक्षरक्षांसि राजसाः | प्रेतान्भूतगणांश्चान्ये यजन्ते तामसा जनाः
english: The Sattvic or the pure men worship the gods; the Rajasic or the passionate worship the Yakshas and the Rakshasas; the others (the Tamasic or the deluded people) worship the ghosts and the hosts of the nature-spirits.
brief_explanation: The faith's nature determines the object of worship. Sattvic individuals (pure men) tend to worship gods, while Rajasic (passionate) individuals might worship ghosts or hosts of Bhutas (nature spirits). Tamasic (dull) individuals worship people.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: अशास्त्रविहितं घोरं तप्यन्ते ये तपो जनाः | दम्भाहंकारसंयुक्ताः कामरागबलान्विताः
english: Those men who practise terrific austerities not enjoined by the scriptures, given to hypocrisy and egoism, impelled by the force of lust and attachment.
brief_explanation: The text describes individuals who practice extreme austerities motivated by egoism, hypocrisy, and attachment to lust. They inflict pain on themselves and others, performing unauthorized practices and even killing innocent animals under false pretenses. These people are not acquainted with scriptural teachings, often speaking ill of them while being consumed by their own delusions and infatuations.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: कर्षयन्तः शरीरस्थं भूतग्राममचेतसः | मां चैवान्तःशरीरस्थं तान्विद्ध्यासुरनिश्चयान्
english: Senseless, torturing all the elements in the body and Me also, Who dwell in the body, know thou these to be of demonical resolves.
brief_explanation: The passage refers to those who dwell within the body, controlling all elements (Bhutagramam), including organs. They are considered senseless (Achetasah) as they disregard the teachings of God (Mam), also known as Vaasudeva. Their resolve is demoniac (Antasharirastham Viddhi Aasuranishchayan).

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: आहारस्त्वपि सर्वस्य त्रिविधो भवति प्रियः | यज्ञस्तपस्तथा दानं तेषां भेदमिमं शृणु
english: The food also which is dear to each is threefold, as also sacrifice, austerity and almsgiving. Hear thou the distinction of these.
brief_explanation: The text describes three types of food based on their effect on the body and mind, determined by one's Guna or temperament. The foods are classified as Sattvic (calming), Rajasic (exciting passion), and Tamasic (impure). The nature of a person can be inferred from their preference for certain foods.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: आयुःसत्त्वबलारोग्यसुखप्रीतिविवर्धनाः | रस्याः स्निग्धाः स्थिरा हृद्या आहाराः सात्त्विकप्रियाः
english: The foods which increase life, purity, strength, health, joy and cheerfulness (good appetite), which are savoury and oleaginous, substantial and agreeable, are dear to the Sattvic (pure) people.
brief_explanation: Foods that increase life, purity, strength, health, joy, cheerfulness, good appetite, are savory, oleaginous, substantial, agreeable, and dear to Sattvic (pure). They produce cheerfulness, serenity, mental clarity, and help maintain mental poise and nervous equilibrium. Sattvic food is highly conducive to health.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: कट्वम्ललवणात्युष्णतीक्ष्णरूक्षविदाहिनः | आहारा राजसस्येष्टा दुःखशोकामयप्रदाः
english: The foods that are bitter, sour, saline, excessively hot, pungent, dry and burning, are liked by the Rajasic and are productive of pain, grief and disease.
brief_explanation: Foods that are excessively bitter, sour, saline, hot, pungent, dry, and burning are liked by the Rajasic and contribute to pain, grief, and disease. A Rajasic person prepares various spicy dishes using salt, chillies, mustard, cloves, condiments, pungent pickles, etc., in excess, causing physical discomfort and mental restlessness. Common Rajasic foods include ladysfinger, Puri, Kachori, pungent condiments, meat, fish, eggs, sweets, potato, fried bread, curd, brinjal, carrots, blackgram, onions, garlic, lemon, Masur, tea, coffee, betels, tobacco.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: यातयामं गतरसं पूति पर्युषितं च यत् | उच्छिष्टमपि चामेध्यं भोजनं तामसप्रियम्
english: That which is state, tasteless, putrid, rotten, refuse and impure, is the food liked by the Tamasic.
brief_explanation: Stale food (Yatayamam, Gatarasam) is referred to as tasteless and putrid (Paryushitam). Uchchishtam refers to leftovers from a meal. Tamasic individuals consume food that has been cooked the previous day or is half-cooked/burnt.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: अफलाङ्क्षिभिर्यज्ञो विधिदृष्टो य इज्यते | यष्टव्यमेवेति मनः समाधाय स सात्त्विकः
english: That sacrifice which is offered by men without desire for reward as enjoined by the ordinance (scripture), with a firm faith that to do so is a duty, is Sattvic or pure.
brief_explanation: When a sacrifice is performed with Sattvic rites, faith, devotion, and without desire for reward, with the mind fixed solely on the sacrifice, it's considered pure in nature. This selfless action, done in a disinterested spirit, aims to attain Self-knowledge. Such actions purify the mind, preparing the aspirant for divine light or knowledge.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: अभिसन्धाय तु फलं दम्भार्थमपि चैव यत् | इज्यते भरतश्रेष्ठ तं यज्ञं विद्धि राजसम्
english: The sacrifice which is offered, O Arjuna, seeking a reward and for ostentation, know thou that to be a Rajasic Yajna.
brief_explanation: Performing a sacrifice with the aim of acquiring heaven, son, wealth, or fame is Rajasic in nature. The performer seeks personal recognition, worldly popularity, rewards, and self-glorification rather than seeking self-knowledge.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: विधिहीनमसृष्टान्नं मन्त्रहीनमदक्षिणम् | श्रद्धाविरहितं यज्ञं तामसं परिचक्षते
english: They declare that sacrifice to be Tamasic which is contrary to the ordinances of the scriptures, in which no food is distributed, which is devoid of Mantras, gifts and faith.
brief_explanation: A Tamasic sacrifice lacks adherence to ordinances, proper food distribution, Mantras, gifts, faith, and hymn recitation. It's characterized by irregularities and may have missing components or no recitation at all, earning no merit for the performer.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: देवद्विजगुरुप्राज्ञपूजनं शौचमार्जवम् | ब्रह्मचर्यमहिंसा च शारीरं तप उच्यते
english: Worship of the gods, the twice-born, the teachers and the wise, purity, straightforwardness, celibacy and non-injury are called the austerities of the body.
brief_explanation: Physical austerity includes using the body for religious rituals, serving parents and the needy, and practicing non-stealing and non-covetousness. Tapas (austerity) is self-discipline through these physical practices. Brahmacharya refers to controlling but not suppressing sexual desire through meditation, Japa, prayer, study of scriptures, and contemplation of the pure Self.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: अनुद्वेगकरं वाक्यं सत्यं प्रियहितं च यत् | स्वाध्यायाभ्यसनं चैव वाङ्मयं तप उच्यते
english: Speech which causes no excitement, truthful, pleasant and beneficial, the practice of the study of the Vedas, are called austerity of speech.
brief_explanation: The practice of controlled, truthful, and beneficial speech is called "svadhyayabhyasanam." This austere form of speech brings solace and benefits to others while avoiding causing pain or excitement. Speech that lacks one or more of these attributes cannot be considered an austerity of speech.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: मनः प्रसादः सौम्यत्वं मौनमात्मविनिग्रहः | भावसंशुद्धिरित्येतत्तपो मानसमुच्यते
english: Serenity of mind, good-heartedness, self-control, purity of nature this is called mental austerity.
brief_explanation: Serenity of mind and goodheartedness are forms of mental austerity, achieved through calmness and control of thought, silence, and purity of nature. Self-control involves the regulation of thoughts, speech, and senses to maintain tranquility in the presence of disturbing factors. Purity of nature refers to honesty and freedom from base desires such as lust, anger, and greed.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: श्रद्धया परया तप्तं तपस्तत्त्रिविधं नरैः | अफलाकाङ्क्षिभिर्युक्तैः सात्त्विकं परिचक्षते
english: This threefold austerity, practised by steadfast men, with the utmost faith, desiring no reward, they call Sattvic.
brief_explanation: Trividham refers to threefold austerity: physical, vocal, and mental. The practitioners are steadfast (Yuktaih) and desire no fruit, maintaining balance in mind regardless of success or failure. With faith (Sraddhaya), they believe in the existence of God, their preceptor's words, scriptures, and their own Self.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: सत्कारमानपूजार्थं तपो दम्भेन चैव यत् | क्रियते तदिह प्रोक्तं राजसं चलमध्रुवम्
english: The austerity which is practised with the object of gaining good reception, honour and worship, and with hypocrisy, is here said to be Rajasic, unstable and transitory.
brief_explanation: Penance practiced insincerely for personal honor, hypocrisy, and temporary fame is Rajasic (passionate) and unstable, yielding transitory results. Penance performed with the hope of gaining good reception or mana (honor) is temporary and without niyama (fixity).

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: मूढग्राहेणात्मनो यत्पीडया क्रियते तपः | परस्योत्सादनार्थं वा तत्तामसमुदाहृतम्
english: That austerity which is practised out of a foolish notion, with self-torture, or for the purpose of destroying another, is declared to be Tamasic.
brief_explanation: The text declares that practices of self-torture for destroying another, such as sulphur burning, hook piercing, hanging over fire, standing in cold water, or Panchagni Tapas, are considered Tamasic (of a dark, ignorant nature). These methods do not lead to the attainment of self-knowledge.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: दातव्यमिति यद्दानं दीयतेऽनुपकारिणे | देशे काले च पात्रे च तद्दानं सात्त्विकं स्मृतम्
english: That gift which is given to one who does nothing in return, knowing it to be a duty to give in a fit place and time to a worthy person, that gift is held to be Sattvic.
brief_explanation: The gift ought to be given to one who cannot return it and in a sacred place like Kurukshetra or Varanasi. A worthy recipient, who is pious, well-versed in scriptures, and able to protect both themselves and the donor, should receive the Sattvic gift during an auspicious time such as solar or lunar eclipses or special occasions. Boasting about charity is discouraged.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: यत्तु प्रत्युपकारार्थं फलमुद्दिश्य वा पुनः | दीयते च परिक्लिष्टं तद्दानं राजसं स्मृतम्
english: And, that gift which is given with a view to receive something in return, or looking for a reward, or reluctantly, is held to be Rajasic.
brief_explanation: The gift given with anticipation of future return, public praise, unseen rewards, or heavenly pleasure is considered Rajasic (passionate). Gifts to Brahmanas or Sannyasins aiming for sin removal and subsequent sorrow are also deemed Rajasic.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: अदेशकाले यद्दानमपात्रेभ्यश्च दीयते | असत्कृतमवज्ञातं तत्तामसमुदाहृतम्
english: The gift that is given at a wrong place and time, to unworthy persons, without respect or with insult is declared to be Tamasic.
brief_explanation: Giving a gift without respect and with insult is declared as Tamasic, occurring at an inappropriate place and time, such as among irreligious people or beggars, or at times that are not auspicious. This does not discourage giving to the poor and needy. The donor lacks good faith, doesn't worship, offer a seat, or treat the recipient with contempt.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: ॐतत्सदिति निर्देशो ब्रह्मणस्त्रिविधः स्मृतः | ब्राह्मणास्तेन वेदाश्च यज्ञाश्च विहिताः पुरा
english: "Om Tat Sat": This has been declared to be the triple designation of Brahman. By that were created formerly, the Brahmanas, the Vedas and the sacrifices.
brief_explanation: The phrase "Om Tat Sat" is a root of the universe, symbolizing the indefinable Brahman (Supreme Being) beyond names and classes. It has been declared as the threefold designation of Brahman by those who know it. In ancient times, Brahmanas were given Vedas and directed to perform sacrifices, with "Om Tat Sat" serving as a powerful mantra for creation and success in rituals.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: तस्मादोमित्युदाहृत्य यज्ञदानतपःक्रियाः | प्रवर्तन्ते विधानोक्ताः सततं ब्रह्मवादिनाम्
english: Therefore, with the utterance of "Om" are the acts of sacrifice, gift and austerity as enjoined in the scriptures, always begun by the students of Brahman.
brief_explanation: The commentary suggests that, after meditating on Om, practitioners of Brahman begin their acts of sacrifice, charity, and austerity as per scriptural guidelines. Om is compared to a hillstick for climbing a hill and a boat for crossing a river, emphasizing its utility in initiating actions or sacrifices. Performing these rituals without self-interest or egoism aids in the easy attainment of Self-realization.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: तदित्यनभिसन्धाय फलं यज्ञतपःक्रियाः | दानक्रियाश्च विविधाः क्रियन्ते मोक्षकाङ्क्षिभिः
english: Uttering ï1Tatï1, without aiming at the fruits, are the acts of sacrifice and austerity and the various acts of gifts performed by the seekers of liberation.
brief_explanation: The word "Tat" refers to the immortal Soul, transcending the world, three Gunas, bodies, and states of consciousness. Seekers of liberation meditate on it, offering all actions and their fruits to Brahman, attaining Self-realization through purity of heart caused by selfless actions. The use of "Tat" symbolizes presenting all fruits of activities to Brahman.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: सद्भावे साधुभावे च सदित्येतत्प्रयुज्यते | प्रशस्ते कर्मणि तथा सच्छब्दः पार्थ युज्यते
english: The word ï1Satï1 is used in the sense of reality and of goodness; and so also, O Arjuna, the word ï1Satï1 is used in the sense of an auspicious act.
brief_explanation: The term 'Sat' signifies the permanent and unchanging reality behind ever-changing names and forms, serving as the substratum for these transient entities. In terms of action (karma), it represents goodness or merit. 'Sadhubhava' refers to an attribute of harmony with nature, ensuring the smooth cycle of the worlds.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: यज्ञे तपसि दाने च स्थितिः सदिति चोच्यते | कर्म चैव तदर्थीयं सदित्येवाभिधीयते
english: Steadfastness in sacrifice, austerity and gift, is also called 'Sat' and also action in connection with these (or for the sake of the Supreme) is called 'Sat'.
brief_explanation: The verse describes actions such as sacrifice, austerity, and gift done with pure intentions towards the Supreme Being, leading to attainment of highest goals like immortality, freedom, and eternal bliss. Performing these actions for Brahman leads to perfection and supreme peace. Firm faith in Om Tat Sat brings liberation from the cycle of birth and death.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: अश्रद्धया हुतं दत्तं तपस्तप्तं कृतं च यत् | असदित्युच्यते पार्थ न च तत्प्रेत्य नो इह
english: Whatever is sacrificed, given or performed, and whatever austerity is practised without faith, it is called 'Asat', O Arjuna; it is naught here or hereafter (after death).
brief_explanation: Acts performed without faith, such as sacrifice, austerity, or giving, lack permanence and yield no lasting benefits. Without dedicating actions to the Lord, they are worthless, like rain on rocky ground or ghee on cold ashes. Lack of faith leads to egoism, obstinacy, and a hardened heart.

speaker: Arjuna
sanskrit: अर्जुन उवाच | संन्यासस्य महाबाहो तत्त्वमिच्छामि वेदितुम् | त्यागस्य च हृषीकेश पृथक्केशिनिषूदन
english: Arjuna said I desire to know severally, O mighty-armed, the essence or truth of renunciation, O Hrishikesa, as also of abandonment, O slayer of Kesi.
brief_explanation: The GitaSastra's teachings are summarized in this discourse, providing a concise summary of previous chapters. Arjuna seeks clarification on the distinction between Sannyasa and Tyaga (renunciation and abandonment). Lord Krishna, also known as Kesinishudana for slaying the Asura Kesi, explains their correct meanings in the following verse.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: श्रीभगवानुवाच | काम्यानां कर्मणां न्यासं संन्यासं कवयो विदुः | सर्वकर्मफलत्यागं प्राहुस्त्यागं विचक्षणाः
english: The Blessed Lord said The sages understand Sannyasa to be the renunciation of action with desire; the wise declare the abandonment of the fruits of all actions as Tyaga.
brief_explanation: The term Kamya Karmani refers to actions performed for personal gain, such as the Asvamedha sacrifice. The wise declare that Tyaga, or renunciation, means abandoning the fruits of all Nitya and Naimittika works (duties). Both Sannyasa and Tyaga imply giving up, but they convey slightly different ideas without being entirely distinct.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: त्याज्यं दोषवदित्येके कर्म प्राहुर्मनीषिणः | यज्ञदानतपःकर्म न त्याज्यमिति चापरे
english: Some philosophers declare that actions should be abandoned as an evil; while others (declare) that acts of sacrifice, gift and austerity should not be relinished.
brief_explanation: The phrase "tyajyam doshavat" suggests some philosophers believe all actions should be abandoned as evil by those fit for Karma Yoga, likening them to passion and other negative tendencies. Others argue that acts of sacrifice, gifts, and austerities should not be renounced by Karma Yogins. These contrasting views are held among those with great understanding, and Krishna will clarify the proper practice of renunciation for Karma Yogins.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: निश्चयं शृणु मे तत्र त्यागे भरतसत्तम | त्यागो हि पुरुषव्याघ्र त्रिविधः सम्प्रकीर्तितः
english: Hear from Me the conclusion or the final truth about this abandonment, O best of the Bharatas; abandonment, verily, O best of men, has been declared to be of three kinds.
brief_explanation: The Lord provides His personal view on the matter, stating that abandonment has three forms: Sattvic, Rajasic, and Tamasic. He asserts that only He can enlighten one about the authenticity of renunciation for liberation from worldly suffering.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: यज्ञदानतपःकर्म न त्याज्यं कार्यमेव तत् | यज्ञो दानं तपश्चैव पावनानि मनीषिणाम्
english: Acts of sacrifice, gift and austerity should not be abandoned, but should be performed; sacrifice, gift and also austerity are the purifiers of the wise.
brief_explanation: The acts of sacrifice, gift, and austerity purify the hearts of those who perform them without seeking rewards. These actions are considered essential and should be performed. Skillfully executed actions lose their binding power on the soul, leading to spiritual freedom.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: एतान्यपि तु कर्माणि सङ्गं त्यक्त्वा फलानि च | कर्तव्यानीति मे पार्थ निश्चितं मतमुत्तमम्
english: But even these actions should be performed leaving aside attachment and the desire for rewards, O Arjuna; this is My certain and best conviction.
brief_explanation: The passage summarizes the doctrine of Karma Yoga, stating that even actions like sacrifice, charity, and austerity should be performed without attachment or expectation of rewards to achieve emancipation. The word "even" implies these actions should be done by an aspirant, but they bind those with attachment to the action and a desire for reward. Abandoning the desire for rewards can help burn the fruit-bearing tendency of Karma, making one's actions purifying.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: नियतस्य तु संन्यासः कर्मणो नोपपद्यते | मोहात्तस्य परित्यागस्तामसः परिकीर्तितः
english: Verily the renunciation of obligatory action is not proper; the abandonment of the same from delusion is declared to be Tamasic.
brief_explanation: The term 'niyatasya' refers to prescribed duties based on one's religion. Abandoning such duties, which are considered obligatory, contradicts the performer's own belief and can be indicative of ignorance or delusion. Renunciation in this context is associated with tamas (ignorance), as it goes against one's prescribed actions.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: दुःखमित्येव यत्कर्म कायक्लेशभयात्त्यजेत् | स कृत्वा राजसं त्यागं नैव त्यागफलं लभेत्
english: He who abandons action on account of the fear of bodily trouble (because it is painful), does not obtain the merit of renunciation by doing such Rajasic renunciation.
brief_explanation: Renouncing actions due to fear of bodily trouble is not abandonment in a sattvic sense, as the fruit of such abandonment is not Moksha or emancipation. Performing religious duties with determination and persistence is required. However, one may start an action but abandon it before completion due to difficulties or physical suffering.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: कार्यमित्येव यत्कर्म नियतं क्रियतेऽर्जुन | सङ्गं त्यक्त्वा फलं चैव स त्यागः सात्त्विको मतः
english: Whatever obligatory action is done, O Arjuna, merely because it ought to be done, abandoning attachment and also the desire for reward, that renunciation is regarded as Sattvic (pure).
brief_explanation: The verse suggests that one should perform obligatory duties as they come, according to capacity and nature, without pride or expectation of reward. It also advises abandoning the idea that duties produce fruits for self-purification or to prevent sin. This verse praises abandonment of rewards from actions and emphasizes doing duties unselfishly for purification of the mind, preparing it for divine light or Self-knowledge.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: न द्वेष्ट्यकुशलं कर्म कुशले नानुषज्जते | त्यागी सत्त्वसमाविष्टो मेधावी छिन्नसंशयः
english: The man of renunciation, pervaded by purity, intelligent, and with his doubts cut asunder, does not hate a disagreeable work nor is he attached to an agreeable one.
brief_explanation: The renouncer doesn't hate disagreeable actions or desire pleasant ones, as they have no attachment to any action or its rewards. They perform actions for the welfare of all beings without expectation of reward. The wise individual, filled with purity and intelligence, has doubts cut asunder when they realize the only means of attaining supreme bliss is knowledge of the Self.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: न हि देहभृता शक्यं त्यक्तुं कर्माण्यशेषतः | यस्तु कर्मफलत्यागी स त्यागीत्यभिधीयते
english: Verily, it is not possible for an embodied being to abandon actions entirely; but he who relinishes the rewards of actions is verily called a man of renunciation.
brief_explanation: The embodied being, identifying with the body, grumbles about performing actions, showing ignorance. Relinishing entirely from actions is impossible for such an individual who thinks himself the doer. One can only abandon the desire for action's fruits and be called a 'relinisher of the fruits of actions'.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: अनिष्टमिष्टं मिश्रं च त्रिविधं कर्मणः फलम् | भवत्यत्यागिनां प्रेत्य न तु संन्यासिनां क्वचित्
english: The threefold fruit of action (evil, good and mixed) accrues after death to the non-abandoners, but never to the abandoners.
brief_explanation: The fruit (Phalam) of action can be pleasant, unpleasant, or a mix. Nonrenouncers are reborn based on their good, evil, or mixed deeds after death. Renouncers, however, are not reborn due to their actions being detached from any desire for rewards.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: पञ्चैतानि महाबाहो कारणानि निबोध मे | साङ्ख्ये कृतान्ते प्रोक्तानि सिद्धये सर्वकर्मणाम्
english: Learn from Me, O mighty-armed Arjuna, these five causes as declared in the Sankhya system for the accomplishment of all actions.
brief_explanation: The five causes are enumerated: Sankhya, a philosophical system, explains these as ending all actions. Vedanta knowledge of the Self puts an end to action, making Vedanta the culmination of all actions, leading to liberation for one who has attained Self-knowledge according to the instructions in the Upanishads.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: अधिष्ठानं तथा कर्ता करणं च पृथग्विधम् | विविधाश्च पृथक्चेष्टा दैवं चैवात्र पञ्चमम्
english: The seat (body), the doer, the various senses, the different functions of various sorts, and the presiding deity, also, the fifth.
brief_explanation: The body is referred to as the seat or support, serving as a platform for experiencing pleasure, pain, desire, hatred, and knowledge. The individual soul is the doer or agent, erroneously claiming credit for actions executed by nature. Different organs such as eyes, ears, mind, and others carry out their functions with the help of presiding deities like the Sun.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: शरीरवाङ्मनोभिर्यत्कर्म प्रारभते नरः | न्याय्यं वा विपरीतं वा पञ्चैते तस्य हेतवः
english: Whatever action a man performs with his body, speech and mind whether right or the reverse these five are its causes.
brief_explanation: Actions performed by body, speech, or mind can be right (nyayyam) if they conform to Dharma, the scriptures, and are justifiable. Conversely, actions can be opposite (viparitam) if they are against Dharma and unjustifiable. These actions serve as effects of past Dharma and Adharma.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: तत्रैवं सति कर्तारमात्मानं केवलं तु यः | पश्यत्यकृतबुद्धित्वान्न स पश्यति दुर्मतिः
english: Now, such being the case, verily he who owing to untrained understanding looks upon his Self, which is isolated, as the agent, he of perverted intelligence, sees not.
brief_explanation: The Self is always actionless, yet some perceive themselves as the agents due to untrained understanding. This misconception leads to reincarnation and ignorance, binding them in a physical prison. A person with perverted intelligence considers the body as consciousness and sees not the actionless, self-luminous Self.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: यस्य नाहंकृतो भावो बुद्धिर्यस्य न लिप्यते | हत्वाऽपि स इमाँल्लोकान्न हन्ति न निबध्यते
english: He who is free from the egoistic notion, whose intelligence is not tainted (by good or evil), though he slays these people, he slayeth not, nor is he bound (by the action).
brief_explanation: The individual who transcends activity has renounced desire and personal gain, recognizing that nature, not self, is the doer. This individual's killing, devoid of desire, serves for world peace and harmony, similar to an executioner maintaining law and order. A person with a trained intellect, knowledge of scriptures, logic, and guidance from their preceptor has a pure understanding and reason, acknowledging the Self as the silent witness, not the doer.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: ज्ञानं ज्ञेयं परिज्ञाता त्रिविधा कर्मचोदना | करणं कर्म कर्तेति त्रिविधः कर्मसंग्रहः
english: Knowledge, the knowable and the knower form the threefold impulse to action; the organ, the action and the agent form the threefold basis of action.
brief_explanation: The triad of knowledge, the knower, and the known is the seed of this world, known as Triputi or the traid. It impels a man to threefold action: mental, verbal, and physical. This triad is the driving force of all human activities.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: ज्ञानं कर्म च कर्ताच त्रिधैव गुणभेदतः | प्रोच्यते गुणसङ्ख्याने यथावच्छृणु तान्यपि
english: Knowledge, action and actor are declared in the science of the Gunas (Sankhya philosophy) to be of three kinds only, according to the distinction of the Gunas. Of these also, hear duly.
brief_explanation: The three alities (knowledge, action, actor) are declared in the science of Gunas according to their predominant nature. These distinctions cause variations in knowledge, action, and actors due to different Gunas. This science originates from Kapila's philosophy system, though it opposes Vedanta on the Supreme Truth, yet it provides insights into the Gunas.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: सर्वभूतेषु येनैकं भावमव्ययमीक्षते | अविभक्तं विभक्तेषु तज्ज्ञानं विद्धि सात्त्विकम्
english: That by which one sees the one indestructible Reality in all beings, not separate in all the separate beings know thou that knowledge to be Sattvic.
brief_explanation: The Sattvic (pure) knowledge perceives the indestructible, indivisible reality behind all diverse objects, seeing unity in diversity. This perception views the one Self, which is common in all beings and is not different across various entities.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: पृथक्त्वेन तु यज्ज्ञानं नानाभावान्पृथग्विधान् | वेत्ति सर्वेषु भूतेषु तज्ज्ञानं विद्धि राजसम्
english: But that knowledge which sees in all beings various entities of distinct kinds as different from one another know thou that knowledge to be Rajasic.
brief_explanation: The knowledge that perceives entities as different, even within beings, and focuses on separateness, is Rajasic (passionate) and can delude both the wise and the ordinary. This form of knowledge, which views multiplicity and differentiates based on form and size, obscures unity and promotes a focus on diversity. This concept will be further explained to avoid such knowledge, O Arjuna.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: यत्तु कृत्स्नवदेकस्मिन्कार्ये सक्तमहैतुकम् | अतत्त्वार्थवदल्पं च तत्तामसमुदाहृतम्
english: But that which clings to one single effect as if it were the whole, without reason, without foundation in Truth, and trivial that is declared to be Tamasic.
brief_explanation: The knowledge that perceives every object or being as self-existent and perfect is tamasic. It includes viewing the body as the Self, idolizing objects, or considering Isvara as mere stone or wood. This narrow, unreasonable view lacks comprehensiveness and produces limited results.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: नियतं सङ्गरहितमरागद्वेषतः कृतम् | अफलप्रेप्सुना कर्म यत्तत्सात्त्विकमुच्यते
english: An action which is ordained, which is free from attachment, and which is done without love or hatred by one who is not desirous of any reward that action is declared to be Sattvic.
brief_explanation: The term "Niyatam" refers to obligatory or ordained actions. One should perform these actions without attachment, free from love or hatred. Such actions are declared as Sattvic (pure), bringing great joy to the doer.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: यत्तु कामेप्सुना कर्म साहंकारेण वा पुनः | क्रियते बहुलायासं तद्राजसमुदाहृतम्
english: But that action which is done by one longing for the fulfilment of desires or gain with egoism or with much effort that is declared to be Rajasic (passionate).
brief_explanation: The Rajasic individual performs actions with much egoism, driven by desires and expects rewards. A liberated sage, however, has no longing or craving as all desires are gratified when realizing Brahman, making them Aptakama. Even those who perform pure acts without self-knowledge exhibit egoism.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: अनुबन्धं क्षयं हिंसामनपेक्ष्य च पौरुषम् | मोहादारभ्यते कर्म यत्तत्तामसमुच्यते
english: That action which is undertaken from delusion, without a regard for the conseences, loss, injury and (one's own) ability that is declared to be Tamasic (dark).
brief_explanation: Tamasic actions cause injury and loss, performed without regard for one's abilities or consequences. Pure agency refers to the distinction between various types of agents, as discussed by the Lord in this context.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: मुक्तसङ्गोऽनहंवादी धृत्युत्साहसमन्वितः | सिद्ध्यसिद्ध्योर्निर्विकारः कर्ता सात्त्विक उच्यते
english: An agent who is free from attachment, non-egoistic, endowed with firmness and enthusiasm, and unaffected by success or failure, is called Sattvic (pure).
brief_explanation: A pure agent, free from attachment and nonegoistic, performs actions with firmness and enthusiasm, remaining unaffected in success or failure. This agent is an active participant, characterized by Sattvic qualities. In attaining success (siddhi), they are not motivated by the reward but follow scriptural behests.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: रागी कर्मफलप्रेप्सुर्लुब्धो हिंसात्मकोऽशुचिः | हर्षशोकान्वितः कर्ता राजसः परिकीर्तितः
english: Passionate, desiring to obtain the reward of actions, greedy, cruel, impure, moved by joy and sorrow, such an agent is said to be Rajasic (passionate).
brief_explanation: A passionate agent is deeply rooted in worldly greed and sins, striving solely for personal gain and hoarding wealth. They experience joy upon achieving their desires but are overcome with sorrow due to failures or losses. The greedy (Lubdhah) fail to share their wealth with the deserving, while the cruel (Himsatmakah) inflict harm on others.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: अयुक्तः प्राकृतः स्तब्धः शठो नैष्कृतिकोऽलसः | विषादी दीर्घसूत्री च कर्ता तामस उच्यते
english: Unsteady, vulgar, unbending, cheating, malicious, lazy, desponding and procrastinating such an agent is called Tamasic.
brief_explanation: The Tamasic individual is vulgar, lacking discernment between right and wrong actions. They are often proud and refuse to prostrate before deities or sages. Their behavior is rigid and deceitful, embodying vices such as gambling.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: बुद्धेर्भेदं धृतेश्चैव गुणतस्त्रिविधं शृणु | प्रोच्यमानमशेषेण पृथक्त्वेन धनञ्जय
english: Hear thou the threefold division of intellect and firmness according to the Gunas, as I declare them fully and distinctly, O Arjuna.
brief_explanation: The Intellect's division, firmness, and qualities are threefold; listen as I declare this fully and distinctly, Dhananjaya, who is named "conqueror of wealth" due to the material and spiritual riches he acquired during his conquest tours.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: प्रवृत्तिं च निवृत्तिं च कार्याकार्ये भयाभये | बन्धं मोक्षं च या वेत्ति बुद्धिः सा पार्थ सात्त्विकी
english: The intellect which knows the path of work and renunciation, what ought to be done and what ought not to be done, fear and fearlessness, bondage and liberation that intellect is Sattvic (pure), O Arjuna.
brief_explanation: The threefold nature of the intellect is described: 1. Pravritti (Action): Cause of bondage, the path of work. 2.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: यया धर्ममधर्मं च कार्यं चाकार्यमेव च | अयथावत्प्रजानाति बुद्धिः सा पार्थ राजसी
english: That, by which one wrongly understands Dharma and Adharma and also what ought to be done and what ought not to be done that intellect, O Arjuna, is Rajasic (passionate).
brief_explanation: Dharma refers to that which elevates one toward the goal, such as Brahman or the Self. Adharma is the opposite, leading one astray. Duty, righteousness, and virtue are inadequate translations.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: अधर्मं धर्ममिति या मन्यते तमसावृता | सर्वार्थान्विपरीतांश्च बुद्धिः सा पार्थ तामसी
english: That, which, enveloped in darkness, sees Adharma as Dharma and all things perverted that intellect, O Arjuna, is Tamasic (dark).
brief_explanation: The "Tamasic" intellect misinterprets righteous acts as evil, considers right things false, and views everything in a perverted light, treating virtues as vices. This is explained to Arjuna as one of the three aspects of the intellect.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: धृत्या यया धारयते मनःप्राणेन्द्रियक्रियाः | योगेनाव्यभिचारिण्या धृतिः सा पार्थ सात्त्विकी
english: The unwavering firmness by which, through Yoga, the functions of the mind, the life-force and the senses are restrained that firmness, O Arjuna, is Sattvic (pure).
brief_explanation: The Sattvic firmness controls the mind, lifeforce, and senses by bringing them under control through Yoga (concentration). It prevents the senses from being distracted by external objects and checks their outgoing tendencies, transforming them intelligently rather than repressing or suppressing them.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: यया तु धर्मकामार्थान्धृत्या धारयतेऽर्जुन | प्रसङ्गेन फलाकाङ्क्षी धृतिः सा पार्थ राजसी
english: But that, O Arjuna, by which, on account of attachment and desire for reward, one holds fast to Dharma (duty), enjoyment of pleasures and earning of wealth that firmness, O Arjuna, is Rajasic (passionate).
brief_explanation: The third kind of firmness, Tamasic, refers to one who acts without concern for the results, due to inertia or ignorance. This person is indifferent towards Dharma, desire, and wealth. O Arjuna, listen next for the description of this type of firmness.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: यया स्वप्नं भयं शोकं विषादं मदमेव च | न विमुञ्चति दुर्मेधा धृतिः सा पार्थ तामसी
english: That, by which a stupid man does not abandon sleep, fear, grief, despair and also conceit that firmness, O Arjuna, is Tamasic.
brief_explanation: The Tamasic man, embodied by evil, is indolent, sinful, and addicted to sleep. He experiences sorrow due to his unrighteous actions, fears the body greatly, is discontented, lustful, self-conceited, lacks decorum, and indulges in sensual pleasures excessively.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: सुखं त्विदानीं त्रिविधं शृणु मे भरतर्षभ | अभ्यासाद्रमते यत्र दुःखान्तं च निगच्छति
english: And now hear from Me, O Arjuna, of the threefold pleasure, in which one rejoices by practice and surely comes to the end of pain.
brief_explanation: The pleasure derived from practicing Me brings an end to suffering, and it has a threefold nature which will be discussed further, O Arjuna (Cf. VI.20-30).

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: यत्तदग्रे विषमिव परिणामेऽमृतोपमम् | तत्सुखं सात्त्विकं प्रोक्तमात्मबुद्धिप्रसादजम्
english: That which is like poison at first but in the end like nectar that happiness is declared to be Sattvic, born of the purity of one's own mind due to Self-realisation.
brief_explanation: The referred verse describes that which is initially attended with much pain, like poison, but in the end provides a nectar-like pleasure, born of the purity of one's own mind due to Self-realization. It is declared as Sattvic happiness, born of the direct and perfect knowledge of the supreme Self or the Absolute.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: विषयेन्द्रियसंयोगाद्यत्तदग्रेऽमृतोपमम् | परिणामे विषमिव तत्सुखं राजसं स्मृतम्
english: That happiness which arises from the contact of the sense-organs with the objects, which is at first like nectar, and in the end like poison that is declared to be Rajasic.
brief_explanation: Sensory pleasure, as first experienced, is compared to nectar. However, it is declared that it is mixed with pain, fear, and sin. Indulging in sensual pleasures leads to a cycle of suffering due to attachment, which can lead to repeated rebirths.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: यदग्रे चानुबन्धे च सुखं मोहनमात्मनः | निद्रालस्यप्रमादोत्थं तत्तामसमुदाहृतम्
english: That happiness which at first as well as in the seel deludes the self, and which arises from sleep, indolence and heedlessness that is declared to be Tamasic.
brief_explanation: The pleasure arising from bad habits like excessive drinking, lying, and consuming worthless food is a delusion for the self. It leads to oblivion towards one's righteous path, resembling darkness. This is declared in the conscience after its termination.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: न तदस्ति पृथिव्यां वा दिवि देवेषु वा पुनः | सत्त्वं प्रकृतिजैर्मुक्तं यदेभिः स्यात्त्रिभिर्गुणैः
english: There is no being on earth or again in heaven among the gods, that is liberated from the three alities born of Nature.
brief_explanation: The Gunas, the alities of Nature, are intrinsic to all creation. No creature in the universe is free from them. They form the basis of the Trinity (Brahma, Vishnu, Siva) and are responsible for various functions in the world of mortals.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: ब्राह्मणक्षत्रियविशां शूद्राणां च परन्तप | कर्माणि प्रविभक्तानि स्वभावप्रभवैर्गुणैः
english: Of Brahmanas, Kshatriyas and Vaisyas, as also of Sudras, O Arjuna, the duties are distributed according to the alities born of their own nature.
brief_explanation: The text explains that Brahmanas, Kshatriyas, and Vaisyas are born with qualities suitable for practicing Vedic rites and distributing duties according to their nature, which is determined by the alities of Sattva, Rajas, and Tamas. The Sudras, who serve the first three castes, have no claim to these rites or study of the Vedas. Each caste's life is divided into four stages based on their nature and degree of growth from the alities.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: शमो दमस्तपः शौचं क्षान्तिरार्जवमेव च | ज्ञानं विज्ञानमास्तिक्यं ब्रह्मकर्म स्वभावजम्
english: Serenity, self-restraint, austerity, purity, forgiveness and also uprightness, knowledge, realisation and belief in God are the duties of the Brahmanas, born of (their own) nature.
brief_explanation: The nine virtues of a Brahmana are serenity, self-restraint, austerity, purity, forgiveness, uprightness, knowledge, realization, and belief in God. These qualities are born of nature for them. Astikyam refers to faith in the teachings of the scriptures, the existence of God, and one's own Self.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: शौर्यं तेजो धृतिर्दाक्ष्यं युद्धे चाप्यपलायनम् | दानमीश्वरभावश्च क्षात्रं कर्म स्वभावजम्
english: Prowess, splendour, firmness, dexterity and also not fleeing from battle, generosity and lordliness are the duties of the Kshatriyas, born of (their own) nature.
brief_explanation: The first duty of a Kshatriya is bravery, firmness, dexterity, and skill in battle, born of nature. They are prompt in action, fearless, generous, and enjoy sovereignty over their subjects, exercising ruling power and punishing the unrighteous.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: कृषिगौरक्ष्यवाणिज्यं वैश्यकर्म स्वभावजम् | परिचर्यात्मकं कर्म शूद्रस्यापि स्वभावजम्
english: Agriculture, cattle-rearing and trade are the duties of the Vaisya (merchant), born of (their own) nature; and action consisting of service is the duty of the Sudra (servant-class), born of (their own) nature.
brief_explanation: The verse suggests that agriculture, cattle-rearing, trade, and service are duties associated with the Vaisya caste, which are inherent to one's nature. Additionally, the Sudra caste also has duties (likely related to service) that are natural to them. According to Apastambha Dharma Sutra, when individuals perform their respective duties rightly according to their caste and order of life, they purify their hearts and attain heaven after death, and then through residual actions, they reap superior lives, learning, conduct, wealth, happiness, and intelligence.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: स्वे स्वे कर्मण्यभिरतः संसिद्धिं लभते नरः | स्वकर्मनिरतः सिद्धिं यथा विन्दति तच्छृणु
english: He who does actions, offering them to Brahman, and abandoning attachment, is not tainted by sin, just as a lotus-leaf is not tainted by water.
brief_explanation: The Yogi who performs actions without egoism and attachment, regarding them as offerings to the Lord, remains untainted by actions. He has no desire for liberation and sees inaction in action. All his actions are purified by wisdom, freeing him from the cycle of birth and death, attaining a pure heart, and ultimately realizing self-knowledge, resulting in liberation.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: यतः प्रवृत्तिर्भूतानां येन सर्वमिदं ततम् | स्वकर्मणा तमभ्यर्च्य सिद्धिं विन्दति मानवः
english: He from Whom all the beings have evolved and by Whom all this is pervaded worshipping Him with his own duty, man attains perfection.
brief_explanation: The performance of a man's own duty is an expression of the Supreme's intention, who pervades all creation. Worshipping the Supreme through one's actions leads to the attainment of dispassion and discrimination, ultimately leading to the realization of Self-knowledge.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: श्रेयान्स्वधर्मो विगुणः परधर्मात्स्वनुष्ठितात् | स्वभावनियतं कर्म कुर्वन्नाप्नोति किल्बिषम्
english: Better is one's own duty (though) destitute of merits, than the duty of another well performed. He who does the duty ordained by his own nature incurs no sin.
brief_explanation: Performing one's own duty, even if it seems devoid of merits, is better than pursuing the duty of another. This is because it aligns with one's nature and leads to self-liberation, regardless of its apparent difficulty. Attempting another's duty may lead to danger due to lack of understanding.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: सहजं कर्म कौन्तेय सदोषमपि न त्यजेत् | सर्वारम्भा हि दोषेण धूमेनाग्निरिवावृताः
english: One should not abandon, O Arjuna, the duty to which one is born, though faulty; for, all undertakings are enveloped by evil, as fire by smoke.
brief_explanation: The 'Sahajam' refers to actions born with one at birth, as they are part of one's constitution. All undertakings (duties) should not be abandoned because performing another's duty brings fear and it's improper. Since complete renunciation of action is challenging for one lacking Self-knowledge, abandoning action entirely is not advised.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: असक्तबुद्धिः सर्वत्र जितात्मा विगतस्पृहः | नैष्कर्म्यसिद्धिं परमां संन्यासेनाधिगच्छति
english: He whose intellect is unattached everywhere, who has subdued his self, from whom desire has fled, he by renunciation, attains the supreme state of freedom from action.
brief_explanation: The person with unattached intellect, control over self, and vanished desires attains the supreme perfection through renunciation - a state of dispassion and discrimination towards worldly sensual objects. This state is achieved by knowledge of the Self, leading to absolute freedom from action. This freedom can be attained through renunciation, right knowledge, or the renunciation of all actions brought about by the attainment of the knowledge of the Self.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: सिद्धिं प्राप्तो यथा ब्रह्म तथाप्नोति निबोध मे | समासेनैव कौन्तेय निष्ठा ज्ञानस्य या परा
english: Learn from Me in brief, O Arjuna, how he who has attained perfection reaches Brahman (the Eternal), that supreme state of knowledge.
brief_explanation: The perfection (Siddhi) is achieved through JnanaNishtha, devotion to knowledge, which leads to self-realization and union with the Supreme Being. This method will be explained briefly in the following verses, requiring direct instruction from a qualified teacher or Guru.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: बुद्ध्या विशुद्धया युक्तो धृत्यात्मानं नियम्य च | शब्दादीन्विषयांस्त्यक्त्वा रागद्वेषौ व्युदस्य च
english: Endowed with a pure intellect, controlling the self by firmness, relinishing sound and other objects and abandoning attraction and hatred.
brief_explanation: The Self, endowed with a pure intellect and firmness, controls the self while relinquishing sensory distractions, such as sound and other sense objects, to avoid attraction and hatred. Pure intellect, free from impurities like lust, anger, and doubt, is compared to a clear mirror and considered a great power. The self, through repeated practice of self-restraint and abstraction, gradually gains control over the senses, eliminating attachment and hatred while maintaining necessary minimal possessions without attachment or aversion.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: विविक्तसेवी लघ्वाशी यतवाक्कायमानसः | ध्यानयोगपरो नित्यं वैराग्यं समुपाश्रितः
english: Dwelling in solitude, eating but little, with speech, body and mind subdued, always engaged in meditation and concentration, resorting to dispassion.
brief_explanation: Solitude offers spiritual benefits, enhancing meditation with minimal effort. It's recommended to spend holidays at holy places like Rishikesh or Uttarakashi for peace and self-realization. A moderate diet promotes a light body and mind beneficial for meditation.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: अहंकारं बलं दर्पं कामं क्रोधं परिग्रहम् | विमुच्य निर्ममः शान्तो ब्रह्मभूयाय कल्पते
english: Having abandoned egoism, strength, arrogance, desire, anger and covetousness, and free from the notion of 'mine' and peaceful, he is fit for becoming Brahman.
brief_explanation: Egoism refers to identifying the self with the physical body, which is a form of error as it mistakes the mortal self for the immortal one. Strength here means the one combined with passion, desire, and attachment, and not the physical strength which can't be abandoned. Arrogance or insolence follows states of exaltation, often triggered by wealth or learning.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: ब्रह्मभूतः प्रसन्नात्मा न शोचति न काङ्क्षति | समः सर्वेषु भूतेषु मद्भक्तिं लभते पराम्
english: Becoming Brahman, serene in the Self, he neither grieves nor desires, the same to all beings, he obtains supreme devotion to Me.
brief_explanation: The verse describes a state where one has become Brahman, attaining perfect freedom and oneness with the Supreme. This person is serene-minded, experiencing no grief or desire in all beings. They keep an even mind in success and failure, without longing for unattained objects.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: भक्त्या मामभिजानाति यावान्यश्चास्मि तत्त्वतः | ततो मां तत्त्वतो ज्ञात्वा विशते तदनन्तरम्
english: By devotion he knows Me in truth, what and who I am; then having known Me in truth, he forthwith enters into the Supreme.
brief_explanation: The devotee who unites with the self through devoted focus is the divine consciousness itself. Devotion leads to understanding the true nature of the self as all-pervading, nondual, and eternal. Knowing the self in truth leads to immediate entry into the divine.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: सर्वकर्माण्यपि सदा कुर्वाणो मद्व्यपाश्रयः | मत्प्रसादादवाप्नोति शाश्वतं पदमव्ययम्
english: Doing all actions always having taken refuge in Me, by My grace he obtains the eternal indestructible state of being.
brief_explanation: The devotee, through worshipping the Lord with good actions (and even prohibited ones), purifies their heart and unites with the Lord, achieving an indestructible, eternal abode. This is a form of yoga, or union with the divine.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: चेतसा सर्वकर्माणि मयि संन्यस्य मत्परः | बुद्धियोगमुपाश्रित्य मच्चित्तः सततं भव
english: Mentally renouncing all actions in Me, having Me as the highest goal, resorting to the Yoga of discrimination do thou ever fix thy mind on Me.
brief_explanation: The Bhagavad Gita suggests that one should mentally resign all actions to God (Me), while having Him as the highest goal, resorting to the Yoga of discrimination, and fixing the mind on God consistently. This involves a discriminative faith that knowledge ultimately leads to liberation when the heart is purified through selfless works dedicated to God.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: मच्चित्तः सर्वदुर्गाणि मत्प्रसादात्तरिष्यसि | अथ चेत्त्वमहंकारान्न श्रोष्यसि विनङ्क्ष्यसि
english: Fixing thy mind on Me, thou shalt by My grace overcome all obstacles; but if from egoism thou wilt not hear Me, thou shalt perish.
brief_explanation: When focused solely on Me, you'll surpass all obstacles by My grace. Rejecting My teachings through egoism leads to ruin. Obstacles refer to spiritual difficulties, pitfalls, temptations, diseases, and other trials in Samsara.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: यदहंकारमाश्रित्य न योत्स्य इति मन्यसे | मिथ्यैष व्यवसायस्ते प्रकृतिस्त्वां नियोक्ष्यति
english: If, filled with egoism, thou thinkest: "I will not fight", vain is this, thy resolve; Nature will compel thee.
brief_explanation: The determination you possess will ultimately be rendered ineffective by your inherent nature, which will force you to act as a warrior. Regarding your egoism about being Arjuna or considering killing relatives a sin, it is an illusion.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: स्वभावजेन कौन्तेय निबद्धः स्वेन कर्मणा | कर्तुं नेच्छसि यन्मोहात्करिष्यस्यवशोपि तत्
english: O Arjuna, bound by thy own Karma (action) born of thy own nature, that which from delusion thou wishest not to do, even that thou shalt do helplessly.
brief_explanation: Thou, Arjuna, possess martial qualities due to your inherent nature. Despite not wishing to fight, you are bound by these qualities and will be compelled to do so against your will.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: ईश्वरः सर्वभूतानां हृद्देशेऽर्जुन तिष्ठति | भ्रामयन्सर्वभूतानि यन्त्रारूढानि मायया
english: The Lord dwells in the hearts of all beings, O Arjuna, causing all beings, by His illusive power, to revolve as if mounted on a machine.
brief_explanation: The Lord, referred to as Isvara or Narayana, dwells in the hearts of all beings, acting through illusion (Maya) to cause all beings to move like puppets on a machine.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: तमेव शरणं गच्छ सर्वभावेन भारत | तत्प्रसादात्परां शान्तिं स्थानं प्राप्स्यसि शाश्वतम्
english: Fly unto Him for refuge with all thy being, O Arjuna; by His grace thou shalt obtain supreme peace (and) the eternal abode.
brief_explanation: Surrender completely to the Lord, eliminating all secret desires and egoism that hinder self-surrender. Seek refuge in the Lord with your entire being for liberation from worldly troubles. By His grace, you will achieve the supreme peace and attain the eternal Abode.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: इति ते ज्ञानमाख्यातं गुह्याद्गुह्यतरं मया | विमृश्यैतदशेषेण यथेच्छसि तथा कुरु
english: Thus has wisdom, more secret than secrecy itself, been declared unto thee by Me; having reflected over it fully, then act as thou wishest.
brief_explanation: Teaching revealed by me, more profound than all secrets, is the Gita - considered the essence of all Vedas. By following this and living its spirit, one can achieve supreme peace, highest knowledge, and immortality. This is certain.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: सर्वगुह्यतमं भूयः शृणु मे परमं वचः | इष्टोऽसि मे दृढमिति ततो वक्ष्यामि ते हितम्
english: Hear thou again My supreme word, most secret of all; because thou art dearly beloved of Me, I will tell thee what is good.
brief_explanation: The speaker (Krishna) reiterates, emphasizing the importance of listening closely to His words due to the listener's sincere aspirations and dear status in His eyes. Krishna will share a profound secret, the supreme good or highest form of blessing, with this beloved disciple.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: मन्मना भव मद्भक्तो मद्याजी मां नमस्कुरु | मामेवैष्यसि सत्यं ते प्रतिजाने प्रियोऽसि मे
english: Fix thy mind on Me, by devoted to Me, sacrifice to Me, bow down to Me. Thou shalt come even to Me; truly do I promise unto thee, (for) thou art dear to Me.
brief_explanation: Fix your mind on Me, offer all actions to Me, and let your actions be for Me to attain Me. The Lord promises that with faith in Him as sole refuge, one will assuredly come to Him.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: सर्वधर्मान्परित्यज्य मामेकं शरणं व्रज | अहं त्वा सर्वपापेभ्यो मोक्षयिष्यामि मा शुचः
english: Abandoning all duties, take refuge in Me alone: I will liberate thee from all sins; grieve not.
brief_explanation: Abandoning all duties, seek refuge in Me alone, I will liberate you from all sins. This implies understanding unity without duality, knowing that everything is part of the Self. Regarding objects, perceive Brahman, not forms, as they are illusory and unreal.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: इदं ते नातपस्काय नाभक्ताय कदाचन | न चाशुश्रूषवे वाच्यं न च मां योऽभ्यसूयति
english: This is never to be spoken by thee to one who is devoid of austerities or devotion, nor to one who does not render service or who does not desire to listen, nor to one who cavils at Me.
brief_explanation: The scripture taught to you can be spoken to one who does not criticize the Lord, is austere, devoted, eager to listen and serves his Guru. One who disparages the Lord is excluded.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: य इदं परमं गुह्यं मद्भक्तेष्वभिधास्यति | भक्तिं मयि परां कृत्वा मामेवैष्यत्यसंशयः
english: He who with supreme devotion to Me will teach this supreme secret to My devotees, shall doubtlessly come to Me.
brief_explanation: The supreme secret, or teachings of the Gita, is a dialogue between Lord Krishna and Arjuna. It's called a supreme secret because it leads to immortality or liberation from the cycle of birth and death. Only one who has devotion can receive these teachings.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: न च तस्मान्मनुष्येषु कश्चिन्मे प्रियकृत्तमः | भविता न च मे तस्मादन्यः प्रियतरो भुवि
english: Nor is there any among men who does dearer service to Me, nor shall there be another on earth dearer to Me than he.
brief_explanation: The individual who disseminates the Bhagavad Gita to My devoted followers performs a highly valued service. This person is particularly dear to me, and there is no one else currently or in the future who can offer a greater service to me on Earth.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: अध्येष्यते च य इमं धर्म्यं संवादमावयोः | ज्ञानयज्ञेन तेनाहमिष्टः स्यामिति मे मतिः
english: And he who will study this sacred dialogue of ours, by him I shall have been worshipped by the sacrifice of wisdom, such is My conviction.
brief_explanation: The Gita is described as a sacrifice of wisdom (JnanaYajna). One who studies this sacred dialogue with faith and devotion is equivalent to having performed such a wisdom sacrifice, attaining a fruit comparable to that from meditation on a deity.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: श्रद्धावाननसूयश्च शृणुयादपि यो नरः | सोऽपि मुक्तः शुभाँल्लोकान्प्राप्नुयात्पुण्यकर्मणाम्
english: Also the man who hears this, full of faith and free from malice, he, too, liberated, shall attain to the happy worlds of those of righteous deeds.
brief_explanation: The verse describes a person who is full of faith, free from malice, and can hear even more so when they understand the teachings of the Gita, live by its spirit, and practice its spiritual instructions. This individual will attain happy worlds of those who have done righteous deeds.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit: कच्चिदेतच्छ्रुतं पार्थ त्वयैकाग्रेण चेतसा | कच्चिदज्ञानसम्मोहः प्रनष्टस्ते धनञ्जय
english: Has this been heard, O Arjuna, with one-pointed mind? Has the delusion of thy ignorance been destroyed, O Dhananjaya?
brief_explanation: The Lord questions Arjuna if he has truly understood the teachings, having heard them with a one-pointed mind, aiming to destroy his ignorance-induced delusion, which is the goal of spiritual learning.

speaker: Arjuna
sanskrit: अर्जुन उवाच | नष्टो मोहः स्मृतिर्लब्धा त्वत्प्रसादान्मयाच्युत | स्थितोऽस्मि गतसन्देहः करिष्ये वचनं तव
english: Arjuna said Destroyed is my delusion as I have gained my knowledge (memory) through Thy grace, O Krishna. I remain freed from doubts. I will act according to Thy word.
brief_explanation: Through Krishna's grace, delusion (moha) has been destroyed and knowledge (smriti) attained. Remaining steadfast, Arjuna indicates his firm faith in Krishna. Having achieved the purpose of life through Krishna's grace, he is now free from doubts and actions, and sees the Self in all beings.

speaker: Sanjaya
sanskrit: सञ्जय उवाच | इत्यहं वासुदेवस्य पार्थस्य च महात्मनः | संवादमिममश्रौषमद्भुतं रोमहर्षणम्
english: Sanjaya said Thus I have heard this wonderful dialogue between Krishna and the high-souled Arjuna, which causes the hair to stand on end.
brief_explanation: Dialogue between Krishna, Arjuna, and the high-souled, is a wonderful and awe-inspiring dialogue as it discusses Yoga and spiritual matters concerning the immortal Self. It causes an emotional response that can cause one's hair to stand on end when higher emotions manifest within the heart.

speaker: Unknown
sanskrit: व्यासप्रसादाच्छ्रुतवानेतद्गुह्यमहं परम् | योगं योगेश्वरात्कृष्णात्साक्षात्कथयतः स्वयम्
english: Through the grace of Vyasa I have heard this supreme and most secret Yoga direct from Krishna, the Lord of Yoga, Himself declaring it.
brief_explanation: The dialogue is secretly revealed by Krishna Himself, who is the supreme Yoga, as obtained through Vyasa's grace. It is known as Yoga due to its focus on Yoga and its purpose of uniting with the Lord of Yoga.

speaker: Unknown
sanskrit: राजन्संस्मृत्य संस्मृत्य संवादमिममद्भुतम् | केशवार्जुनयोः पुण्यं हृष्यामि च मुहुर्मुहुः
english: O King, remembering this wonderful and holy dialogue between Krishna and Arjuna, I rejoice again and again.
brief_explanation: The dialogue between Kesava (Krishna) and Arjuna, remembered by King Dhritarashtra through Sanjaya, is wonderful and holy. It brings joy to the listener, and hearing it repeatedly purifies one's soul, turning their thoughts towards the divine.

speaker: Unknown
sanskrit: तच्च संस्मृत्य संस्मृत्य रूपमत्यद्भुतं हरेः | विस्मयो मे महान् राजन्हृष्यामि च पुनः पुनः
english: And, remembering again and again, also that most wonderful form of Hari, great is my wonder, O King; and I rejoice again and again.
brief_explanation: The form of Hari (God) in its most wonderful cosmic manifestation, remembered, leaves one in great wonder and rejoice, O King, and does so repeatedly.

speaker: Unknown
sanskrit: यत्र योगेश्वरः कृष्णो यत्र पार्थो धनुर्धरः | तत्र श्रीर्विजयो भूतिर्ध्रुवा नीतिर्मतिर्मम
english: Wherever is Krishna, the Lord of Yoga; wherever is Arjuna, the wielder of the bow; there are prosperity, victory, happiness and firm policy; such is my conviction.
brief_explanation: The verse "Yatra Yogesvarah Krishnah, Yatra Partho Dhanurdharah" signifies the Lord of Yoga as Krishna and Arjuna as the archer. This is known as the Ekasloki Gita, where repeating this one verse offers benefits equivalent to reading the entire scripture. The eighteenth discourse of the Bhagavad Gita ends with the title "The Yoga of Liberation by Renunciation."
